```python
"""
Panel description handler.

Owns the panel's *content*: the machine-readable description that every
frontend (the Krita docker, the browser panel, the Emacs client)
renders. The description is a list of sections; each section is a
metadata strip, a form, a workflow-bar, or a set of action buttons.

Two config models
=================
  * **Command fields** — carry a `set_command`; the docker sends the
    command on edit. Used for state the daemon owns (run options,
    workflow picker, intercept toggle).

  * **Config fields** — carry a `config_path` into the v2 config dict
    (resources/params/crop/paste). The docker watches these for edits
    and pushes a full `comfy_apply_config` on a 150 ms debounce.

Workflow bar
============
The `workflow-bar` section kind renders the workflow picker and the
Load / Save-config buttons on one row. Kept as its own section kind
rather than a form+actions pair so the renderer can layout them
together (picker stretches, buttons hug the right edge).

Autoload on comfy_load
======================
`comfy_load` autoloads `panel_configs/<slug>.json` if it exists. The
providers here read `_active_config` to populate field values, so
autoloaded values appear in the panel with no extra work on this side.

Slot extraction failure
=======================
When `comfy_load` could not extract slots (duplicate @-name or
`_meta.title`), the panel has no fields to render, but it is not
broken — the graph is loaded.  `WorkflowMetadataProvider` renders a
red "Slot error" line so the user sees *why* the form is empty
instead of a silently blank panel.

Composite (row) fields
======================
A field with `type: "row"` is a composite: one row containing N
sub-widgets laid out horizontally. Each sub-widget carries its own
`key`, `config_path`, and (optionally) `visible_when` / `stretch` /
`kind_hint`. Both renderers register the sub-widgets as ordinary
leaf fields keyed by their own key; the composite key itself is only
the row's label.

Used by ResourcesProvider so each resource renders as
    @thecanvas    [ global/active/layer ▼ ]   [ thecanvas________ ]
on one line, with the layer-name input shown only when the dropdown
is "layer".

Layer alias kind hints
======================
Each resource slot has a `kind` from `comfyui_inspect`'s resource
extractor: `"image"` for `LoadImage`, `"mask"` for `LoadImageMask`.
`ResourcesProvider` propagates that as `kind_hint` on the layer-name
sub-field, which tells the docker to render an editable
`_LayerComboBox` populated with layers of that kind (image-bearing
vs transparency/selection masks) and ordered by the recent-alias
list. Fields without `kind_hint` continue to render as plain
`QLineEdit`s.

Hidden fields (`visible: false`)
================================
A field carrying `visible: false` is created by both renderers but
not shown to the user. Its widget still exists (and its current
value is still read by `build_config_from_widgets`), so the field is
still submitted to `comfy_apply_config`. Only the UI row is hidden.

This capability is not used by any daemon-side provider today.  It
exists so that a *client* (the docker or the web panel) can mark
fields as hidden when it applies a local display filter — the
Parameters prefix filter being the one such filter today.  Each
client filters its own copy of the description before passing it to
the renderer, so the daemon emits all fields unconditionally.

Param prefix filter (client-side)
=================================
The Parameters section carries a "Filter prefix" text field at the
top with `local_handler: "param_prefix_filter"`.  That field has no
`set_command` — it is not routed through the daemon.  Each client
(docker, web panel) registers a local handler for that name, stores
the current prefix in its own settings (QSettings on the docker
side, localStorage on the web side, keyed by workflow name), and
applies the filter to its local copy of the description before
rendering.  The daemon never sees the prefix, which means docker and
web panel can filter independently without interfering.

When a workflow changes, each client restores its saved prefix for
that workflow.  The config file does not carry the prefix — a
display preference in a shared, daemon-owned file would let one
client's choice leak into another client's UI.

Crop section removed
====================
The Crop section (`context`, `padding`) was removed because neither
field can influence an inpaint run.  Rule 1 of `_determine_crop_bounds`
reads `@thecontext`'s bbox and ignores `[crop]`.  Rule 2 only fires for
`source="global"` resources, which the user's workflows do not use.
The daemon still honors `[crop]` in config files and CLI batches —
`comfy_apply_config` validates and normalizes it — the fields just
are not surfaced in the panel.  This keeps the file format
backward-compatible while removing noise from the UI.

Paste section: name + batch mode only
=====================================
`x`, `y`, and `resize_canvas` used to be exposed here.  They are gone
from the panel because none of them can influence an inpaint run:
the paste origin is `crop_bounds[0..1] + (x, y)`, and `crop_bounds`
comes from `@thecontext`'s bbox — pasting at that origin is already
exact, so `x = y = 0` is the only correct value.  `resize_canvas`
only matters for dimension-changing workflows; inpaint preserves
dimensions.  The daemon still honors all three fields if a config
file sets them; they are just not exposed in the panel.

`name` and `batch_mode` stay because they *can* matter the day a
workflow produces more than one image per run (naming the pasted
layers; choosing between stack-as-layers and import-as-animation).

Intercept toggle
================
"Route via interceptor" lives in the **Run options** section,
alongside timeout / count / seed — it is a run-time routing decision,
so it belongs with the other per-run switches, not in its own
section.

The field has `set_command`, not `config_path`: the toggle is
daemon-owned state, not a per-client display preference.  It is
rendered only when the daemon reports an `intercept` block in
`comfy_status` — older daemon builds without intercept mode simply
hide it.  Because it is a `set_command` field, its edits are not
included in `build_config_from_widgets` and therefore do not trigger
the debounced `comfy_apply_config` path.  The daemon command
(`comfy_set_intercept --enabled <bool>`) fires directly.

The field's appearance does not depend on whether a workflow is
loaded — a user can pre-configure the mode before their first Run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import threading
from typing import Callable, Optional

from ..decorators import command, AutoDispatchHandler
from .comfyui_types import _WORKFLOW_DIR


PANEL_ID = "kritomatic_main"
PANEL_TITLE = "Kritomatic"


# ============================================================================
#  Description builder
# ============================================================================

class PanelDescriptionBuilder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sections: list = []

    def add_section(self, section: dict) -> None:
        self.sections.append(section)


_STRUCTURE_FIELD_KEYS = (
    "key", "type", "options", "visible_when", "visible",
    "set_command", "arg_key", "kind_hint", "local_handler",
    "config_path", "no_sync",
)

# Sub-fields contribute to the structure hash only by their *shape*
# (key, type, options, config_path, visibility rule, stretch,
# kind_hint, local_handler) — never by their current value. Otherwise
# a value change would produce a new structure_id and defeat the
# sync-in-place optimization in both renderers.
#
# `kind_hint`, `visible`, and `local_handler` are *shape*, not value:
# whether a text field renders as a plain QLineEdit or as a
# _LayerComboBox, whether it is hidden behind a `visible: false`, and
# whether a commit routes through the daemon or a client-local
# handler, are all decided at rebuild time. Switching any at runtime
# requires the tree to be rebuilt. So a change to any of them must
# change structure_id.
_STRUCTURE_SUBFIELD_KEYS = (
    "key", "type", "options", "visible_when", "visible",
    "config_path", "kind_hint", "stretch", "local_handler",
)


def _field_structure(f: dict) -> dict:
    out = {k: f.get(k) for k in _STRUCTURE_FIELD_KEYS}
    subs = f.get("sub_fields")
    if isinstance(subs, list):
        out["sub_fields"] = [
            {k: sf.get(k) for k in _STRUCTURE_SUBFIELD_KEYS}
            for sf in subs if isinstance(sf, dict)
        ]
    return out


def _finalize_description(sections: list) -> dict:
    structure_src = []
    for s in sections:
        structure_src.append({
            "id": s.get("id"),
            "kind": s.get("kind"),
            "title": s.get("title"),
            "commit": s.get("commit"),
            "fields": [
                _field_structure(f)
                for f in (s.get("fields") or [])
            ],
            "items": s.get("items"),
        })
    digest = hashlib.sha1(
        json.dumps(structure_src, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
    ).hexdigest()[:12]
    return {
        "id": PANEL_ID,
        "title": PANEL_TITLE,
        "structure_id": digest,
        "sections": sections,
    }


# ============================================================================
#  Providers
# ============================================================================

class WorkflowPickerProvider:
    """The workflow picker + Load + Save-config buttons, on one row.

    Replaces the previous form section that only carried the picker.
    Load and Save-config moved here from `run-actions` because they
    operate on the current workflow's config file, not on execution
    state.
    """

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):
        status = ctx.get("comfy_status") or {}
        current = status.get("workflow") or ""

        try:
            slugs = sorted(p.stem for p in _WORKFLOW_DIR.glob("*.json"))
        except OSError:
            slugs = []

        if not slugs:
            picker_field = {
                "key": "workflow-name",
                "label": "Name",
                "type": "text",
                "value": "",
                "set_command": {"type": "comfy_load"},
                "arg_key": "name",
            }
        else:
            selected = current if current in slugs else slugs[0]
            picker_field = {
                "key": "workflow-name",
                "label": "Name",
                "type": "select",
                "options": slugs,
                "value": selected,
                "set_command": {"type": "comfy_load"},
                "arg_key": "name",
            }

        builder.add_section({
            "id": "workflow-picker",
            "kind": "workflow-bar",
            "title": "Workflow",
            "fields": [picker_field],
            "items": [
                {
                    "key": "load",
                    "label": "Load",
                    "command": {"type": "comfy_load"},
                    "collect": {"workflow-name": "name"},
                },
                {
                    "key": "save_config",
                    "label": "Save config",
                    "command": {"type": "comfy_save_config"},
                },
            ],
        })


class WorkflowMetadataProvider:
    """Workflow identity, source, output-node count, slot error,
    active-batch count. Rendered only when a workflow is loaded."""

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):
        status = ctx.get("comfy_status") or {}
        if not status.get("workflow"):
            return
        fields = [{
            "label": "Workflow",
            "value": status.get("workflow", ""),
            "emphasis": "strong",
        }]
        if status.get("workflow_source"):
            fields.append({
                "label": "Source",
                "value": status["workflow_source"],
                "emphasis": "dim",
            })
        output_nodes = status.get("workflow_output_nodes") or {}
        if output_nodes:
            fields.append({
                "label": "Output nodes",
                "value": str(len(output_nodes)),
                "emphasis": "dim",
            })
        if status.get("workflow_slot_error"):
            fields.append({
                "label": "Slot error",
                "value": status["workflow_slot_error"],
                "emphasis": "danger",
            })
        active_batches = status.get("active_batches") or []
        if active_batches:
            fields.append({
                "label": "Active batches",
                "value": str(len(active_batches)),
                "emphasis": "dim",
            })
        intercepted = status.get("intercepted_batches") or []
        if intercepted:
            fields.append({
                "label": "Intercepted",
                "value": str(len(intercepted)) + " pending",
                "emphasis": "dim",
            })
        builder.add_section({
            "id": "workflow",
            "kind": "metadata",
            "title": None,
            "fields": fields,
        })


class ResourcesProvider:
    """Per-@-name: a single composite row with the source dropdown and
    a conditional layer_name field.

    The composite's `key` is only the row's label. Its sub-widgets
    carry the real `config_path`s and are wired independently — the
    docker auto-applies on every edit to either sub-widget.

    The layer_name sub-field carries two hints that matter to the
    docker:

      * `kind_hint` — copied from the workflow slot's `kind`. Value is
        "image" (LoadImage) or "mask" (LoadImageMask). The docker
        uses this to decide whether the field renders as a plain
        `QLineEdit` or as an editable `_LayerComboBox` populated
        with layers of the matching kind.

      * `visible_when` — points at the sibling `source` sub-widget,
        so the field collapses when the dropdown is `active` or
        `global` and reappears on `layer`. Both renderers register
        sub-widgets as ordinary leaf fields keyed by their own key,
        so all per-field plumbing (read_widget_value, apply_value,
        sync_values, build_config_from_widgets, focus and in-flight
        tracking, set_layers) works unchanged.
    """

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):
        status = ctx.get("comfy_status") or {}
        slots = status.get("workflow_resource_slots") or {}
        if not slots:
            return
        config = status.get("config") or {}
        cfg_resources = config.get("resources") or {}
        fields = []
        for name in sorted(slots.keys()):
            slot = slots.get(name) or {}
            # The extractor records `kind` as "image" or "mask"
            # depending on whether the node was LoadImage or
            # LoadImageMask. That's exactly what the docker's
            # _LayerComboBox needs to pick the right bucket. Default
            # to "image" if the slot dict is somehow missing the
            # field — a plain text input is the safe fallback.
            slot_kind = slot.get("kind") or "image"
            res_cfg = cfg_resources.get(name) or {}
            current_source = res_cfg.get("source") or "layer"
            current_layer = (
                res_cfg.get("layer_name") or name.lstrip("@")
            )
            fields.append({
                "key": f"cfg-resource.{name}",
                "label": name,
                "type": "row",
                "sub_fields": [
                    {
                        "key": f"cfg-resource.{name}.source",
                        "type": "select",
                        "options": ["active", "global", "layer"],
                        "value": current_source,
                        "config_path": ["resources", name, "source"],
                        "stretch": 0,
                    },
                    {
                        "key": f"cfg-resource.{name}.layer_name",
                        "type": "text",
                        "value": current_layer,
                        "config_path": ["resources", name, "layer_name"],
                        "visible_when": {
                            f"cfg-resource.{name}.source": "layer",
                        },
                        "kind_hint": slot_kind,
                        "stretch": 1,
                    },
                ],
            })
        builder.add_section({
            "id": "resources",
            "kind": "form",
            "title": "Resources",
            "fields": fields,
        })


def _param_widget_and_default(kind: str):
    if kind == "float":
        return "number", 0.0
    if kind == "int":
        return "integer", 0
    if kind == "boolean":
        return "toggle", False
    return "text", ""


class ParamsProvider:
    """Per-title: a typed input matching the slot kind. The docker
    auto-applies on every edit.

    Emits one form section with a `local_handler` text field at the
    top — the prefix filter — followed by one field per param.  The
    prefix field is not routed through the daemon; each client
    registers a handler named `param_prefix_filter` and stores the
    prefix in its own settings.  See the module docstring, "Param
    prefix filter (client-side)".

    The daemon emits *all* params unconditionally, with their current
    `_active_config` values.  A client that has an active prefix
    filters its local copy of the description before rendering; the
    params it hides keep their `config_path` and value, so
    `build_config_from_widgets` still re-applies them through
    `comfy_apply_config` on every subsequent edit.
    """

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):
        status = ctx.get("comfy_status") or {}
        slots = status.get("workflow_param_slots") or {}
        if not slots:
            return
        config = status.get("config") or {}
        cfg_params = config.get("params") or {}

        fields = []

        # Prefix filter field first. It sits inside the Parameters
        # section — not a separate "Filter" section — because it's
        # the control that decides which of the fields below are
        # shown.  `local_handler` means "the client invokes its own
        # handler for this field; do not send a command".  The
        # daemon does not know, and must not know, what prefix the
        # client is filtering by.
        fields.append({
            "key": "param-prefix",
            "label": "Filter prefix",
            "type": "text",
            "value": "",
            "local_handler": "param_prefix_filter",
        })

        for title in sorted(slots.keys()):
            slot = slots[title]
            kind = slot.get("kind", "string")
            widget_type, kind_default = _param_widget_and_default(kind)
            workflow_default = slot.get("default")
            if workflow_default is None:
                workflow_default = kind_default
            current = cfg_params.get(title, workflow_default)
            fields.append({
                "key": f"cfg-param.{title}",
                "label": title,
                "type": widget_type,
                "value": current,
                "config_path": ["params", title],
            })

        builder.add_section({
            "id": "params",
            "kind": "form",
            "title": "Parameters",
            "fields": fields,
        })

    layers; choosing between stack-as-layers and import-as-animation).

    behavior.

        output_nodes = status.get("workflow_output_nodes") or {}
        if not output_nodes:

class RunOptionsProvider:
    """Timeout, count, seed — and the 'Route via interceptor' toggle.

    Timeout / count / seed commit via `panel_set_run_options`; the
    toggle commits via `comfy_set_intercept`.  All four are per-run

    The intercept toggle is rendered only when the daemon reports an

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):

        opts = (ctx.get("panel_state") or {}).get("run_options") or {}
        try:
            timeout = float(opts.get("timeout", 55.0))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            timeout = 55.0
        try:
            count = int(opts.get("count", 1))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            count = 1

                "label": "Count",
                "type": "integer",
                "value": count,
                "min": 1, "max": 64,

                    "type": "panel_set_run_options",
                    "name": "count",
                },
                "arg_key": "value",
            },

                "type": "text",

        ]

        # Placed last so the numeric run parameters stay grouped at the
        # top; the toggle is the final "and where does this go?" switch
        # before the Run button below.
        intercept = status.get("intercept")
        if isinstance(intercept, dict):
            fields.append({

                "label": "Route via interceptor",
                "type": "toggle",
                "value": bool(intercept.get("enabled", False)),
                "set_command": {"type": "comfy_set_intercept"},
                "arg_key": "enabled",
            })

        builder.add_section({
            "id": "run-options",
            "kind": "form",
            "title": "Run options",
            "fields": fields,

class RunActionsProvider:
    """Run / Cancel / Cancel-All.

    def contribute(self, builder, ctx):

            "id": "run-actions",

            "items": [
                {
                    "key": "run",
                    "label": "Run",
                    "style": "primary",
                    "command": {"type": "comfy_panel_run"},
                    "collect": {
                        "run-timeout": "timeout",

                    "key": "cancel",

                    "style": "danger",

# ============================================================================
#  Panel handler
# ============================================================================

class PanelHandler(AutoDispatchHandler):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._run_options = {
            "timeout": 55.0,
            "count": 1,
            "seed": "",
            "output_name": "",
        }
        self._last_comfy_status: dict = {}
        self._latest_description: dict = _finalize_description([])
        self._comfy_status_puller: Optional[Callable[[], dict]] = None
        self._providers = [
            WorkflowPickerProvider(),
            WorkflowMetadataProvider(),
            ResourcesProvider(),
            ParamsProvider(),
            PasteProvider(),
            RunOptionsProvider(),
            RunActionsProvider(),
        ]
        self._register_listener()

    def set_comfy_status_puller(self, puller: Callable[[], dict]) -> None:
        self._comfy_status_puller = puller

    def _pull_current_comfy_status(self) -> Optional[dict]:
        if self._comfy_status_puller is None:
            return None
        try:
            result = self._comfy_status_puller()
        except Exception:
            return None
        if not isinstance(result, dict):
            return None
        if not result.get('success'):
            return None
        data = result.get('data')
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None

    def _register_listener(self):
        try:
            from ..server.event_bus import get_event_bus
            get_event_bus().add_listener(self._on_bus_event)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _on_bus_event(self, event_type, data):
        if event_type != "state":
            return
        try:
            with self._lock:
                self._last_comfy_status = dict(data or {})
            self._republish()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _build_description_from_state(self) -> dict:
        builder = PanelDescriptionBuilder()
        with self._lock:
            comfy_status = dict(self._last_comfy_status)
            panel_state = {"run_options": dict(self._run_options)}
        ctx = {
            "comfy_status": comfy_status,
            "panel_state": panel_state,
        }
        for provider in self._providers:
            try:
                provider.contribute(builder, ctx)
            except Exception as e:
                builder.add_section({
                    "id": f"provider-error-{len(builder.sections)}",
                    "kind": "metadata",
                    "title": None,
                    "fields": [{
                        "label": "Provider error",
                        "value": f"{type(provider).__name__}: {e}",
                        "emphasis": "danger",
                    }],
                })
        return _finalize_description(builder.sections)

    def _republish(self):
        try:
            description = self._build_description_from_state()
            with self._lock:
                self._latest_description = description
            from ..server.event_bus import get_event_bus
            get_event_bus().publish("panel", description)
        except Exception:
            pass

    @command(
        category='panel',
        help_text='Return the current panel description.',
        args={},
    )
    def panel_description(self, params):
        pulled = self._pull_current_comfy_status()
        if pulled is not None:
            with self._lock:
                self._last_comfy_status = dict(pulled)
        description = self._build_description_from_state()
        with self._lock:
            self._latest_description = description
        return {
            'success': True,
            'message': 'panel description',
            'data': description,
        }

    @command(
        category='panel',
        help_text='Report the panel handler state (run options).',
        args={},
    )
    def panel_status(self, params):
        with self._lock:
            return {
                'success': True,
                'message': 'panel handler state',
                'data': {
                    'run_options': dict(self._run_options),
                },
            }

    @command(
        category='panel',
        help_text='Set a panel run option.',
        args={
            '--name': {
                'type': 'str', 'required': True,
                'choices': ['timeout', 'count', 'seed', 'output_name'],
                'help': 'Option name',
            },
            '--value': {
                'type': 'str', 'required': True,
                'help': 'New value, as a string',
            },
        },
    )
    def panel_set_run_options(self, params):
        name = params.get('name')
        value = params.get('value')
        if name not in ('timeout', 'count', 'seed', 'output_name'):
            return {'success': False,
                    'message': f'unknown option: {name}'}
        with self._lock:
            if name == 'timeout':
                try:
                    coerced = float(value)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    return {'success': False,
                            'message': f'timeout must be a number, got {value!r}'}
            elif name == 'count':
                try:
                    coerced = int(value)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    return {'success': False,
                            'message': f'count must be an integer, got {value!r}'}
                if coerced < 1:
                    return {'success': False,
                            'message': 'count must be >= 1'}
            else:
                coerced = '' if value is None else str(value)
            self._run_options[name] = coerced
        self._republish()
        return {
            'success': True,
            'message': f'{name} = {coerced!r}',
            'data': {'name': name, 'value': coerced},
        }

    @command(
        category='panel',
        help_text='Rebuild and republish the panel description.',
        args={},
    )
    def panel_rebuild(self, params):
        self._republish()
        return {'success': True, 'message': 'panel description republished'}

"""
Docker panel package.

The docker is a Qt widget tree that renders a *panel description* pushed
by the daemon (see handlers/panel.py). It knows nothing about comfyui;
it knows field types and command names.

This package is on reload_daemon's keep-list. Live QDockWidget instances
are bound to the classes here, so the modules must not be dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def _dock_position_right():
    """Return the DockRight position constant, tolerating both Krita 5
    and Krita 6.

    Krita 5 (PyQt5) exposes the enum as a bare class attribute on
    `DockWidgetFactoryBase`; Krita 6 (PyQt6) namespaces it under
    `DockPosition`. The behaviour is identical, only the access path
    changed.
    """
    from krita import DockWidgetFactoryBase
    try:
        return DockWidgetFactoryBase.DockPosition.DockRight
    except AttributeError:
        pass
    try:
        return DockWidgetFactoryBase.DockRight
    except AttributeError:
        pass
    raise AttributeError(
        "could not find DockRight on DockWidgetFactoryBase; "
        "this Krita build exposes the dock position enum differently"
    )


def register_dock_widget() -> None:
    """Register the panel docker factory with Krita.

    Must run exactly once per Krita session. Called from
    kritomatic_daemon/__init__.py, which is imported once and never
    reloaded.
    """
    try:
        from krita import Krita, DockWidgetFactory
    except ImportError:
        return

    from .docker import KritomaticPanel

    factory = DockWidgetFactory(
        "KritomaticPanel",
        _dock_position_right(),
        KritomaticPanel,
    )
    Krita.instance().addDockWidgetFactory(factory)
    print("✓ Kritomatic panel docker factory registered")

```python
"""
Socket client for the daemon's event and command streams.

One persistent event connection (port 12347) that forwards every push
as a Qt signal. One command worker thread that drains a queue of
requests, each on its own fresh connection (port 12346).

Everything runs on plain Python threads and communicates with the
GUI thread through Qt signals. No widget is ever touched off the
GUI thread.

Why the serial worker (and when it is bypassed)
===============================================
The single command worker is by design: it serialises state-mutating
commands so an edit is committed before the next command reaches the
daemon. That is what makes "edit a parameter then click Run" reliable.

The corollary is that a command sent while the worker is busy waits.
For long-running commands (`comfy_generate` holds the worker for the
whole duration of the run), a queued follow-up would never be
delivered until the run finished — which is exactly wrong for a
cancel, for a read, or for the user's second Run click.

Three methods therefore bypass the queue and open their own socket
per call:

  send_run_now(request_id, bundle)      fire a run on its own thread
                                         and socket; streams progress
                                         and the batch_complete summary
                                         back through the same Qt
                                         signals the serial worker
                                         uses.
  send_cancel_now(batch_id, request_id)  fire a cancel; single reply
                                         line.
  request_layers()                       two commands, two sockets;
                                         the daemon's inner loop parses
                                         each chunk as one JSON object,
                                         so two commands concatenated on
                                         one socket would fail to parse.

Each runs on its own background thread, so N concurrent calls to any
of them do not interfere. `send_run_now` in particular is what makes
"click Run twice" work: each click fires a bundle on its own socket,
the daemon's per-connection handler spawns a handler thread for each,
and the two runs proceed concurrently.

There is deliberately no `request_batches()` here. The daemon
publishes a `state` event at batch *start* and again at batch *end*,
and the `active_batches` field in those state events is the sole
source of truth for "is anything running anywhere". The docker's
`_on_state` handler reads it directly.

Layer cache invalidation
========================
`request_layers` deduplicates fetches: if the layer signature
(`image` tuple, `mask` tuple, `recent` tuple) matches `_last_layers`,
it returns without emitting `layersFetched`. That suppresses noisy
re-emits when the watcher fires spuriously.

The dedup has one blind spot: when the panel's widget tree is
rebuilt (a description push whose `structure_id` changed), every
`_LayerComboBox` is destroyed and recreated with no items — the
combo's *text* is set from the spec, but the dropdown has nothing
to offer. If the daemon's layer set happens to be unchanged since
the last emit (the common case: rebuilds are triggered by workflow
loads, not by layer edits), `request_layers` skips the emit and
`set_layers` never runs against the new combos — they stay empty
until the layer set actually changes.

`invalidate_layers_cache` fixes that: it resets `_last_layers` to
its sentinel initial value (the empty tuple), which can never equal
a real signature, so the next fetch always emits. The docker calls
it from `_on_panel` whenever `structure_id` changes, right before
scheduling the watcher, so the next fetch is guaranteed to
repopulate the new combos.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import queue
import socket
import threading

from PyQt6.QtCore import QObject, pyqtSignal

from ..utils.layer_types import IMAGE_LAYER_TYPES, MASK_LAYER_TYPES


EVENT_HOST = "localhost"
EVENT_PORT = 12347
COMMAND_HOST = "localhost"
COMMAND_PORT = 12346

RECONNECT_DELAY = 2.0


class DaemonConnection(QObject):
    """Client for the daemon's event and command sockets.

    Signals (all emitted from worker threads; Qt delivers them queued
    to the GUI thread):

      stateReceived(dict)          — comfy_status state snapshots
      panelReceived(dict)          — panel description updates
      runEventReceived(dict)       — progress entries from any running
                                     command (serial worker or
                                     send_run_now); `request_id` in the
                                     payload identifies which run
      connectionStateChanged(bool) — event socket up/down
      commandCompleted(str, bool, dict)
                                   — (request_id, ok, summary)
      layersFetched(dict)          — {"image": [...], "mask": [...],
                                      "recent": [...]}
    """

    stateReceived = pyqtSignal(dict)
    panelReceived = pyqtSignal(dict)
    runEventReceived = pyqtSignal(dict)
    connectionStateChanged = pyqtSignal(bool)
    commandCompleted = pyqtSignal(str, bool, dict)
    layersFetched = pyqtSignal(dict)

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
        self._command_queue: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()
        self._event_thread = None
        self._command_thread = None
        self._shutting_down = False

        # Deduplication state for request_layers. The empty tuple is
        # the sentinel initial value; any real signature is a 3-tuple
        # of tuples, which never compares equal to the bare empty
        # tuple. `invalidate_layers_cache` resets to this sentinel to
        # force the next fetch to emit.
        self._last_layers: tuple = ()

    # -- lifecycle --

    def start(self) -> None:
        self._stop_event.clear()
        self._shutting_down = False
        self._event_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._event_loop,
            name="kritomatic-panel-event",
            daemon=True,
        )
        self._command_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._command_loop,
            name="kritomatic-panel-cmd",
            daemon=True,
        )
        self._event_thread.start()
        self._command_thread.start()

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        self._shutting_down = True
        self._stop_event.set()
        self._command_queue.put(None)

    def enqueue(self, request_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:
        if self._shutting_down:
            return
        self._command_queue.put((request_id, bundle))

    # -- out-of-band single-command fetches --

    @staticmethod
    def _fetch_one(command_dict: dict, timeout: float = 5.0):
        """Open a fresh socket, send one command, read one line,
        close, return the parsed reply or None.

        The daemon's socket server parses each incoming chunk as one
        JSON object; one command per socket is what it expects.
        """
        sock = None
        try:
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            sock.settimeout(timeout)
            sock.connect((COMMAND_HOST, COMMAND_PORT))
            sock.settimeout(None)
            sock.sendall(
                (json.dumps(command_dict) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
            )
            buffer = b""
            while b"\n" not in buffer:
                chunk = sock.recv(65536)
                if not chunk:
                    return None
                buffer += chunk
            line = buffer.split(b"\n", 1)[0]
            return json.loads(line.decode("utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return None
        finally:
            if sock is not None:
                try:
                    sock.close()
                except OSError:
                    pass

    def send_cancel_now(self, batch_id, request_id: str) -> None:
        """Send a `comfy_cancel` on a fresh socket, on a background
        thread. Bypasses the command queue so the cancel reaches the
        daemon while a long-running `comfy_generate` is still in
        flight.

        When `batch_id` is falsy, the `batch_id` key is omitted from
        the payload, and the daemon cancels *every* active batch —
        the same path the CLI's `panel cancel --all` uses.
        """
        def _run():
            cmd = {"type": "comfy_cancel"}
            if batch_id:
                cmd["batch_id"] = batch_id
            summary = self._fetch_one(cmd)
            if summary is None:
                self.commandCompleted.emit(
                    request_id, False,
                    {"status": "error",
                     "message": "no response from daemon"},
                )
                return
            ok = summary.get("status") == "success"
            self.commandCompleted.emit(request_id, ok, summary)

        threading.Thread(
            target=_run,
            name="kritomatic-cancel",
            daemon=True,
        ).start()

    def send_run_now(self, request_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:
        """Fire a run bundle on its own thread and socket, bypassing
        the serial command worker.

        Runs a `{"id": ..., "commands": [...]}` bundle exactly the way
        the serial worker would, but without queueing. This is what
        lets the docker user click Run multiple times in quick
        succession: each click calls this method once, and N concurrent
        calls run on N threads with N sockets.

        Delegates to `_run_one_command`, which already implements the
        protocol: send the bundle, stream `progress` messages through
        `runEventReceived`, and terminate with one `commandCompleted`
        carrying the `batch_complete` summary. The only difference
        between this and the serial worker's path is that the call
        happens on a fresh thread instead of through the queue.

        The daemon accepts concurrent connections (one handler thread
        per inbound socket), so the two runs proceed concurrently on
        the daemon side too; see `server/socket_server.py`.
        """
        threading.Thread(
            target=self._run_one_command,
            args=(request_id, bundle),
            name=f"kritomatic-run-{request_id}",
            daemon=True,
        ).start()

    def invalidate_layers_cache(self) -> None:
        """Force the next `request_layers` to emit even if the daemon's
        layer set matches the last successful fetch.

        Called by the docker when the panel's widget tree is rebuilt
        (a description push whose `structure_id` changed). The rebuild
        destroys every `_LayerComboBox` and recreates them empty; if
        the daemon's layer set hasn't changed since the last emit,
        `request_layers`'s signature dedup would skip the emit and
        `set_layers` would never repopulate the new combos. Resetting
        `_last_layers` to its sentinel initial value (the empty tuple)
        forces the next fetch to emit.

        Thread-safe: `_last_layers` is written by `request_layers`
        on its own background thread and read here from the GUI
        thread. The comparison is against a fresh tuple from the
        next fetch, so a transient torn read (Python doesn't have
        them, but consider the abstract hazard) can only cause one
        spurious re-emit, never a missed population. The failure
        mode of a wrong read is "one extra fetch" — benign.
        """
        self._last_layers = ()

    def request_layers(self) -> None:
        """Fetch the layer list and recent aliases, classify, emit
        `layersFetched({"image": [...], "mask": [...], "recent": [...]})`.

        Runs on its own background thread. Sends each command on its
        own socket (see the module docstring) so the two do not
        concatenate on one wire. Diffed against the last fetched
        payload to suppress redundant emits when the layer tree and
        the recent-aliases list are both unchanged.

        `list_layers` is called with `all=True`: the default walk
        recurses only into groups, which hides masks — a selection
        mask or a transparency mask is a child of a paint layer, not
        of a group. Without `all=True` the mask bucket is always empty
        and mask alias combos have no items.

        Emits are also forced when `_last_layers` was reset by
        `invalidate_layers_cache` — the comparison against the
        sentinel empty tuple always fails, so the fetch emits
        unconditionally. See the module docstring, "Layer cache
        invalidation".
        """
        def _run():
            layers_resp = self._fetch_one(
                {"type": "list_layers", "all": True}
            )
            recent_resp = self._fetch_one(
                {"type": "comfy_list_recent_aliases"}
            )

            image_names: list = []
            mask_names: list = []
            if layers_resp is not None:
                data = layers_resp.get("data") or {}
                for entry in (data.get("layers") or []):
                    name = entry.get("name") or ""
                    ltype = entry.get("type") or ""
                    if not name:
                        continue
                    if ltype in IMAGE_LAYER_TYPES:
                        image_names.append(name)
                    elif ltype in MASK_LAYER_TYPES:
                        mask_names.append(name)

            recent_names: list = []
            if recent_resp is not None:
                data = recent_resp.get("data") or {}
                raw = data.get("recent_aliases") or []
                if isinstance(raw, list):
                    recent_names = [str(a) for a in raw
                                    if isinstance(a, str)]

            new_signature = (
                tuple(image_names),
                tuple(mask_names),
                tuple(recent_names),
            )
            if new_signature == self._last_layers:
                return
            self._last_layers = new_signature

            self.layersFetched.emit({
                "image": image_names,
                "mask": mask_names,
                "recent": recent_names,
            })

        threading.Thread(
            target=_run,
            name="kritomatic-layers-fetch",
            daemon=True,
        ).start()

    # -- event loop --

    def _event_loop(self) -> None:
        while not self._stop_event.is_set():
            try:
                self._run_event_connection()
            except Exception:
                pass
            if self._stop_event.wait(RECONNECT_DELAY):
                return

    def _run_event_connection(self) -> None:
        try:
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            sock.settimeout(10.0)
            sock.connect((EVENT_HOST, EVENT_PORT))
        except OSError:
            return

        try:
            self.connectionStateChanged.emit(True)
            sock.settimeout(None)
            buffer = b""
            while not self._stop_event.is_set():
                try:
                    chunk = sock.recv(65536)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not chunk:
                    break
                buffer += chunk
                while b"\n" in buffer:
                    line, buffer = buffer.split(b"\n", 1)
                    line = line.strip()
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    try:
                        event = json.loads(line.decode("utf-8"))
                    except Exception:
                        continue
                    self._dispatch_event(event)
        finally:
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
            self.connectionStateChanged.emit(False)

    def _dispatch_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        etype = event.get("type")
        data = event.get("data") or {}
        if etype == "state":
            self.stateReceived.emit(data)
        elif etype == "panel":
            self.panelReceived.emit(data)
        elif etype == "run":
            self.runEventReceived.emit(data)

    # -- command loop --

    def _command_loop(self) -> None:
        while not self._stop_event.is_set():
            item = self._command_queue.get()
            if item is None:
                return
            request_id, bundle = item
            try:
                self._run_one_command(request_id, bundle)
            except Exception as e:
                self.commandCompleted.emit(
                    request_id, False, {"error": str(e)},
                )

    def _run_one_command(self, request_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:
        """Send one bundle on a fresh socket, stream progress, emit
        the summary.

        Runs on the serial worker thread (from `_command_loop`) when
        invoked through `enqueue`, or on a fresh thread when invoked
        through `send_run_now`. Both call sites share this
        implementation because the wire protocol is the same.
        """
        try:
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            sock.settimeout(10.0)
            sock.connect((COMMAND_HOST, COMMAND_PORT))
        except OSError as e:
            self.commandCompleted.emit(
                request_id, False, {"error": f"connect failed: {e}"},
            )
            return

        summary = None
        try:
            sock.settimeout(None)
            sock.sendall((json.dumps(bundle) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
            buffer = b""
            while True:
                try:
                    chunk = sock.recv(65536)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not chunk:
                    break
                buffer += chunk
                while b"\n" in buffer:
                    line, buffer = buffer.split(b"\n", 1)
                    line = line.strip()
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    try:
                        msg = json.loads(line.decode("utf-8"))
                    except Exception:
                        continue
                    mtype = msg.get("type")
                    if mtype == "progress":
                        self.runEventReceived.emit({
                            "kind": "progress",
                            "request_id": request_id,
                            "index": msg.get("index", 0),
                            "total": msg.get("total", 0),
                            "result": msg.get("result", {}),
                        })
                    elif (mtype == "batch_complete"
                          or msg.get("status") == "batch_complete"):
                        summary = msg
                        break
                    else:
                        summary = msg
                        break
                if summary is not None:
                    break
        finally:
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

        summary = summary or {"error": "no response"}
        status = summary.get("status")
        if status == "batch_complete":
            ok = bool(summary.get("failed", 0) == 0)
        elif status == "success":
            ok = True
        else:
            ok = False
        self.commandCompleted.emit(request_id, ok, summary)
