======================================================================
```python
"""
The Kritomatic panel docker.

A QDockWidget that lives in Krita's main window and renders the panel
description pushed by the daemon. The docker is a *client* of the
daemon: it connects to the event socket and the command socket over
loopback TCP, exactly like the browser panel and the Emacs client.

Config auto-apply
=================
Config fields are not committed per-field — the daemon's
`comfy_apply_config` validates a whole config at once. Every config
field edit starts a 150 ms single-shot debounce timer; when the timer
fires, `_apply_config_from_widgets` assembles the four config sections
from the current widget state and enqueues one `comfy_apply_config`.

`comfy_panel_run` and `comfy_save_config` receive the same four
sections as additional command fields; the docker enriches them from
`build_config_from_widgets()` at click time.

Workflow bar
============
The `workflow-bar` section kind (picker + Load + Save-config) is
handled by the renderer as a single row. The docker's action handler
enriches `comfy_save_config` with config sections, same as
`comfy_panel_run`.

Pinned action row
=================
The panel's `run-actions` section (Run / Cancel / Cancel-All) is a
`kind: "actions"` section.  The docker places such sections in a
dedicated layout that sits between the scrollable form area and the
Log section, both of which are non-scrolling children of the dock's
root layout.  The effect: the run controls stay visible at all times,
regardless of how far the user has scrolled the Resources /
Parameters / Crop / Paste fields.

Cancel semantics
================
Cancel targets every run *this docker* started, one `comfy_cancel` per
run, each on its own socket via `send_cancel_now`.  A docker that has
N runs in flight and presses Cancel issues N cancels; the daemon's
`comfy_generate` handlers each see their own `cancel_event` and route
to the proxy independently.  Cancel-All targets every batch on the
daemon (including external jobs registered by the inpaint playground,
intercepted batches awaiting review in the interceptor playground,
and runs started by another docker or by the CLI or the web panel).

Concurrent runs
===============
The Run button allows multiple concurrent clicks. Each click:

  · allocates a unique `run-<ts>-<uuid>` request_id,
  · records it in `self._active_runs: dict[str, float]`,
  · enqueues the bundle via `DaemonConnection.send_run_now`, which runs
    the send/stream/reply on its own thread and socket — bypassing the
    serial command worker so the next click is not delayed by the
    first's duration.

The daemon accepts concurrent connections (one handler thread per
inbound socket) and its `comfy_panel_run` embeds its config in the
bundle, so two in-flight runs cannot clobber each other's config.
See `comfyui_config.py` and `comfyui_generation.py`'s module
docstrings for the daemon-side detail.

The run log prefixes every line with a short suffix of the run's
request id so concurrent runs' progress entries remain distinguishable
in the shared log widget.

Playground input section (registry-driven, slot-based)
======================================================
Live-running playgrounds register with the daemon; each registration
carries a list of **layer slots** — each an `@`-prefixed identifier
with its own `{source, layer_name}` selector.  See
`handlers/playgrounds.py` for the wire shape.  The docker renders one
row per (playground, slot), in a QGroupBox pinned between the
scrollable form and the pinned action row:

    Layout Editor   @thelayout   [source▼] [layer_name]

The slot's `@`-prefixed id IS the display name — no separate label
field, no friendly-name indirection.  Resource-name style, same as
`@thecanvas` for resources.  For multi-slot playgrounds, the
playground's name appears only on its first slot's row; subsequent
slots indent under it.  Slots are addressed independently.

The layer picker is a `_LayerComboBox` — the same widget class the
resources section's alias fields use — so the completer behaviour
(case-insensitive, narrows as you type), recent-first ordering,
popup-open guard, and text-preservation rule are identical on both
sides.  Repopulation goes through `_LayerComboBox.apply_layers`;
no ordering logic is duplicated in this file.

Auto-selection on source switch
-------------------------------
When the user changes a slot's source dropdown from `active` or
`global` to `layer`, `_maybe_auto_select_layer` seeds the layer
picker with the slot's `auto_select_layer` hint (from the register
call) **if** that layer is present in the current image-layer list
**and** the picker is empty.  This turns the common "I want my
companion layer" flow into a single click.

Guards: fires only when the picker is empty (never overwrites a user
choice); fires only when the hint layer exists.  If the picker is
still empty after the check (hint not set, or hint layer missing),
the command is still sent with an empty `layer_name`, and the
daemon's "layer_name is required" error surfaces in the log.

`self._last_layers_payload` caches the most recent `layersFetched`
payload so newly-added rows can be populated immediately instead of
waiting for the next refresh.  `_update_playgrounds` calls
`_apply_layers_to_playground_combos` after every diff for that reason.

Per-row editing is tracked with `entry["editing"]`: while the user's
change is in flight, state pushes from the daemon that still carry the
pre-change selector are ignored for that row.  Cleared when a state
push arrives whose selector matches the user's choice.

Workflow hint text
==================
`_update_workflow_hint` renders a "No workflow loaded" hint when the
panel description carries no `workflow` metadata section.

Layer cache invalidation on structure change
============================================
When a panel description push carries a different `structure_id`
from the previous one, the renderer tears down its widget tree and
rebuilds it. Every `_LayerComboBox` in the new tree is created
empty — its text is set from the spec, but its item list is not
populated until `set_layers` runs with a fresh `layersFetched`.

`request_layers` deduplicates by layer signature (see
`connection.py`'s module docstring, "Layer cache invalidation").
Without intervention, a rebuild that lands between fetches would
leave the new combos empty until the daemon's layer set happened to
change — which, for the common case of workflow loading, it does
not.

`_on_panel` therefore calls `DaemonConnection.invalidate_layers_cache`
whenever `structure_id` changed, forcing the next `request_layers`
to emit. The watcher (already scheduled on every panel push) then
fires, the fetch emits, and `set_layers` repopulates the new combos.

Client-side Parameters filter
=============================
The Parameters section's filter prefix is a *client-local* display
preference.  The renderer emits a `local_handler: "param_prefix_filter"`
field at the top of the Parameters section, and the docker registers
a handler for that name in `__init__`:

  - On commit, the handler stores the new prefix in `QSettings`
    under `param_prefix/<workflow>`, keyed by the current workflow
    name, so each workflow remembers its own prefix.
  - The handler then calls `renderer.set_param_prefix(prefix)`,
    which re-filters the last panel description and rebuilds the
    tree, hiding every `cfg-param.*` field whose title does not
    start with the prefix.

`_on_state` watches for workflow changes and, on transition,
restores `QSettings`'s saved prefix for the new workflow, calling
`renderer.set_param_prefix` before the next panel description
arrives so the very first render for the new workflow is filtered
correctly.

The daemon never sees the prefix.  The web panel's localStorage-
backed filter is independent of this docker's; the two clients can
filter by different prefixes at the same time without interfering.

Startup workflow autoload
=========================
The docker remembers the last-loaded workflow's *slug* in `QSettings`
under the key `last_workflow`.  `_remember_workflow` is called from
`_on_state` on every transition to a non-empty `workflow` field — that
state push is the authoritative "a workflow just got loaded" signal,
and it fires for every load path (the Load button, a picker change,
the CLI's `comfy_load`, another client's load).

On the next docker launch, `_maybe_autoload_remembered_workflow` (called
once from `_on_panel`) does the reverse: if the daemon reports *no*
active workflow and the remembered slug still appears in the workflow
picker's option list, it enqueues one `comfy_load`.  The daemon's
normal autoload of `panel_configs/<slug>.json` then restores the
user's resources / params / crop / paste alongside the workflow.

Failure modes:
  * Daemon already has a workflow at startup — nothing fires (the
    `_description_workflow_name` check).  If it happens to match the
    remembered slug, nothing needs to happen; if it's a different
    one (CLI load, another client), the daemon's choice wins — the
    user explicitly loaded it.
  * Remembered slug no longer exists in the workflows directory —
    warn and skip; no phantom load error on the daemon.
  * Workflows directory empty (a freshly cloned repo before any
    workflow is dropped in) — silently skip.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
import uuid

from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt, QSettings, QTimer
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import (
    QDockWidget, QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QHBoxLayout, QScrollArea, QLabel,
    QPlainTextEdit, QFrame, QComboBox, QGroupBox,
)

from .connection import DaemonConnection
from .layers_watcher import LayersWatcher
from .renderer import PanelRenderer, _LayerComboBox


_CONFIG_APPLY_DEBOUNCE_MS = 150

_LAYER_SOURCES = ("active", "global", "layer")


class KritomaticPanel(QDockWidget):

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__("Kritomatic", parent)
        self.setObjectName("KritomaticPanel")
        self.setAllowedAreas(
            Qt.DockWidgetArea.LeftDockWidgetArea
            | Qt.DockWidgetArea.RightDockWidgetArea
        )

        # Runs this docker started, keyed by request_id, value = start
        # timestamp (monotonic, informational only). Multiple concurrent
        # entries are the whole point; see the module docstring,
        # "Concurrent runs".
        self._active_runs: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._active_batches_count = 0
        self._workflow_loaded = False

        # Playground input rows.  Keyed by `(playground_id, slot_id)`;
        # values are the per-row widget record.  See the module
        # docstring, "Playground input section".
        self._playground_rows: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        # Cache of the most recent `layersFetched` payload.  Used by
        # `_update_playgrounds` to populate newly-added rows and by
        # `_maybe_auto_select_layer`.
        self._last_layers_payload: dict = {}

        # Client-side Parameters filter.  Persisted per workflow in
        # `_settings`; restored by `_on_state` when the workflow
        # changes.  The daemon never sees this.
        self._param_prefix_filter: str = ""
        self._current_workflow: str = ""
        self._settings = QSettings("kritomatic", "panel")

        # Startup workflow autoload state.  See the module docstring,
        # "Startup workflow autoload".
        self._startup_autoload_done = False
        self._remembered_workflow: str = self._load_remembered_workflow()

        self._pending_apply_timer = QTimer(self)
        self._pending_apply_timer.setSingleShot(True)
        self._pending_apply_timer.setInterval(_CONFIG_APPLY_DEBOUNCE_MS)
        self._pending_apply_timer.timeout.connect(self._flush_pending_apply)
        self._pending_apply_source = ""

        root = QWidget()
        root_layout = QVBoxLayout(root)
        root_layout.setContentsMargins(6, 6, 6, 6)
        root_layout.setSpacing(6)

        self._status = QLabel("Connecting to daemon…")
        self._status.setWordWrap(True)
        self._status.setTextFormat(Qt.TextFormat.RichText)
        root_layout.addWidget(self._status)

        self._hint = QLabel("")
        self._hint.setWordWrap(True)
        self._hint.setTextFormat(Qt.TextFormat.RichText)
        self._hint.setStyleSheet(
            "color:#a05a00;font-style:italic;font-size:0.85em;"
            "padding:2px 0;"
        )
        self._hint.hide()
        root_layout.addWidget(self._hint)

        self._scroll = QScrollArea()
        self._scroll.setWidgetResizable(True)
        self._scroll.setFrameShape(QFrame.Shape.NoFrame)
        self._form_container = QWidget()
        self._form_layout = QVBoxLayout(self._form_container)
        self._form_layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self._form_layout.setSpacing(6)
        self._form_layout.addStretch(1)
        self._scroll.setWidget(self._form_container)
        root_layout.addWidget(self._scroll, 1)

        # Playground input section — pinned between the scrollable
        # form and the pinned action row.  A QGroupBox (rather than a
        # hand-styled QLabel header) so its title inherits the theme's
        # default widget style and matches the form sections above.
        # Hidden when no playgrounds are registered.  See the module
        # docstring, "Playground input section".
        self._playgrounds_container = QGroupBox("Playground Input")
        playgrounds_outer = QVBoxLayout(self._playgrounds_container)
        playgrounds_outer.setContentsMargins(8, 6, 8, 6)
        playgrounds_outer.setSpacing(3)

        self._playgrounds_layout = QVBoxLayout()
        self._playgrounds_layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self._playgrounds_layout.setSpacing(2)
        playgrounds_outer.addLayout(self._playgrounds_layout)

        self._playgrounds_container.hide()
        root_layout.addWidget(self._playgrounds_container)

        # Pinned action row container.
        self._actions_container = QWidget()
        self._actions_layout = QVBoxLayout(self._actions_container)
        self._actions_layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self._actions_layout.setSpacing(0)
        root_layout.addWidget(self._actions_container)

        log_label = QLabel("Log")
        log_label.setStyleSheet(
            "color:#888;font-size:0.72rem;"
            "text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.05em;"
        )
        root_layout.addWidget(log_label)
        self._log = QPlainTextEdit()
        self._log.setReadOnly(True)
        self._log.setMaximumBlockCount(500)
        self._log.setFixedHeight(140)
        root_layout.addWidget(self._log)

        self.setWidget(root)

        self._renderer = PanelRenderer(
            self._form_layout,
            self._on_field_commit,
            self._on_action,
            actions_layout=self._actions_layout,
        )
        # Register the client-local handler for the Parameters filter
        # prefix field.  See the module docstring, "Client-side
        # Parameters filter".
        self._renderer.set_local_handler(
            "param_prefix_filter",
            self._on_param_prefix_committed,
        )

        self._conn = DaemonConnection()
        self._conn.stateReceived.connect(self._on_state)
        self._conn.panelReceived.connect(self._on_panel)
        self._conn.runEventReceived.connect(self._on_run_event)
        self._conn.connectionStateChanged.connect(self._on_conn_state)
        self._conn.commandCompleted.connect(self._on_command_completed)
        self._conn.layersFetched.connect(self._on_layers_fetched)
        self._conn.start()

        self._layers_watcher = LayersWatcher(self)
        self._layers_watcher.layersChanged.connect(self._on_layers_changed)
        self._renderer.layerRefreshRequested.connect(
            self._layers_watcher.schedule)
        self._conn.request_layers()
        self._update_run_buttons()

    def closeEvent(self, event):
        try:
            self._pending_apply_timer.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self._layers_watcher.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self._conn.shutdown()
        except Exception:
            pass
        super().closeEvent(event)

    def focusInEvent(self, event):
        super().focusInEvent(event)
        try:
            self._layers_watcher.schedule()
        except Exception:
            pass

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Startup workflow autoload — persistence
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _load_remembered_workflow(self) -> str:
        try:
            return str(self._settings.value(
                "last_workflow", "", type=str,
            ) or "")
        except Exception:
            return ""

    def _remember_workflow(self, workflow: str) -> None:
        if not workflow:
            return
        if workflow == self._remembered_workflow:
            return
        self._remembered_workflow = workflow
        try:
            self._settings.setValue("last_workflow", workflow)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _description_workflow_name(self, description: dict) -> str:
        for s in description.get("sections") or []:
            if not isinstance(s, dict):
                continue
            if s.get("id") != "workflow":
                continue
            for f in s.get("fields") or []:
                if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("label") == "Workflow":
                    return str(f.get("value") or "")
        return ""

    @staticmethod
    def _available_workflow_slugs(description: dict) -> list:
        for s in description.get("sections") or []:
            if not isinstance(s, dict):
                continue
            if s.get("id") != "workflow-picker":
                continue
            for f in s.get("fields") or []:
                if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("key") == "workflow-name":
                    return list(f.get("options") or [])
        return []

    def _maybe_autoload_remembered_workflow(self, description) -> None:
        if self._startup_autoload_done:
            return
        self._startup_autoload_done = True

        if not isinstance(description, dict):
            return
        if not self._remembered_workflow:
            return

        if self._description_workflow_name(description):
            return

        available = self._available_workflow_slugs(description)
        if not available:
            return

        if self._remembered_workflow not in available:
            self._append_log(
                "warn",
                f"Auto-load skipped: remembered workflow "
                f"{self._remembered_workflow!r} no longer exists in "
                f"the workflows directory.",
            )
            return

        command = {
            "type": "comfy_load",
            "name": self._remembered_workflow,
        }
        request_id = f"autoload-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
        self._conn.enqueue(
            request_id, {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]},
        )
        self._append_log(
            "hdr",
            f"Auto-loading remembered workflow "
            f"{self._remembered_workflow!r}\u2026",
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Event handlers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _on_conn_state(self, connected: bool) -> None:
        if connected:
            self._status.setText("Connected to daemon.")
            try:
                self._layers_watcher.schedule()
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            self._status.setText("Waiting for daemon event stream…")
            self._active_batches_count = 0
            self._workflow_loaded = False
        self._update_run_buttons()

    def _on_state(self, data: dict) -> None:
        try:
            batches = data.get("active_batches") or []
            self._active_batches_count = len(batches)
            new_workflow = data.get("workflow") or ""
            old_workflow = self._current_workflow
            self._workflow_loaded = bool(new_workflow)
            self._current_workflow = new_workflow
            if new_workflow != old_workflow:
                self._restore_param_filter_for_workflow(new_workflow)
                if new_workflow:
                    self._remember_workflow(new_workflow)

            playgrounds = data.get("playgrounds")
            if isinstance(playgrounds, list):
                self._update_playgrounds(playgrounds)
        except Exception:
            pass
        self._update_run_buttons()

    def _restore_param_filter_for_workflow(self, workflow: str) -> None:
        if not workflow:
            self._param_prefix_filter = ""
            try:
                self._renderer.set_param_prefix("")
            except Exception:
                pass
            return
        try:
            saved = self._settings.value(
                f"param_prefix/{workflow}", "", type=str,
            )
        except Exception:
            saved = ""
        self._param_prefix_filter = saved or ""
        try:
            self._renderer.set_param_prefix(self._param_prefix_filter)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _on_param_prefix_committed(self, prefix: str) -> None:
        self._param_prefix_filter = str(prefix or "")
        if self._current_workflow:
            try:
                self._settings.setValue(
                    f"param_prefix/{self._current_workflow}",
                    self._param_prefix_filter,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
        try:
            self._renderer.set_param_prefix(self._param_prefix_filter)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _on_panel(self, description: dict) -> None:
        old_structure = self._renderer._structure_id
        try:
            self._renderer.render(description)
        except Exception as e:
            self._append_log("err", f"render error: {e}")
        new_structure = self._renderer._structure_id
        structure_changed = old_structure != new_structure

        self._update_workflow_hint(description)
        self._update_run_buttons()

        if structure_changed:
            try:
                self._conn.invalidate_layers_cache()
            except Exception:
                pass

        try:
            self._layers_watcher.schedule()
        except Exception:
            pass

        if structure_changed and self._workflow_loaded:
            self._apply_config_from_widgets("auto_load")

        self._maybe_autoload_remembered_workflow(description)

    def _on_layers_changed(self) -> None:
        self._conn.request_layers()

    def _on_layers_fetched(self, layers: dict) -> None:
        self._last_layers_payload = layers
        try:
            self._renderer.set_layers(layers)
        except Exception as e:
            self._append_log("err", f"layers update error: {e}")
        try:
            self._apply_layers_to_playground_combos(layers)
        except Exception as e:
            self._append_log(
                "err", f"playground layers update error: {e}",
            )

    def _apply_layers_to_playground_combos(self, layers: dict) -> None:
        """Push the shared layer data into every playground picker.

        Same bucket the resources section uses for `@thecanvas`:
        image layers (paint layers).  Playgrounds display a reference
        image, not a mask, so the mask bucket is not relevant here.
        Uses `_LayerComboBox.apply_layers`, so ordering, dedup, and
        popup guard are shared with the renderer.
        """
        image_list = layers.get("image") or []
        recent = layers.get("recent") or []
        for entry in self._playground_rows.values():
            widget = entry.get("layer_combo")
            if widget is None:
                continue
            try:
                widget.apply_layers(image_list, recent)
            except Exception:
                pass

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Playground input section
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _update_playgrounds(self, playgrounds: list) -> None:
        """Diff the daemon's playground registry against current rows.

        Each (playground, slot) pair gets its own row; the playground's
        name is shown only on its first slot's row.
        """
        desired_keys: set = set()
        for p in playgrounds:
            if not isinstance(p, dict):
                continue
            pid = p.get("id")
            if not pid:
                continue
            for slot in (p.get("layer_slots") or []):
                sid = slot.get("id") if isinstance(slot, dict) else None
                if sid:
                    desired_keys.add((pid, sid))

        # Remove vanished rows.
        for key in list(self._playground_rows.keys()):
            if key not in desired_keys:
                entry = self._playground_rows.pop(key)
                entry["row"].setParent(None)
                entry["row"].deleteLater()

        # Add or update rows.
        for p in playgrounds:
            if not isinstance(p, dict):
                continue
            pid = p.get("id")
            if not pid:
                continue
            slots = p.get("layer_slots") or []
            for i, slot in enumerate(slots):
                if not isinstance(slot, dict):
                    continue
                sid = slot.get("id")
                if not sid:
                    continue
                key = (pid, sid)
                entry = self._playground_rows.get(key)
                if entry is None:
                    entry = self._make_playground_row(
                        p, slot, show_name=(i == 0),
                    )
                    self._playground_rows[key] = entry
                    self._playgrounds_layout.addWidget(entry["row"])
                self._sync_playground_row(entry, p, slot)

        self._playgrounds_container.setVisible(bool(self._playground_rows))

        # Populate newly-added rows' pickers from cache.
        if self._last_layers_payload:
            self._apply_layers_to_playground_combos(self._last_layers_payload)

    def _make_playground_row(self, p: dict, slot: dict,
                             show_name: bool) -> dict:
        pid = p.get("id")
        sid = slot.get("id")
        pname = p.get("name") or pid or "?"

        row = QWidget()
        h = QHBoxLayout(row)
        h.setContentsMargins(0, 1, 0, 1)
        h.setSpacing(6)

        name_label = QLabel(pname if show_name else "")
        name_label.setStyleSheet("font-weight:600;")
        name_label.setMinimumWidth(110)
        h.addWidget(name_label, 0)

        # The slot id IS the display name.  No label field.
        slot_id_widget = QLabel(sid)
        slot_id_widget.setToolTip(
            f"Slot {sid!r} of the {pname!r} playground.\n"
            f"Layer displayed by that playground."
        )
        slot_id_widget.setMinimumWidth(90)
        h.addWidget(slot_id_widget, 0)

        source_combo = QComboBox()
        for opt in _LAYER_SOURCES:
            source_combo.addItem(opt)
        source_combo.setMinimumWidth(80)
        h.addWidget(source_combo, 0)

        layer_combo = _LayerComboBox(kind_hint="image")
        layer_combo.setMinimumWidth(110)
        h.addWidget(layer_combo, 1)

        entry = {
            "row": row,
            "name_label": name_label,
            "slot_id_widget": slot_id_widget,
            "source_combo": source_combo,
            "layer_combo": layer_combo,
            "playground_id": pid,
            "slot_id": sid,
            "auto_select_layer": slot.get("auto_select_layer"),
            "updating": False,
            "editing": False,
        }

        def on_source_changed(text, _entry=entry):
            if _entry["updating"]:
                return
            _entry["editing"] = True
            _entry["layer_combo"].setVisible(text == "layer")
            if text == "layer":
                self._maybe_auto_select_layer(
                    _entry["layer_combo"],
                    _entry["auto_select_layer"],
                )
            self._send_playground_set_layer(
                _entry["playground_id"], _entry["slot_id"], text,
                _entry["layer_combo"].currentText().strip()
                if text == "layer" else "",
            )

        def on_layer_activated(_i, _entry=entry):
            if _entry["updating"]:
                return
            if _entry["source_combo"].currentText() != "layer":
                return
            _entry["editing"] = True
            self._send_playground_set_layer(
                _entry["playground_id"], _entry["slot_id"], "layer",
                _entry["layer_combo"].currentText().strip(),
            )

        def on_layer_editing_finished(_entry=entry):
            if _entry["updating"]:
                return
            if _entry["source_combo"].currentText() != "layer":
                return
            _entry["editing"] = True
            self._send_playground_set_layer(
                _entry["playground_id"], _entry["slot_id"], "layer",
                _entry["layer_combo"].currentText().strip(),
            )

        source_combo.currentTextChanged.connect(on_source_changed)
        layer_combo.activated.connect(on_layer_activated)
        le = layer_combo.lineEdit()
        if le is not None:
            le.editingFinished.connect(on_layer_editing_finished)
        layer_combo.popupAboutToShow.connect(self._layers_watcher.schedule)

        return entry

    def _maybe_auto_select_layer(self, combo: _LayerComboBox,
                                 layer_name) -> bool:
        """Seed a slot's layer picker with `layer_name`.

        Fires only when:

          · `layer_name` is set (the slot spec included an
            `auto_select_layer` hint),
          · that layer is present in the current image-layer list, and
          · the combo's text is empty (a layer the user already picked
            or typed is never overwritten).

        Signals are blocked on both the combo and its line-edit so the
        programmatic `setCurrentText` does not fire `activated` /
        `editingFinished` — those would double-send the commit.
        """
        if not layer_name:
            return False
        image_layers = (self._last_layers_payload or {}).get("image") or []
        if layer_name not in image_layers:
            return False
        if combo.currentText().strip():
            return False

        combo.blockSignals(True)
        le = combo.lineEdit()
        if le is not None:
            le.blockSignals(True)
        try:
            combo.setCurrentText(layer_name)
        finally:
            if le is not None:
                le.blockSignals(False)
            combo.blockSignals(False)
        return True

    def _sync_playground_row(self, entry: dict, p: dict, slot: dict) -> None:
        new_pname = p.get("name") or p.get("id") or "?"
        # Only update the name text if this row is the one showing it
        # (the first slot row).  Subsequent rows have an empty text
        # label already.
        if entry["name_label"].text() != "":
            if entry["name_label"].text() != new_pname:
                entry["name_label"].setText(new_pname)

        # Slot id IS the display name.
        new_sid = slot.get("id") or "?"
        if entry["slot_id_widget"].text() != new_sid:
            entry["slot_id_widget"].setText(new_sid)
        entry["auto_select_layer"] = slot.get("auto_select_layer")

        selector = slot.get("selector") or {}
        source = selector.get("source") or "active"
        layer_name = selector.get("layer_name") or ""

        if entry["editing"]:
            if entry["source_combo"].currentText() == source:
                entry["editing"] = False
            else:
                return

        entry["updating"] = True
        try:
            if entry["source_combo"].currentText() != source:
                idx = entry["source_combo"].findText(source)
                if idx >= 0:
                    entry["source_combo"].setCurrentIndex(idx)

            combo = entry["layer_combo"]
            le = combo.lineEdit()
            has_focus = combo.hasFocus() or (
                le is not None and le.hasFocus()
            )
            if not has_focus:
                if combo.currentText() != layer_name:
                    combo.blockSignals(True)
                    if le is not None:
                        le.blockSignals(True)
                    try:
                        combo.setCurrentText(layer_name)
                    finally:
                        if le is not None:
                            le.blockSignals(False)
                        combo.blockSignals(False)
            combo.setVisible(source == "layer")
        finally:
            entry["updating"] = False

    def _send_playground_set_layer(
        self, pid: str, slot_id: str, source: str, layer_name: str,
    ) -> None:
        command = {
            "type": "playground_set_layer",
            "id": pid,
            "slot_id": slot_id,
            "source": source,
            "layer_name": layer_name if source == "layer" else "",
        }
        request_id = (
            f"playground-{pid}-{slot_id}-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
        )
        bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
        self._conn.enqueue(request_id, bundle)

    def _update_workflow_hint(self, description) -> None:
        has_workflow = False
        if isinstance(description, dict):
            sections = description.get("sections")
            if isinstance(sections, list):
                for s in sections:
                    if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("id") == "workflow":
                        has_workflow = True
                        break
        if has_workflow:
            self._hint.setText("")
            self._hint.hide()
        else:
            self._hint.setText(
                "No workflow loaded. Type a name in the Workflow field "
                "above and press Enter, or run "
                "<code>kritomatic comfyui comfy_load --name "
                "&lt;name&gt;</code> / <code>kritomatic comfyui panel "
                "run &lt;name&gt;</code> from a terminal."
            )
            self._hint.show()

    @staticmethod
    def _short_id_from_request_id(request_id: str) -> str:
        if not request_id:
            return "?"
        parts = request_id.split("-")
        return parts[-1] if parts else request_id

    def _on_run_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        if event.get("kind") != "progress":
            return
        result = event.get("result") or {}
        idx = event.get("index", 0)
        total = event.get("total", 0)
        cmd = result.get("command", "?")
        status = result.get("status", "?")
        message = result.get("message", "")
        cls = "ok" if status == "success" else "err"
        rid = event.get("request_id") or ""
        short_id = self._short_id_from_request_id(rid)
        self._append_log(
            cls, f"[{short_id}] [{idx + 1}/{total}] {cmd}: {message}"
        )

    def _on_command_completed(self, request_id: str, ok: bool,
                              summary: dict) -> None:
        if request_id.startswith("playground-"):
            if not ok:
                msg = summary.get("message", "") or "unknown error"
                self._append_log(
                    "err", f"Playground selector failed: {msg}",
                )
            return

        if request_id.startswith(("cancel-", "cancel_all-")):
            msg = summary.get("message", "")
            if ok:
                self._append_log("warn", f"Cancel sent: {msg}")
            else:
                self._append_log("err", f"Cancel failed: {msg}")
            return

        if request_id.startswith("apply-"):
            if not ok:
                msg = summary.get("message", "")
                self._append_log("err", f"config rejected: {msg}")
            return

        if request_id.startswith("save_config-"):
            if ok:
                msg = summary.get("message", "") or "saved"
                self._append_log("ok", msg)
            else:
                msg = summary.get("message", "")
                self._append_log("err", f"Save failed: {msg}")
            return

        if request_id.startswith("action-load-"):
            if ok:
                msg = summary.get("message", "") or "workflow loaded"
                self._append_log("ok", msg)
            else:
                msg = summary.get("message", "")
                self._append_log("err", f"Load failed: {msg}")
            return

        if request_id.startswith("autoload-"):
            results = summary.get("results", []) or []
            detail = ""
            if results and isinstance(results[0], dict):
                detail = results[0].get("message", "") or ""
            if not detail:
                detail = (summary.get("message")
                          or summary.get("error")
                          or "")
            if ok:
                self._append_log(
                    "ok",
                    "Auto-loaded: "
                    + (detail or repr(self._remembered_workflow)),
                )
            else:
                self._append_log(
                    "err",
                    "Auto-load failed: " + (detail or "unknown error"),
                )
            return

        # ---- Any run-<id> completion ----
        if not request_id.startswith("run-"):
            return

        self._active_runs.pop(request_id, None)
        short_id = self._short_id_from_request_id(request_id)

        if summary.get("intercepted"):
            msg = summary.get("message") or "Run intercepted"
            self._append_log(
                "hdr",
                f"[{short_id}] {msg} \u2014 review in interceptor playground",
            )
            self._update_run_buttons()
            return

        results = summary.get("results", []) or []
        cancelled_count = sum(
            1 for r in results
            if r.get("status") == "error"
            and "cancelled" in (r.get("message") or "").lower()
        )
        succ = summary.get("successful", 0)
        fail = summary.get("failed", 0)

        if cancelled_count > 0 and succ == 0:
            self._append_log(
                "warn",
                f"[{short_id}] Run cancelled. {cancelled_count} run(s) "
                f"not completed.",
            )
        elif summary.get("status") == "batch_complete":
            self._append_log(
                "hdr",
                f"[{short_id}] Run done: {succ} ok, {fail} failed.",
            )
        else:
            self._append_log("hdr", f"[{short_id}] Run done.")
        self._update_run_buttons()

    # ---- command submission ----

    def _on_field_commit(self, key: str, command: dict) -> None:
        if command.get("type") == "comfy_apply_config_from_widgets":
            self._pending_apply_source = key
            self._pending_apply_timer.start()
            return

        request_id = f"field-{key}"
        bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
        self._conn.enqueue(request_id, bundle)

    def _flush_pending_apply(self) -> None:
        source = self._pending_apply_source or "auto"
        self._pending_apply_source = ""
        self._apply_config_from_widgets(source)

    def _apply_config_from_widgets(self, source_key: str) -> None:
        try:
            cfg = self._renderer.build_config_from_widgets()
        except Exception as e:
            self._append_log("err", f"config build failed: {e}")
            return
        command = {
            "type": "comfy_apply_config",
            "resources": json.dumps(cfg["resources"]),
            "params": json.dumps(cfg["params"]),
            "crop": json.dumps(cfg["crop"]),
            "paste": json.dumps(cfg["paste"]),
        }
        request_id = f"apply-{source_key}-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
        bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
        self._conn.enqueue(request_id, bundle)

    def _on_action(self, item: dict, values: dict) -> None:
        key = item.get("key") or ""
        command = dict(item.get("command") or {})
        for fk, argname in (item.get("collect") or {}).items():
            if fk in values:
                v = values[fk]
                if argname == "seed":
                    if v not in (None, ""):
                        command[argname] = v
                    continue
                if argname == "output_name":
                    if v not in (None, ""):
                        command[argname] = v
                    continue
                if argname == "count":
                    try:
                        iv = int(v)
                    except (TypeError, ValueError):
                        iv = 1
                    if iv > 1:
                        command[argname] = iv
                    continue
                if argname == "timeout":
                    try:
                        fv = float(v)
                    except (TypeError, ValueError):
                        continue
                    command[argname] = fv
                    continue
                command[argname] = v

        if command.get("type") in ("comfy_panel_run", "comfy_save_config"):
            cfg = self._renderer.build_config_from_widgets()
            command["resources"] = json.dumps(cfg["resources"])
            command["params"] = json.dumps(cfg["params"])
            command["crop"] = json.dumps(cfg["crop"])
            command["paste"] = json.dumps(cfg["paste"])

        if key == "run":
            self._pending_apply_timer.stop()
            self._pending_apply_source = ""

            request_id = (
                f"run-{int(time.time() * 1000)}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
            )
            self._active_runs[request_id] = time.time()
            bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
            self._conn.send_run_now(request_id, bundle)
            short_id = self._short_id_from_request_id(request_id)
            self._append_log("hdr", f"[{short_id}] Run started.")
            self._update_run_buttons()

        elif key == "cancel":
            if not self._active_runs:
                self._append_log(
                    "warn", "No run in progress to cancel.",
                )
                return
            for run_id in list(self._active_runs.keys()):
                cancel_request_id = (
                    f"cancel-{int(time.time() * 1000)}-"
                    f"{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
                )
                self._conn.send_cancel_now(run_id, cancel_request_id)

        elif key == "cancel_all":
            request_id = f"cancel_all-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
            self._conn.send_cancel_now(None, request_id)

        elif key == "save_config":
            request_id = f"save_config-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
            bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
            self._conn.enqueue(request_id, bundle)
            self._append_log("hdr", "Saving config…")

        else:
            request_id = f"action-{key}-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
            bundle = {"id": request_id, "commands": [command]}
            self._conn.enqueue(request_id, bundle)
            self._append_log("hdr", f"Action {key} sent.")

    def _update_run_buttons(self) -> None:
        any_run = bool(self._active_runs)
        self._renderer.set_action_enabled(
            "run", self._workflow_loaded)
        self._renderer.set_action_enabled("cancel", any_run)
        any_batch = any_run or self._active_batches_count > 0
        self._renderer.set_action_enabled("cancel_all", any_batch)
        self._renderer.set_action_enabled("load", not any_run)
        self._renderer.set_action_enabled(
            "save_config", self._workflow_loaded and not any_run)

    def _append_log(self, kind: str, text: str) -> None:
        color = {
            "ok": "#0d652d",
            "err": "#c5221f",
            "warn": "#a05a00",
            "hdr": "#333",
        }.get(kind, "#333")
        weight = "bold" if kind == "hdr" else "normal"
        safe = (text.replace("&", "&amp;")
                    .replace("<", "&lt;")
                    .replace(">", "&gt;"))
        self._log.appendHtml(
            f'<span style="color:{color};font-weight:{weight};'
            f'font-family:monospace;">{safe}</span>'
        )

"""
layers_watcher.py — debounced, event-driven refresh trigger for the
                    docker's layer-alias dropdown.

Why this exists, and what Krita cannot do
=========================================
The docker's alias fields offer a dropdown of layer names, filtered by
kind (`image` vs `mask`). Keeping that list current requires knowing
when the layer tree changes.

Krita 6's Python API does not expose a signal that fires on layer
changes. A probe of the installed build shows:

    Notifier has: imageCreated, imageClosed, imageSaved,
                  applicationClosing, viewClosed, viewCreated,
                  windowCreated, windowIsBeingCreated,
                  configurationChanged.
    Document has: no modified / nodeAdded / nodeRemoved /
                  activeNodeChanged signal.
    Node has:     no sigChildAdded / sigChildRemoved / sigNameChanged /
                  sigVisibleChanged / sigOpacityChanged signal.

A layer add or remove performed in Krita's native layer panel is
therefore invisible to the daemon and the docker until somebody looks.

The alternative to a signal is polling. Polling is rejected by design:
it wakes the process on a schedule regardless of whether anything
happened, and the delay between a layer change and the list update is
bounded only by the poll interval. This module instead uses a set of
discrete, event-driven triggers, each of which fires on a specific
meaningful action:

  1. Notifier.imageCreated / imageClosed — a document appeared or
     disappeared, taking its layers with it.

  2. Panel events from the daemon — any state-mutating daemon command
     republishes the panel description; daemon-issued layer changes
     (notably the paste at the end of a comfy_generate run) come
     through here. Wired by the docker, not by this module.

  3. Docker focusInEvent — the user has engaged with the docker;
     refresh before they can click into an alias field. Wired by the
     docker.

  4. Layer combo showPopup — the user is about to open the dropdown;
     refresh immediately so the list is current at the moment they
     look. Wired by the docker via PanelRenderer.layerRefreshRequested.

  5. Event socket connected — the daemon just became reachable; catch
     anything missed during startup. Wired by the docker.

All five call `schedule()`. A burst (the daemon pasting five layers,
or the user tabbing quickly across several fields) collapses to one
fire because the timer is restarted on every call.

The one gap
===========
No trigger fires for a native-Krita layer change performed while no
other event happens. The specific case: the user has an alias field
focused, presses a Krita keyboard shortcut that adds a layer without
changing focus, then keeps typing. The list stays stale until the
next trigger — which is almost always the next popup open or the next
focus in, i.e. the next moment the user could actually consult it.
This is the accepted cost of not polling.

Debounce interval
=================
150 ms. Long enough to collapse any batch burst the daemon can produce
(the fastest state-mutating commands complete in tens of ms each, so a
`comfy_generate` paste of N layers is one burst), short enough to feel
immediate after a single manual layer add.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from PyQt6.QtCore import QObject, QTimer, pyqtSignal


DEBOUNCE_MS = 150


class LayersWatcher(QObject):
    """Debounced trigger. Emits `layersChanged` at most once per
    DEBOUNCE_MS, on any of the events listed in the module docstring.
    The consumer (KritomaticPanel) wires `layersChanged` to
    `DaemonConnection.request_layers`, which does the actual fetch on
    a fresh socket.
    """

    layersChanged = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._timer = QTimer(self)
        self._timer.setSingleShot(True)
        self._timer.setInterval(DEBOUNCE_MS)
        self._timer.timeout.connect(self._fire)

        self._notifier = None
        self._attach_notifier()

    # -- notifier wiring --

    def _attach_notifier(self) -> None:
        try:
            from krita import Krita
            self._notifier = Krita.instance().notifier()
        except Exception:
            self._notifier = None
            return
        if self._notifier is None:
            return
        try:
            self._notifier.imageCreated.connect(self._on_document_opened)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self._notifier.imageClosed.connect(self._on_document_closed)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _on_document_opened(self, _doc) -> None:
        self.schedule()

    def _on_document_closed(self, _doc) -> None:
        self.schedule()

    # -- debounced fire --

    def schedule(self) -> None:
        """(Re)start the debounce timer. Every trigger calls this."""
        self._timer.start()

    def _fire(self) -> None:
        self.layersChanged.emit()

    # -- lifecycle --

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the timer and disconnect from Notifier. Idempotent."""
        try:
            self._timer.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
        if self._notifier is not None:
            try:
                self._notifier.imageCreated.disconnect(
                    self._on_document_opened)
            except Exception:
                pass
            try:
                self._notifier.imageClosed.disconnect(
                    self._on_document_closed)
            except Exception:
                pass
            self._notifier = None
