```python
"""
Description → Qt widget tree.

Consumes the panel description and builds a widget tree in a container
layout. Section kinds supported:

    metadata      — key/value rows
    form          — QGroupBox + QFormLayout of typed fields
    actions       — row of buttons
    workflow-bar  — picker + Load / Save-config on one row

On a new description:

  * If structure_id is unchanged, values are synced in place. Fields
    that currently have focus are skipped.
  * If structure_id changed, the tree is rebuilt.

Edits are routed to a commit callback. Actions are routed to an action
callback.

Composite (row) fields
======================
A field with `type: "row"` is built by `_build_row_field` into a
QWidget with an HBoxLayout, one sub-widget per `sub_fields` entry.
The composite itself is *not* registered in `_field_widgets` — its
`key` is only the row's label. Its sub-widgets are registered as
ordinary leaf fields under their own `key`s, so every method that
iterates `_field_widgets` (read / apply / sync / focus / in-flight /
build_config_from_widgets / set_layers) works unchanged. The only
places that needed a new branch were `_build_form`, `_sync_values`,
and `_find_section`; each gained a small flattening step that walks
`sub_fields` in addition to the top level.

Pinned actions
==============
A section with `kind == "actions"` contains a row of buttons (Run /
Cancel / Cancel-All on the docker's run-actions section). If the host
passed an `actions_layout` to the constructor, actions sections are
routed there instead of into the scrollable form layout. The host is
expected to place that layout at a fixed position outside any scroll
area — the docker puts it right above the Log section, so those
buttons stay visible regardless of how far the user has scrolled the
form.

When no `actions_layout` is provided (e.g. the web panel does its own
rendering and never uses this class), actions sections fall through
to the scrollable form, same as before this change.

The renderer's contract: it always clears `actions_layout` on rebuild
before repopulating it. Widgets from the previous render are detached
and scheduled for deletion via `_section_widgets` (which holds every
built widget regardless of location), and the layout's bookkeeping is
cleared via `takeAt(0)` so the layout does not hold dangling
references. Double-calling `deleteLater()` on a widget already
scheduled for deletion is safe.

Hidden fields (`visible: false`)
================================
A field carrying `visible: false` is created and registered exactly
like any other leaf field, but it is not added to the QFormLayout
row. Instead, it is parented to the containing QGroupBox and hidden
via `setVisible(False)`.

QFormLayout has no per-row visibility primitive in Qt6, so the
"parent to group, skip addRow" arrangement is the only one where
the field's widget takes zero space in the form while still existing
as a live QObject parented to the section.

The registration in `_field_widgets` is what makes
`build_config_from_widgets` still pick up the hidden field's value —
which is the entire point of `visible: false` versus dropping the
field from the description. A param hidden by a client-side filter
keeps its last-applied value through every subsequent
`comfy_apply_config` that the docker sends, exactly as if it were
still on screen.

`_reevaluate_visibility` treats `visible: false` as a hard-hide that
`visible_when` cannot override.

Client-side filters (`set_param_prefix`)
========================================
The docker maintains a Parameters-section filter prefix that is a
*client-local display preference* — not a daemon-side setting. When
the prefix changes, the docker calls `set_param_prefix()`, which
forces a rebuild of the tree against the last received description
with `cfg-param.*` fields whose title does not start with the prefix
marked `visible: false`. This is how the docker and the web panel
can maintain independent filters: the daemon never sees the prefix
at all.

`_filtered_description` is also where the current prefix is
*injected back into* every `local_handler: "param_prefix_filter"`
field's `value`. The daemon always sends `value: ""` for such fields
(it has no reason to carry a value the client owns), so without this
injection a rebuild or sync from the daemon would silently clear the
prefix field's widget while leaving the params filtered — the very
bug the injection prevents.

Local handlers (`local_handler`)
================================
A field carrying `local_handler: "name"` is a client-side widget
whose edits are not sent to the daemon. When the widget's commit
signal fires, the renderer invokes the handler registered under
`name` via `set_local_handler`, passing the new value. The daemon's
panel description carries such fields for two reasons: (a) so their
row label and position are consistent with the rest of the panel
layout, and (b) so the client's structure-id hash matches the
daemon's (so updates sync in place rather than rebuilding on every
panel push). The daemon's `_STRUCTURE_FIELD_KEYS` includes
`local_handler` for the same reason.

Because the daemon has no value for such fields, the renderer's
`_filtered_description` is where the client's current value is
written back into the description before `_rebuild` and
`_sync_values` consume it. See "Client-side filters" above.

Shared layer picker
===================
The `_LayerComboBox` class (an editable QComboBox with a
case-insensitive, MatchContains completer) is used by both the
resources section's alias pickers and the docker's playgrounds
section's layer picker. Repopulation goes through one method on the
class — `apply_layers(bucket, recent)` — so ordering ("recent-in-
bucket first, then the rest of the bucket in daemon order"), the
popup-open guard, and the text-preservation rule are identical
everywhere. Two call sites use it:

  · `PanelRenderer.set_layers`, which dispatches per-field based on
    the field spec's `kind_hint` (`image` or `mask`).
  · `KritomaticPanel._apply_layers_to_playground_combos`, which
    pushes the `image` bucket into every playground row's combo.

Neither path duplicates the ordering logic. A future widget that
needs a layer picker instantiates `_LayerComboBox` and calls
`apply_layers`; no new code beyond wiring the trigger.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt, QObject, pyqtSignal
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import (
    QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QHBoxLayout, QFormLayout, QGroupBox,
    QLabel, QLineEdit, QPlainTextEdit, QCheckBox, QRadioButton,
    QButtonGroup, QComboBox, QSpinBox, QDoubleSpinBox, QPushButton,
    QFrame, QSizePolicy,
)


def _esc(text) -> str:
    return (str(text)
            .replace("&", "&amp;")
            .replace("<", "&lt;")
            .replace(">", "&gt;"))


_DISABLED_QSS = (
    "QPushButton:disabled { background:#c8c8c8;color:#f0f0f0; }"
)


def _qss_danger(padding: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"QPushButton {{ background:#c5221f;color:white;padding:{padding}; }}"
        + _DISABLED_QSS
    )


def _qss_primary(padding: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"QPushButton {{ background:#1a73e8;color:white;padding:{padding}; }}"
        + _DISABLED_QSS
    )


class _CommittableTextEdit(QPlainTextEdit):
    commitRequested = pyqtSignal(str)

    def focusOutEvent(self, event):
        super().focusOutEvent(event)
        self.commitRequested.emit(self.toPlainText())


class _LayerComboBox(QComboBox):
    popupAboutToShow = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(self, kind_hint: str, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._kind_hint = kind_hint
        self._popup_open = False
        self.setEditable(True)
        self.setInsertPolicy(QComboBox.InsertPolicy.NoInsert)
        self.setSizePolicy(
            QSizePolicy.Policy.Expanding, QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed
        )
        completer = self.completer()
        if completer is not None:
            completer.setCaseSensitivity(
                Qt.CaseSensitivity.CaseInsensitive)
            completer.setFilterMode(Qt.MatchFlag.MatchContains)

    def showPopup(self):
        self._popup_open = True
        self.popupAboutToShow.emit()
        super().showPopup()

    def hidePopup(self):
        super().hidePopup()
        self._popup_open = False

    def is_popup_open(self) -> bool:
        return self._popup_open

    def apply_layers(self, bucket: list, recent: list) -> None:
        """Populate the combo from a bucket of layer names.

        `bucket` is every layer name of this combo's kind (`image`
        for paint layers, `mask` for selection/transparency masks);
        `recent` is the daemon's recent-aliases list, unfiltered.
        Items are ordered: **recent-in-bucket first** (in `recent`'s
        order), then the rest of the bucket (in `bucket`'s order).

        No-op when the popup is open: repopulating mid-selection
        would shuffle the list under the user's cursor.  Both the
        renderer's `set_layers` and the docker's playground rows go
        through this method, so the ordering and popup guard are the
        same everywhere.

        Preserves the current text across the repopulation so a
        typed-but-not-yet-committed value survives a background
        `layersFetched` emit.
        """
        if self.is_popup_open():
            return
        bucket_set = set(bucket)
        recent_in_bucket = [a for a in recent if a in bucket_set]
        recent_set = set(recent_in_bucket)
        rest = [b for b in bucket if b not in recent_set]
        new_list = recent_in_bucket + rest

        current_text = self.currentText()
        self.blockSignals(True)
        le = self.lineEdit()
        if le is not None:
            le.blockSignals(True)
        try:
            self.clear()
            self.addItems(new_list)
            self.setCurrentText(current_text)
        finally:
            if le is not None:
                le.blockSignals(False)
            self.blockSignals(False)


class PanelRenderer(QObject):
    """Renders a panel description into a container layout."""

    layerRefreshRequested = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(self, container_layout, commit_callback, action_callback,
                 actions_layout=None):
        super().__init__()
        self._layout = container_layout
        self._commit = commit_callback
        self._action = action_callback
        # Optional host-supplied layout for `kind == "actions"` sections.
        # When None, actions sections go into the scrollable form (the
        # browser panel's arrangement).  When a QVBoxLayout, actions
        # sections go there instead, and the docker owns that layout's
        # placement in its non-scrolling area.  See "Pinned actions" in
        # the module docstring.
        self._actions_layout = actions_layout
        self._structure_id = None
        self._last_description = None
        self._section_widgets = []
        self._section_specs = []
        self._field_widgets = {}
        self._field_specs = {}
        self._action_buttons = {}
        # Client-side Parameters filter prefix.  Empty string means "no
        # filter".  Set via `set_param_prefix`, which forces a rebuild
        # against `_last_description`.  See "Client-side filters" in
        # the module docstring.
        self._param_prefix_filter = ""
        # Handlers registered via `set_local_handler`; keyed by the
        # `local_handler` string a field spec carries.  See "Local
        # handlers" in the module docstring.
        self._local_handlers = {}

    def set_local_handler(self, name: str, fn) -> None:
        """Register a client-side handler for fields with
        `local_handler: name`.  Replaces any prior registration under
        the same name."""
        self._local_handlers[name] = fn

    def set_param_prefix(self, prefix: str) -> None:
        """Set the client-side Parameters filter prefix.

        If `prefix` differs from the current one, rebuild the tree
        against `_last_description` (re-applying the filter via
        `_filtered_description`).  `_structure_id` is cleared during
        the rebuild so the next `render()` call from the daemon takes
        the rebuild path with the same `struct_id` the daemon sends —
        this keeps the client's view of "last seen daemon structure"
        in sync.

        A no-op if `prefix` matches the current value.
        """
        if prefix == self._param_prefix_filter:
            return
        self._param_prefix_filter = prefix
        if self._last_description is not None:
            self._structure_id = None
            self.render(self._last_description)

    def get_param_prefix(self) -> str:
        """Return the current client-side Parameters filter prefix."""
        return self._param_prefix_filter

    def _filtered_description(self, description: dict) -> dict:
        """Return a copy of `description` with client-side filters and
        local-handler values applied.

        Two transformations:

          1. **Local-handler value injection.**  For each field carrying
             `local_handler: "param_prefix_filter"`, the field's `value`
             is replaced with the renderer's current prefix.  The daemon
             never carries a real value for client-local fields — its
             spec always says `value: ""` — so without this injection a
             rebuild or sync from the daemon would silently clear the
             field's widget.  (Rebuild creates it empty; sync calls
             `_apply_value("")` on the existing widget.)

          2. **Client-side filter.**  Each `cfg-param.*` field whose title
             does not start with `_param_prefix_filter` is marked
             `visible: false`.  The field is still emitted, still has its
             `config_path` and value, and is still read by
             `build_config_from_widgets` — only the visible row is
             hidden.  Empty prefix means "no filter" (no visibility
             changes).

        Returns `description` unchanged (identity) when neither
        transformation would touch anything, so the caller's `is` check
        on the return value still means "nothing changed".
        """
        prefix = self._param_prefix_filter
        sections = description.get("sections") or []
        new_sections = []
        any_change = False
        for s in sections:
            old_fields = s.get("fields") or []
            new_fields = []
            section_changed = False
            for f in old_fields:
                key = f.get("key") or ""
                f_mod = f
                if f.get("local_handler") == "param_prefix_filter":
                    if f.get("value") != prefix:
                        f_mod = dict(f)
                        f_mod["value"] = prefix
                        section_changed = True
                elif prefix and key.startswith("cfg-param."):
                    title = key[len("cfg-param."):]
                    if not title.startswith(prefix):
                        f_mod = dict(f)
                        f_mod["visible"] = False
                        section_changed = True
                new_fields.append(f_mod)
            if section_changed:
                new_s = dict(s)
                new_s["fields"] = new_fields
                new_sections.append(new_s)
                any_change = True
            else:
                new_sections.append(s)
        if not any_change:
            return description
        new_desc = dict(description)
        new_desc["sections"] = new_sections
        return new_desc

    def render(self, description: dict) -> None:
        self._last_description = description
        filtered = self._filtered_description(description)
        struct_id = filtered.get("structure_id", "")
        if struct_id == self._structure_id:
            self._sync_values(filtered)
            return
        self._rebuild(filtered)
        self._structure_id = struct_id

    # ---- rebuild ----

    def _rebuild(self, description: dict) -> None:
        focused_key, focused_cursor = self._capture_focus()

        # Detach and schedule deletion of every widget built by the
        # previous render.  Widgets living in `actions_layout` are in
        # `_section_widgets` too, so this loop clears both placements.
        for w in self._section_widgets:
            w.setParent(None)
            w.deleteLater()
        self._section_widgets = []
        self._field_widgets = {}
        self._field_specs = {}
        self._action_buttons = {}
        self._section_specs = description.get("sections", []) or []

        # Clear the pinned-actions layout's bookkeeping.  The widgets
        # it held were already detached and deleted by the loop above;
        # this just tells the layout to forget them so it does not
        # hold dangling references across the rebuild.
        if self._actions_layout is not None:
            while self._actions_layout.count() > 0:
                item = self._actions_layout.takeAt(0)
                if item is None:
                    break
                w = item.widget()
                if w is not None:
                    # Defensive: also delete here, in case a future
                    # code path adds to actions_layout without going
                    # through _section_widgets.  deleteLater is
                    # idempotent, so double-scheduling is harmless.
                    w.setParent(None)
                    w.deleteLater()

        for section in self._section_specs:
            widget = self._build_section(section)
            if widget is None:
                continue

            if (section.get("kind") == "actions"
                    and self._actions_layout is not None):
                # Pinned: outside the scroll area, above the Log.
                self._actions_layout.addWidget(widget)
            else:
                # Scrollable: insert before the trailing stretch so
                # the form fields stay top-aligned.
                count = self._layout.count()
                insert_at = count
                for i in range(count):
                    item = self._layout.itemAt(i)
                    if item and item.spacerItem():
                        insert_at = i
                        break
                self._layout.insertWidget(insert_at, widget)

            self._section_widgets.append(widget)

        self._restore_focus(focused_key, focused_cursor)

    # ---- focus capture / restore ----

    def _capture_focus(self):
        for key, widget in self._field_widgets.items():
            if widget.hasFocus():
                return key, self._read_cursor(widget)
            for child in widget.findChildren(QWidget):
                if child.hasFocus():
                    return key, self._read_cursor(child)
        return None, None

    @staticmethod
    def _read_cursor(widget):
        try:
            if isinstance(widget, QLineEdit):
                return ("line", widget.cursorPosition())
            if isinstance(widget, QPlainTextEdit):
                return ("plain", widget.textCursor().position())
            if isinstance(widget, QComboBox) and widget.isEditable():
                le = widget.lineEdit()
                if le is not None:
                    return ("combo", le.cursorPosition())
        except Exception:
            pass
        return None

    def _restore_focus(self, key, cursor) -> None:
        if not key or key not in self._field_widgets:
            return
        widget = self._field_widgets[key]
        target = self._find_focusable_leaf(widget)
        if target is None:
            return
        try:
            target.setFocus()
        except Exception:
            return
        if cursor is None:
            return
        kind, pos = cursor
        try:
            if kind == "line" and isinstance(target, QLineEdit):
                target.setCursorPosition(pos)
            elif kind == "plain" and isinstance(target, QPlainTextEdit):
                cur = target.textCursor()
                cur.setPosition(pos)
                target.setTextCursor(cur)
            elif (kind == "combo"
                  and isinstance(target, QComboBox)
                  and target.isEditable()):
                le = target.lineEdit()
                if le is not None:
                    le.setCursorPosition(min(pos, len(le.text())))
        except Exception:
            pass

    @staticmethod
    def _find_focusable_leaf(widget):
        leaf_types = (
            QLineEdit, QPlainTextEdit, QSpinBox, QDoubleSpinBox,
            QComboBox, QCheckBox,
        )
        if isinstance(widget, leaf_types):
            return widget
        for child in widget.findChildren(QWidget):
            if isinstance(child, leaf_types):
                return child
        return None

    def _build_section(self, section: dict):
        kind = section.get("kind")
        if kind == "metadata":
            return self._build_metadata(section)
        if kind == "form":
            return self._build_form(section)
        if kind == "actions":
            return self._build_actions(section)
        if kind == "workflow-bar":
            return self._build_workflow_bar(section)
        return None

    def _build_metadata(self, section: dict):
        fields = section.get("fields") or []
        if not fields:
            return None
        container = QWidget()
        layout = QVBoxLayout(container)
        layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 4)
        layout.setSpacing(2)
        for f in fields:
            label = f.get("label")
            value = f.get("value", "")
            emphasis = f.get("emphasis") or "normal"
            text = f"<b>{_esc(label)}:</b> {_esc(value)}" if label else _esc(value)
            if emphasis == "strong":
                text = f"<b>{text}</b>"
            elif emphasis == "dim":
                text = f"<span style='color:#888'>{text}</span>"
            elif emphasis == "danger":
                text = f"<span style='color:#c5221f'>{text}</span>"
            lbl = QLabel(text)
            lbl.setTextFormat(Qt.TextFormat.RichText)
            lbl.setWordWrap(True)
            layout.addWidget(lbl)
        return container

    def _build_form(self, section: dict):
        group = QGroupBox(section.get("title") or "")
        form = QFormLayout(group)
        form.setFieldGrowthPolicy(
            QFormLayout.FieldGrowthPolicy.ExpandingFieldsGrow
        )
        for f in section.get("fields", []):
            key = f.get("key")
            if not key:
                continue

            if f.get("type") == "row":
                widget = self._build_row_field(f)
                if widget is None:
                    continue
                label = f.get("label") or key
                form.addRow(label, widget)
                continue

            widget = self._build_field_widget(f)
            if widget is None:
                continue
            self._field_widgets[key] = widget
            self._field_specs[key] = f

            if f.get("visible") is False:
                # Invisible but live.  See the module docstring,
                # "Hidden fields (`visible: false`)", for why the
                # widget is parented to the group without a form row
                # rather than added-and-hidden.
                widget.setParent(group)
                widget.setVisible(False)
                continue

            label = f.get("label") or key
            if f.get("overridden"):
                label = f"{label} ●"
            form.addRow(label, widget)
        self._reevaluate_visibility()
        return group

    def _build_row_field(self, f: dict):
        """Build one composite row: N sub-widgets laid out horizontally.

        The sub-widgets are registered in `_field_widgets` /
        `_field_specs` under their own `key`s. The returned container
        is what the form adds to its row, but the container itself is
        *not* registered — it has no `config_path` of its own, only
        its children do.

        `stretch` on each sub-field maps to QHBoxLayout.addWidget's
        stretch argument: 0 sizes the widget to its natural width,
        positive values fill the remaining space proportionally. This
        is what keeps the `global/active/layer` dropdown at its
        natural width while the layer-name text input fills the rest
        of the row.
        """
        subs = f.get("sub_fields")
        if not isinstance(subs, list):
            return None

        container = QWidget()
        layout = QHBoxLayout(container)
        layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        layout.setSpacing(6)

        any_added = False
        for sub in subs:
            if not isinstance(sub, dict):
                continue
            sub_key = sub.get("key")
            if not sub_key:
                continue
            sub_widget = self._build_field_widget(sub)
            if sub_widget is None:
                continue
            self._field_widgets[sub_key] = sub_widget
            self._field_specs[sub_key] = sub

            try:
                stretch = int(sub.get("stretch", 0))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                stretch = 0
            if stretch < 0:
                stretch = 0

            layout.addWidget(sub_widget, stretch)
            any_added = True

        return container if any_added else None

    def _build_workflow_bar(self, section: dict):
        """Picker on the left (expanding), action buttons on the right.

        The section's `fields` list contains exactly one picker field
        in practice; the loop is written as a general `for` so a
        future provider could add more without touching the renderer.
        """
        group = QGroupBox(section.get("title") or "")
        outer = QVBoxLayout(group)
        outer.setContentsMargins(6, 6, 6, 6)
        outer.setSpacing(0)

        row = QWidget()
        h = QHBoxLayout(row)
        h.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        h.setSpacing(6)

        for f in section.get("fields", []) or []:
            key = f.get("key")
            if not key:
                continue
            widget = self._build_field_widget(f)
            if widget is None:
                continue
            self._field_widgets[key] = widget
            self._field_specs[key] = f
            h.addWidget(widget, 1)

        for item in section.get("items", []) or []:
            key = item.get("key") or ""
            btn = QPushButton(item.get("label") or key)
            style = item.get("style")
            if style == "primary":
                btn.setStyleSheet(_qss_primary("6px 14px"))
            elif style == "danger":
                btn.setStyleSheet(_qss_danger("6px 14px"))
            self._action_buttons[key] = btn
            btn.clicked.connect(
                lambda _checked=False, it=item: self._action(
                    it, self._read_all_values()
                )
            )
            h.addWidget(btn, 0)

        outer.addWidget(row)
        return group

    def _build_field_widget(self, f: dict):
        key = f["key"]
        ftype = f.get("type", "text")
        value = f.get("value")

        if ftype == "text":
            kind_hint = f.get("kind_hint")
            if kind_hint in ("image", "mask"):
                w = _LayerComboBox(kind_hint)
                w.setCurrentText("" if value is None else str(value))
                w.activated.connect(
                    lambda _i, k=key, w=w: self._on_text_commit(
                        k, w.currentText()
                    )
                )
                le = w.lineEdit()
                if le is not None:
                    le.editingFinished.connect(
                        lambda k=key, w=w: self._on_text_commit(
                            k, w.currentText()
                        )
                    )
                w.popupAboutToShow.connect(
                    self.layerRefreshRequested.emit
                )
                return w

            w = QLineEdit()
            w.setText("" if value is None else str(value))
            local_handler = f.get("local_handler")
            if local_handler:
                # Route commit through the client-local handler
                # instead of the daemon.  The spec's `value` is kept
                # up to date by `_filtered_description`, so subsequent
                # syncs from the daemon (which carry the daemon's
                # empty-string view of a local-handler field) don't
                # clobber what the client set.
                w.editingFinished.connect(
                    lambda k=key, lh=local_handler, w=w: (
                        self._on_local_handler_commit(k, lh, w.text())
                    )
                )
            else:
                w.editingFinished.connect(
                    lambda k=key, w=w: self._on_text_commit(k, w.text())
                )
            return w

        if ftype == "textarea":
            w = _CommittableTextEdit()
            w.setPlainText("" if value is None else str(value))
            w.setFixedHeight(72)
            w.commitRequested.connect(
                lambda text, k=key: self._on_text_commit(k, text)
            )
            return w

        if ftype == "integer":
            w = QSpinBox()
            try:
                w.setRange(int(f.get("min", -10 ** 9)),
                           int(f.get("max", 10 ** 9)))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                w.setRange(-10 ** 9, 10 ** 9)
            if f.get("step") is not None:
                try:
                    w.setSingleStep(int(f["step"]))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    pass
            if value is not None:
                try:
                    w.setValue(int(value))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    pass
            w.valueChanged.connect(
                lambda v, k=key: self._on_field_commit(k, int(v))
            )
            return w

        if ftype == "number":
            w = QDoubleSpinBox()
            w.setDecimals(6)
            try:
                w.setRange(float(f.get("min", -10 ** 12)),
                           float(f.get("max", 10 ** 12)))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                w.setRange(-10 ** 12, 10 ** 12)
            step = f.get("step")
            if step is not None and step != "any":
                try:
                    w.setSingleStep(float(step))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    pass
            if value is not None:
                try:
                    w.setValue(float(value))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    pass
            w.valueChanged.connect(
                lambda v, k=key: self._on_field_commit(k, float(v))
            )
            return w

        if ftype == "toggle":
            w = QCheckBox()
            w.setChecked(bool(value))
            w.toggled.connect(
                lambda v, k=key: self._on_field_commit(k, bool(v))
            )
            return w

        if ftype == "radio":
            container = QWidget()
            h = QHBoxLayout(container)
            h.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
            grp = QButtonGroup(container)
            for opt in f.get("options", []):
                rb = QRadioButton(str(opt))
                if str(value) == str(opt):
                    rb.setChecked(True)
                grp.addButton(rb)
                h.addWidget(rb)
                rb.toggled.connect(
                    lambda checked, k=key, o=str(opt): (
                        self._on_field_commit(k, o) if checked else None
                    )
                )
            return container

        if ftype == "select":
            w = QComboBox()
            for opt in f.get("options", []):
                w.addItem(str(opt))
            if value is not None:
                idx = w.findText(str(value))
                if idx >= 0:
                    w.setCurrentIndex(idx)
            w.currentTextChanged.connect(
                lambda v, k=key: self._on_field_commit(k, v)
            )
            return w

        return None

    def _build_actions(self, section: dict):
        container = QWidget()
        h = QHBoxLayout(container)
        h.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        h.setSpacing(0)

        items = section.get("items", []) or []
        added_any = False

        for item in items:
            key = item.get("key") or ""
            is_thin = bool(item.get("thin", False))
            attaches = is_thin and bool(item.get("attach_to"))

            if added_any:
                h.addSpacing(-2 if attaches else 6)

            btn = QPushButton(item.get("label") or key)
            style = item.get("style")

            if style == "primary":
                btn.setStyleSheet(_qss_primary("6px 14px"))
            elif style == "danger":
                if is_thin:
                    btn.setFixedWidth(40)
                    btn.setStyleSheet(_qss_danger("6px 4px"))
                else:
                    btn.setStyleSheet(_qss_danger("6px 14px"))

            self._action_buttons[key] = btn
            btn.clicked.connect(
                lambda _checked=False, it=item: self._action(
                    it, self._read_all_values()
                )
            )
            h.addWidget(btn)
            added_any = True

        return container

    # ---- commits ----

    def _on_text_commit(self, key: str, new_value: str) -> None:
        spec = self._field_specs.get(key)
        if spec is None:
            return
        old_value = spec.get("value")
        if str(new_value) == str(old_value if old_value is not None else ""):
            return
        spec["value"] = new_value
        self._on_field_commit(key, new_value)

    def _on_local_handler_commit(
        self, key: str, handler_name: str, new_value: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Commit a `local_handler` field.

        Updates the spec's `value` so subsequent daemon-pushed syncs
        (which carry the daemon's view of the value — empty string for
        fields the daemon never set) don't clobber the widget, then
        invokes the registered client-local handler if any.  No
        daemon command is dispatched.
        """
        spec = self._field_specs.get(key)
        if spec is not None:
            old_value = spec.get("value")
            if str(new_value) == str(
                    old_value if old_value is not None else ""):
                # No change; still invoke the handler so callers can
                # observe "commit" events even without value drift
                # (e.g. persistence on blur, which just re-saves the
                # current value).
                pass
            else:
                spec["value"] = new_value
        handler = self._local_handlers.get(handler_name)
        if handler is None:
            return
        try:
            handler(new_value)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _on_field_commit(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        self._reevaluate_visibility()

        spec = self._field_specs.get(key)
        if spec is None:
            return
        section = self._find_section(key)
        if section is None:
            return

        section_commit = section.get("commit")
        if section_commit:
            args = {}
            for fk, argname in (section_commit.get("arg_map") or {}).items():
                fspec = self._field_specs.get(fk)
                fw = self._field_widgets.get(fk)
                if fspec is None or fw is None:
                    continue
                args[argname] = self._read_widget_value(fspec, fw)
            command = {"type": section_commit["type"], **args}
            self._commit(key, command)
            return

        if spec.get("set_command"):
            arg_key = spec.get("arg_key", "value")
            command = dict(spec["set_command"])
            command[arg_key] = value
            self._commit(key, command)
            return

        if spec.get("config_path"):
            self._commit(key, {"type": "comfy_apply_config_from_widgets"})

    def _read_widget_value(self, spec: dict, widget):
        ftype = spec.get("type", "text")
        try:
            if ftype == "text":
                if isinstance(widget, QComboBox):
                    return widget.currentText()
                return widget.text()
            if ftype == "textarea":
                return widget.toPlainText()
            if ftype == "integer":
                return int(widget.value())
            if ftype == "number":
                return float(widget.value())
            if ftype == "toggle":
                return bool(widget.isChecked())
            if ftype == "select":
                return widget.currentText()
            if ftype == "radio":
                for child in widget.findChildren(QRadioButton):
                    if child.isChecked():
                        return child.text()
                return ""
        except Exception:
            return ""
        return None

    def _read_all_values(self) -> dict:
        out = {}
        for key, widget in self._field_widgets.items():
            spec = self._field_specs.get(key)
            if spec is None:
                continue
            out[key] = self._read_widget_value(spec, widget)
        return out

    def _find_section(self, key: str):
        for section in self._section_specs:
            for f in section.get("fields", []) or []:
                if f.get("key") == key:
                    return section
                if f.get("type") == "row":
                    for sub in f.get("sub_fields", []) or []:
                        if isinstance(sub, dict) and sub.get("key") == key:
                            return section
        return None

    # ---- v2 config collection ----

    def build_config_from_widgets(self) -> dict:
        """Assemble the v2 panel config from the current widget state."""
        cfg: dict = {
            "resources": {},
            "params": {},
            "crop": {},
            "paste": {},
        }
        for key, spec in self._field_specs.items():
            path = spec.get("config_path")
            if not path:
                continue
            widget = self._field_widgets.get(key)
            if widget is None:
                continue
            value = self._read_widget_value(spec, widget)
            self._set_path(cfg, path, value)
        return cfg

    @staticmethod
    def _set_path(cfg: dict, path, value) -> None:
        d = cfg
        for key in path[:-1]:
            if key not in d:
                d[key] = {}
            d = d[key]
        d[path[-1]] = value

    # ---- sync ----

    def _sync_values(self, description: dict) -> None:
        new_specs = {}
        for section in description.get("sections", []) or []:
            for f in section.get("fields", []) or []:
                key = f.get("key")
                if not key:
                    continue
                if f.get("type") == "row":
                    for sub in f.get("sub_fields", []) or []:
                        if isinstance(sub, dict) and sub.get("key"):
                            new_specs[sub["key"]] = sub
                else:
                    new_specs[key] = f

        for key, spec in new_specs.items():
            widget = self._field_widgets.get(key)
            if widget is None:
                continue
            if spec.get("no_sync"):
                self._field_specs[key] = spec
                continue
            if self._is_focused(widget):
                self._field_specs[key] = spec
                continue
            self._apply_value(spec, widget)
            self._field_specs[key] = spec

        self._section_specs = description.get("sections", []) or []
        self._reevaluate_visibility()

    @staticmethod
    def _is_focused(widget) -> bool:
        try:
            if widget.hasFocus():
                return True
            for child in widget.findChildren(QWidget):
                if child.hasFocus():
                    return True
        except Exception:
            pass
        return False

    def _apply_value(self, spec: dict, widget) -> None:
        ftype = spec.get("type", "text")
        value = spec.get("value")
        try:
            if ftype == "text":
                target = "" if value is None else str(value)
                if isinstance(widget, QComboBox):
                    if widget.currentText() != target:
                        widget.blockSignals(True)
                        widget.setCurrentText(target)
                        widget.blockSignals(False)
                else:
                    if widget.text() != target:
                        widget.blockSignals(True)
                        widget.setText(target)
                        widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "textarea":
                target = "" if value is None else str(value)
                if widget.toPlainText() != target:
                    widget.blockSignals(True)
                    widget.setPlainText(target)
                    widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "integer":
                try:
                    target = int(value)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    return
                if widget.value() != target:
                    widget.blockSignals(True)
                    widget.setValue(target)
                    widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "number":
                try:
                    target = float(value)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    return
                if abs(widget.value() - target) > 1e-9:
                    widget.blockSignals(True)
                    widget.setValue(target)
                    widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "toggle":
                target = bool(value)
                if widget.isChecked() != target:
                    widget.blockSignals(True)
                    widget.setChecked(target)
                    widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "select":
                target = "" if value is None else str(value)
                if widget.currentText() != target:
                    idx = widget.findText(target)
                    if idx >= 0:
                        widget.blockSignals(True)
                        widget.setCurrentIndex(idx)
                        widget.blockSignals(False)
            elif ftype == "radio":
                target = "" if value is None else str(value)
                for child in widget.findChildren(QRadioButton):
                    should = child.text() == target
                    if child.isChecked() != should:
                        child.blockSignals(True)
                        child.setChecked(should)
                        child.blockSignals(False)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _reevaluate_visibility(self) -> None:
        for key, spec in self._field_specs.items():
            widget = self._field_widgets.get(key)
            if widget is None:
                continue
            # Fields hidden by `visible: false` never receive a form row
            # and stay hidden regardless of `visible_when`.  A change in
            # `visible` triggers a full rebuild (structure hash covers
            # it), not an in-place visibility flip; so the only job here
            # is to make sure nothing else un-hides them.
            if spec.get("visible") is False:
                widget.setVisible(False)
                continue
            rule = spec.get("visible_when")
            if not rule:
                widget.setVisible(True)
                continue
            visible = True
            for other_key, expected in rule.items():
                other_spec = self._field_specs.get(other_key)
                other_widget = self._field_widgets.get(other_key)
                if other_spec is None or other_widget is None:
                    continue
                val = self._read_widget_value(other_spec, other_widget)
                if str(val) != str(expected):
                    visible = False
                    break
            widget.setVisible(visible)

    def set_action_enabled(self, key: str, enabled: bool) -> None:
        btn = self._action_buttons.get(key)
        if btn is not None:
            btn.setEnabled(bool(enabled))

    # ---- layer list ----

    def set_layers(self, layers: dict) -> None:
        image_list = layers.get("image") or []
        mask_list = layers.get("mask") or []
        recent = layers.get("recent") or []

        for key, widget in self._field_widgets.items():
            if not isinstance(widget, _LayerComboBox):
                continue
            spec = self._field_specs.get(key) or {}
            hint = spec.get("kind_hint")
            if hint == "image":
                widget.apply_layers(image_list, recent)
            elif hint == "mask":
                widget.apply_layers(mask_list, recent)

```python
"""Supervisor for the comfy-api-proxy child process.

The proxy is a separate aiohttp service that puts the Comfy API v2 in
front of ComfyUI. The daemon never imports it; it spawns it in a
dedicated venv and talks to it over HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8189.

Why a dedicated venv
====================
The proxy depends on aiohttp, pydantic, blake3, and PyYAML — heavyweight
packages orthogonal to Krita's runtime. Krita's bundled Python is
fragile; installing them there risks breaking Krita on a version
conflict. A venv also isolates the proxy's upgrade cycle from the
daemon's, and lets `install()` pick a Python 3.10+ from PATH rather
than whatever Krita ships (which is often older).

Layout
======
    ~/.local/share/kritomatic/comfy-api-proxy/       # or %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows
    ├── venv/                # dedicated Python env
    ├── pid.json             # {pid, host, port, comfyui}
    └── proxy.log            # stdout + stderr of the child

Lifecycle
=========
    install(force)        one-time venv creation + pip install (slow, ~30s)
    install_async(force)  kick off install() on a background thread and
                          return immediately; status() reports progress
    start(...)            spawn the child detached (survives daemon restart),
                          wait for /api/v2/health, write pid.json
    stop()                SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL if needed, clear pid.json
    status()              read pid.json, verify PID is ours, health-probe,
                          report install progress; always returns the
                          {success, message, data} envelope
    logs(n)               tail proxy.log
    uninstall()           stop + remove venv

The child runs with start_new_session=True (POSIX) or
DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP (Windows) so it is not killed
when the daemon's parent thread exits. On daemon restart, status()
re-discovers a still-running proxy via pid.json.

Concurrent start() calls
========================
`start()` performs a check-then-spawn sequence:

    status()       → not running
    _port_open()   → False
    Popen(...)     → spawn
    write pid.json

Two threads (e.g. two concurrent `comfy_panel_run` calls, each of
which calls `comfy_connect`, each of which calls `start()`) can race
the check. Without a lock, both can pass both checks and both spawn
a child. The second child's bind() fails, and one of the two
`start()` calls returns `{"success": False, "message": "port already
in use"}` — surfacing as an apparently-random "connect failed" on a
user's second Run click, even though the proxy is healthy.

`_START_LOCK` serializes the whole sequence. It is a module-level
lock; the venv directory on disk is the shared state it protects, and
that state is process-global within a single daemon, so a module
lock is the right scope. The second caller wakes to find `status()`
reporting the child that the first caller spawned; it short-circuits
at the `existing running` branch and returns cleanly.

The lock is *not* held during the health-probe wait (`_wait_health`
polling for up to 15 s). Holding it there would block every other
`comfy_connect` for the duration of the probe, which is worse than
the race it prevents. The check-then-spawn window is what matters:
it is tens of microseconds between `_port_open` and `Popen`, and it
is inside the lock.

Async install
=============
`install()` takes ~30s (venv + pip). The CLI's command transport has a
~2s read timeout. Blocking the call would cause the client to time out
on a call that actually succeeds server-side, leaving the operator with
no visibility into whether it worked. `install_async()` runs the same
work on a background thread, returns immediately, and lets the caller
poll `status()` for the real outcome. State is module-level: a second
`install_async()` while one is running returns "installing" without
spawning a duplicate thread.

Zero external dependencies: only stdlib (`urllib.request`, `socket`,
`subprocess`, `signal`, `threading`). The manager is importable outside
Krita.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Start-race lock (see module docstring)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_START_LOCK = threading.Lock()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Install state (module-level)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# `comfy_proxy_install` runs the slow venv+pip dance on a background
# thread (see `install_async` below); `status()` reports this so the CLI
# can poll it without ever blocking for 30s on a 2s transport read
# timeout.

_INSTALL_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_INSTALL_STATE: dict[str, Any] = {
    "state": "idle",       # idle | installing | done | error
    "message": "",
    "data": None,
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Paths
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PROXY_PKG_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
_PINNED_VERSION_FILE = _PROXY_PKG_DIR / "PINNED_VERSION"


def _data_root() -> Path:
    """Per-user data directory for the proxy venv + state.

    Deliberately NOT Qt's QStandardPaths (which resolves to Krita's own
    data dir when imported inside Krita). We want an independent dir
    that any Python on the machine can find, so manager.py stays
    importable outside Krita for testing.
    """
    if os.name == "nt":
        base = Path(os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA")
                    or (Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local"))
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME")
                    or (Path.home() / ".local" / "share"))
    return base / "kritomatic" / "comfy-api-proxy"


def _venv_dir() -> Path:
    return _data_root() / "venv"


def _venv_python() -> Path:
    if os.name == "nt":
        return _venv_dir() / "Scripts" / "python.exe"
    return _venv_dir() / "bin" / "python"


def _venv_pip() -> Path:
    if os.name == "nt":
        return _venv_dir() / "Scripts" / "pip.exe"
    return _venv_dir() / "bin" / "pip"


def _proxy_bin() -> Path:
    if os.name == "nt":
        return _venv_dir() / "Scripts" / "comfy-api-proxy.exe"
    return _venv_dir() / "bin" / "comfy-api-proxy"


def _pid_file() -> Path:
    return _data_root() / "pid.json"


def _log_file() -> Path:
    return _data_root() / "proxy.log"


def pinned_version() -> str:
    try:
        return _PINNED_VERSION_FILE.read_text().strip()
    except OSError:
        return "0.1.0"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Health probe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _health_url(host: str, port: int) -> str:
    if ":" in host:  # IPv6 literal
        return f"http://[{host}]:{port}/api/v2/health"
    return f"http://{host}:{port}/api/v2/health"


def _health_ok(host: str, port: int, timeout: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(_health_url(host, port),
                                    timeout=timeout) as r:
            return r.status == 200
    except (urllib.error.URLError, socket.timeout, ConnectionError, OSError):
        return False


def _port_open(host: str, port: int, timeout: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    try:
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
            return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def _wait_health(host: str, port: int, proc: subprocess.Popen,
                 timeout: float = 15.0) -> bool:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            return False  # child exited before binding
        if _health_ok(host, port, timeout=1.0):
            return True
        time.sleep(0.2)
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  PID identity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
    if pid <= 0:
        return False
    try:
        os.kill(pid, 0)
        return True
    except ProcessLookupError:
        return False
    except PermissionError:
        return True  # exists, owned by another user
    except OSError:
        return False


def _pid_cmdline(pid: int) -> str | None:
    """Best-effort command line of a PID, or None where it can't be read."""
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            out = subprocess.run(
                ["wmic", "process", "where", f"ProcessId={pid}",
                 "get", "CommandLine"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
            )
        else:
            out = subprocess.run(
                ["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "args="],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
            )
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return out.stdout.strip() or None


def _pid_is_ours(pid: int) -> bool:
    """Is `pid` alive AND (best-effort) actually our proxy — not a recycled PID?

    Falls back to a plain liveness check when the command line can't be
    inspected, so behaviour is never worse than tracking the PID alone.
    """
    if not _pid_alive(pid):
        return False
    cmdline = _pid_cmdline(pid)
    if cmdline is None:
        return True
    return "comfy-api-proxy" in cmdline


def _terminate(pid: int) -> None:
    if os.name == "nt":
        subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(pid), "/T", "/F"],
                       capture_output=True, timeout=10)
        return
    try:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        return
    for _ in range(50):
        if not _pid_alive(pid):
            return
        time.sleep(0.1)
    try:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Python discovery for install()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _find_python_310() -> str | None:
    """Find a Python 3.10+ interpreter to build the venv from.

    Krita's bundled Python is frequently 3.8 or 3.9 — the proxy requires
    3.10+. Prefer a system Python if one is on PATH; fall back to
    sys.executable (Krita's) only if no newer interpreter is found,
    because a 3.9 venv cannot install the proxy.
    """
    for name in ("python3.12", "python3.11", "python3.10", "python3"):
        path = shutil.which(name)
        if not path:
            continue
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(
                [path, "-c",
                 "import sys; print(sys.version_info >= (3, 10))"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
            )
            if r.stdout.strip() == "True":
                return path
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            continue
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  install
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def install(force: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Create the venv and pip-install the pinned proxy version.

    Idempotent: returns `already installed` when the binary exists and
    `force` is False. Slow on first run (~30s for venv + pip).

    Prefer `install_async()` from a command handler: this synchronous
    form blocks for the full ~30s and will time out the CLI's transport.
    """
    if _proxy_bin().exists() and not force:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"already installed at {_proxy_bin()}",
            "data": {"path": str(_proxy_bin()),
                     "version": pinned_version()},
        }

    python = _find_python_310()
    if python is None:
        return {
            "success": False,
            "message": (
                "No Python 3.10+ found on PATH. The comfy-api-proxy "
                "requires Python 3.10 or newer. Install one "
                "(e.g. `sudo apt install python3.11`) and retry, or "
                "install the proxy manually: "
                "`pipx install comfy-api-proxy==" + pinned_version() + "`, "
                "then run `comfy_proxy_start` — the manager will find "
                "the pipx-installed binary on PATH."
            ),
        }

    _data_root().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [python, "-m", "venv", str(_venv_dir())],
            check=True, timeout=180,
            capture_output=True,
        )
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        return {"success": False,
                "message": f"venv creation failed: {e.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[:300]}"}
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"success": False, "message": "venv creation timed out (180s)"}
    except OSError as e:
        return {"success": False, "message": f"venv creation failed: {e}"}

    version = pinned_version()
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [str(_venv_pip()), "install", f"comfy-api-proxy=={version}"],
            check=True, timeout=600,
            capture_output=True,
        )
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        return {"success": False,
                "message": f"pip install failed: {e.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[:500]}"}
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"success": False, "message": "pip install timed out (600s)"}
    except OSError as e:
        return {"success": False, "message": f"pip install failed: {e}"}

    if not _proxy_bin().exists():
        return {"success": False,
                "message": f"pip finished but {_proxy_bin()} is missing"}

    return {
        "success": True,
        "message": f"installed comfy-api-proxy {version} at {_proxy_bin()}",
        "data": {"path": str(_proxy_bin()), "version": version},
    }


def install_async(force: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Kick off `install()` on a background thread and return immediately.

    The CLI's command transport has a short read timeout (~2s), but
    venv creation + pip install take ~30s. Rather than blocking the
    call (and having the client time out on a call that actually
    succeeds server-side), start the install in a thread, return
    `state: "installing"`, and let the caller poll `status()` for the
    real result.

    Idempotent: a call while an install is already running returns
    `state: "installing"` without spawning a second thread. A call
    after a successful install returns `state: "done"` with the
    cached result. `force=True` re-runs even after `state: "done"`.
    """
    with _INSTALL_LOCK:
        current = _INSTALL_STATE["state"]
        if current == "installing":
            return {
                "success": True,
                "message": "install already in progress",
                "data": {"state": "installing"},
            }
        if current == "done" and not force:
            return {
                "success": True,
                "message": "already installed",
                "data": dict(_INSTALL_STATE["data"] or {}),
            }
        _INSTALL_STATE["state"] = "installing"
        _INSTALL_STATE["message"] = "creating venv and pip-installing..."
        _INSTALL_STATE["data"] = None

    def _run() -> None:
        try:
            result = install(force=force)
            with _INSTALL_LOCK:
                _INSTALL_STATE["state"] = (
                    "done" if result.get("success") else "error"
                )
                _INSTALL_STATE["message"] = result.get("message", "")
                _INSTALL_STATE["data"] = result.get("data")
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — surface anything as install error
            with _INSTALL_LOCK:
                _INSTALL_STATE["state"] = "error"
                _INSTALL_STATE["message"] = f"install raised: {e}"
                _INSTALL_STATE["data"] = None

    threading.Thread(
        target=_run, name="comfy-proxy-install", daemon=True,
    ).start()

    return {
        "success": True,
        "message": "install started in background; poll comfy_proxy_status",
        "data": {"state": "installing"},
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  start / stop / status / logs / uninstall
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _read_pid_file() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    path = _pid_file()
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (ValueError, OSError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or int(data.get("pid", -1)) <= 0:
        return None
    return data


def status() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Report whether the proxy is running and healthy, plus install state.

    Returns the standard `{success, message, data}` envelope so the
    daemon's base handler wraps it correctly (a bare dict without
    `success`/`message`/`data` would be reported as
    `{"status": "error", "data": null}` by the caller).

    The `data` block always carries an `install` snapshot plus the
    runtime fields — a caller can distinguish "still installing" from
    "installed but not running" from "running and healthy" without
    extra state.

    `running` = PID file present AND PID is ours. `healthy` = the
    proxy answers /api/v2/health. Both must be True for the daemon to
    route generation through the proxy.
    """
    with _INSTALL_LOCK:
        raw_data = _INSTALL_STATE["data"]
        install_snapshot = {
            "state": _INSTALL_STATE["state"],
            "message": _INSTALL_STATE["message"],
            # Copy the dict so a caller can't mutate module state.
            "data": dict(raw_data) if isinstance(raw_data, dict) else raw_data,
        }

    state = _read_pid_file()
    if state is None:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": "not running",
            "data": {
                "install": install_snapshot,
                "running": False,
                "healthy": False,
            },
        }
    pid = int(state["pid"])
    if not _pid_is_ours(pid):
        # Stale PID file: process is gone or the PID has been recycled.
        # Clear it so the next status() doesn't report a phantom.
        try:
            _pid_file().unlink()
        except OSError:
            pass
        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"not running (cleared stale pid {pid})",
            "data": {
                "install": install_snapshot,
                "running": False,
                "healthy": False,
                "cleared_stale_pid": pid,
            },
        }
    host = state.get("host", "127.0.0.1")
    port = int(state.get("port", 8189))
    healthy = _health_ok(host, port, timeout=0.5)
    return {
        "success": True,
        "message": "running" if healthy else "running (unhealthy)",
        "data": {
            "install": install_snapshot,
            "running": True,
            "healthy": healthy,
            "pid": pid,
            "host": host,
            "port": port,
            "comfyui": state.get("comfyui"),
        },
    }


def start(*,
          host: str = "127.0.0.1",
          port: int = 8189,
          comfyui: str = "http://127.0.0.1:8188",
          comfyui_base_dir: str | None = None,
          token: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Spawn the proxy detached and wait for /api/v2/health.

    Idempotent when an existing proxy already points at the same
    ComfyUI. Errors when one points elsewhere (stop it first), or when
    the port is already taken by another process.

    The check-then-spawn sequence runs under `_START_LOCK` so two
    concurrent `comfy_connect` calls (e.g. from two concurrently-firing
    `comfy_panel_run` runs) cannot both decide "not running" and both
    spawn a child. See the module docstring, "Concurrent start() calls".
    """
    with _START_LOCK:
        existing = status()
        existing_data = existing.get("data") or {}
        if existing_data.get("running"):
            existing_comfyui = existing_data.get("comfyui")
            if existing_comfyui and existing_comfyui != comfyui:
                return {
                    "success": False,
                    "message": (
                        f"proxy already running (pid {existing_data['pid']}) "
                        f"pointed at {existing_comfyui}, not {comfyui}. "
                        f"Run `comfy_proxy_stop` first."
                    ),
                    "data": existing_data,
                }
            return {
                "success": True,
                "message": f"already running (pid {existing_data['pid']})",
                "data": existing_data,
            }

        binary: str | None = None
        if _proxy_bin().exists():
            binary = str(_proxy_bin())
        else:
            on_path = shutil.which("comfy-api-proxy")
            if on_path:
                binary = on_path
        if binary is None:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "message": (
                    "comfy-api-proxy is not installed. Run "
                    "`comfy_proxy_install` first, or install it manually "
                    "with `pipx install comfy-api-proxy`."
                ),
            }

        if _port_open(host, port):
            return {
                "success": False,
                "message": f"port {port} on {host} is already in use",
            }

        argv = [binary, "run", "--comfyui", comfyui,
                "--host", host, "--port", str(port)]
        if comfyui_base_dir:
            argv += ["--comfyui-base-dir", comfyui_base_dir]
        if token:
            argv += ["--token", token]

        _data_root().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _log_file().touch(exist_ok=True)
        log_handle = _log_file().open("ab")
        popen_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "stdin": subprocess.DEVNULL,
            "stdout": log_handle,
            "stderr": log_handle,
        }
        if os.name == "nt":
            popen_kwargs["creationflags"] = 0x00000008 | 0x00000200  # DETACHED | NEW_GROUP
        else:
            popen_kwargs["start_new_session"] = True

        try:
            proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, **popen_kwargs)
        except OSError as e:
            log_handle.close()
            return {"success": False, "message": f"failed to spawn proxy: {e}"}
        finally:
            log_handle.close()

        # Health probe runs *outside* the lock; blocking every other
        # comfy_connect for the full ~15 s probe would be worse than
        # the race it prevents. The check-then-spawn window (below
        # `_port_open` and above `Popen`) is the part that matters,
        # and that is inside the lock.
        if not _wait_health(host, port, proc, timeout=15.0):
            _terminate(proc.pid)
            return {
                "success": False,
                "message": f"proxy failed to become healthy; see {_log_file()}",
                "data": {"pid": proc.pid, "log": str(_log_file())},
            }

        _pid_file().write_text(json.dumps({
            "pid": proc.pid,
            "host": host,
            "port": port,
            "comfyui": comfyui,
        }))

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"started on {host}:{port} (pid {proc.pid})",
            "data": {
                "pid": proc.pid,
                "host": host,
                "port": port,
                "comfyui": comfyui,
            },
        }


def stop() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Stop the proxy and clear the PID file. Idempotent."""
    state = _read_pid_file()
    if state is None:
        return {"success": True, "message": "not running",
                "data": {"running": False}}
    pid = int(state["pid"])
    if not _pid_is_ours(pid):
        try:
            _pid_file().unlink()
        except OSError:
            pass
        return {"success": True,
                "message": f"pid {pid} is gone or recycled; cleared",
                "data": {"cleared_stale_pid": pid}}
    _terminate(pid)
    try:
        _pid_file().unlink()
    except OSError:
        pass
    return {"success": True, "message": f"stopped (pid {pid})",
            "data": {"pid": pid}}


def logs(lines: int = 100) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the last `lines` lines of the proxy log."""
    path = _log_file()
    if not path.exists():
        return {"success": True, "message": "no log yet",
                "data": {"lines": []}}
    try:
        with path.open("r", errors="replace") as f:
            all_lines = f.readlines()
    except OSError as e:
        return {"success": False, "message": f"could not read log: {e}",
                "data": {"lines": []}}
    take = max(1, min(lines, 5000))
    tail = all_lines[-take:]
    return {
        "success": True,
        "message": f"{len(tail)} line(s) of {len(all_lines)}",
        "data": {"lines": [ln.rstrip("\n") for ln in tail]},
    }


def uninstall() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Stop the proxy (if running) and remove its venv."""
    stop()
    with _INSTALL_LOCK:
        _INSTALL_STATE["state"] = "idle"
        _INSTALL_STATE["message"] = ""
        _INSTALL_STATE["data"] = None
    if _venv_dir().exists():
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(_venv_dir())
        except OSError as e:
            return {"success": False,
                    "message": f"could not remove venv: {e}",
                    "data": {"running": False}}
    return {"success": True, "message": "uninstalled",
            "data": {"running": False}}

```python
"""
event_bus.py — a process-wide pub/sub bus for daemon state events.

Any part of the daemon can publish to the bus; any part can subscribe.
Two subscription styles:

  * Queue-based subscriptions (`subscribe`/`unsubscribe`) are used by
    the event server, which needs to block in `select` on a signal
    socket and drain per-subscriber queues at its own pace.

  * Listener callbacks (`add_listener`/`remove_listener`) are used by
    in-process consumers — the panel handler — that want each event
    delivered as a function call. Callbacks are invoked synchronously
    on the publishing thread and must not block.

Publishing is fire-and-forget for the queue subscribers: a slow
subscriber cannot block the publisher, because publishes go through
per-subscriber queues and a full queue is drained rather than blocking.

Delivery guarantees:

  * Queue subscribers: at most one copy per subscriber per publish.
    If the queue is full, the oldest pending event is dropped to make
    room for the newest. State events are idempotent, so this is the
    right trade-off.

  * Listener callbacks: exactly once per publish, called in registration
    order. Exceptions from a listener are swallowed so one broken
    consumer cannot break the publish path for the others.

Thread-safe. Publishing from any thread is fine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import queue
import socket
import threading
from typing import Any, Callable


class Subscription:
    """One queue subscriber's channel: a bounded queue of events, plus
    a socketpair whose read end becomes readable whenever the queue is
    non-empty.
    """

    def __init__(self, queue_size: int):
        self.queue: queue.Queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=queue_size)
        r, w = socket.socketpair()
        r.setblocking(False)
        w.setblocking(False)
        self.signal_r: socket.socket = r
        self.signal_w: socket.socket = w

    def drain_signal(self) -> None:
        while True:
            try:
                chunk = self.signal_r.recv(65536)
            except (BlockingIOError, InterruptedError):
                return
            except OSError:
                return
            if not chunk:
                return

    def close(self) -> None:
        for s in (self.signal_r, self.signal_w):
            try:
                s.close()
            except OSError:
                pass


Listener = Callable[[str, Any], None]


class EventBus:
    """Pub/sub bus for in-process state events."""

    DEFAULT_QUEUE_SIZE = 256

    def __init__(self, queue_size: int = DEFAULT_QUEUE_SIZE):
        self._queue_size = queue_size
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._subscribers: list = []
        self._listeners: list = []

    # -- queue subscribers --

    def subscribe(self) -> Subscription:
        sub = Subscription(self._queue_size)
        with self._lock:
            self._subscribers.append(sub)
        return sub

    def unsubscribe(self, sub: Subscription) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if sub in self._subscribers:
                self._subscribers.remove(sub)
        try:
            sub.signal_w.close()
        except OSError:
            pass

    # -- listener callbacks --

    def add_listener(self, callback: Listener) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if callback not in self._listeners:
                self._listeners.append(callback)

    def remove_listener(self, callback: Listener) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if callback in self._listeners:
                self._listeners.remove(callback)

    def clear_listeners(self) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._listeners = []

    # -- publishing --

    def publish(self, event_type: str, data: Any) -> None:
        event = {"type": event_type, "data": data}

        with self._lock:
            subs = list(self._subscribers)
            listeners = list(self._listeners)

        for sub in subs:
            try:
                sub.queue.put_nowait(event)
            except queue.Full:
                try:
                    sub.queue.get_nowait()
                except queue.Empty:
                    pass
                try:
                    sub.queue.put_nowait(event)
                except queue.Full:
                    pass
            try:
                sub.signal_w.send(b"\x01")
            except (BlockingIOError, InterruptedError):
                pass
            except OSError:
                pass

        for cb in listeners:
            try:
                cb(event_type, data)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def subscriber_count(self) -> int:
        with self._lock:
            return len(self._subscribers)


_bus = EventBus()


def get_event_bus() -> EventBus:
    return _bus
