```python
"""Panel button handlers, pgkit registrations, state sync.

The state-sync path: any change to areas or globals calls
`_scheduleStateSync()`, which debounces and POSTs the full state +
mask b64s to `/state`.  The node fetches `/state` on every execute;
`/version` is cheap for IS_CHANGED.

`Export graph JSON` downloads the API-format graph the node would
build from the current state (works with ComfyUI closed).

`Fetch last run` asks the server to GET ComfyUI's native `/history`
for the most recent run.  The returned JSON is the *submitted*
graph, not the expanded one; the diagnostic summary explains this.

The displayed image is whatever the user picked or imported — no
auto-refresh after generation.  Use `+ From Krita` to pull the
current composite into the canvas.

`Refresh @thecanvas` re-fetches the current `@thecanvas` on demand.
The autosync poller (`pg_autosync.js`) only reacts to *spec* changes
(`active` → `layer X`, `layer X` → `layer Y`), not to pixels behind
a constant spec, so a paint layer whose content was edited in Krita
keeps showing the old pixels until something else triggers a poll.
The button bypasses that gate.  `applyCanvasImage` is used (not
`setImage`), so the area list survives the refresh — same semantics
as the autosync path.

`Clear all areas` empties the area list (masks + prompts) without
touching the loaded image.  This is the counterpart of `Clear image`
which resets both.  The action flows through the same debounced
state sync as every other area mutation, so the daemon's saved
`/state` becomes empty and the `MultiAreaConditioning` node passes
`base_positive` through unchanged on the next execute.

KRITA STATUS MIRRORING
======================
`#kritaStatus` is a persistent panel element like inpaint's:
"✓ reachable" / "✗ not reachable".  The ✗ branch mirrors its reason
to `console.error`, which pgkit/panel_core.js routes to POST
./__log.  The persistent DOM write stays visible on the panel; the
terminal write is the durable record.
"""

PANEL_BINDINGS_JS = r"""
import {
  board, setImage, clearImage, applyCanvasImage,
} from "./pg_state.js";
import {
  addAreaFromB64, removeArea, selectArea, areaById,
} from "./pg_areas.js";
import { syncAreaList, setStateChangeHook } from "./pg_panel_lists.js";
import { syncPanelFields } from "./pg_panel_fields.js";
import {
  importFromKrita, importKritaMasks, uploadImageFile,
  checkKritaStatus, fetchActiveState, fetchResourceImage,
} from "./pg_client.js";
import {
  pgkitRegisterAction, pgkitRegisterLevel, pgkitRegisterField,
} from "./pgkit/remote_client.js";
import { flashStatus } from "./pgkit/panel_core.js";

/* ============================================================
   State sync (debounced POST to /state)
   ============================================================ */

let _syncTimer = null;

function _maskHash(mask) {
  if (mask._hash) return mask._hash;
  let h = 2166136261 >>> 0;
  const s = mask.b64 || "";
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    h ^= s.charCodeAt(i);
    h = Math.imul(h, 16777619) >>> 0;
  }
  mask._hash = s.length.toString(16) + "-" + h.toString(16);
  return mask._hash;
}

function _buildStatePayload() {
  const areas = board.areas.map(a => ({
    id: a.id, name: a.name,
    prompt: a.prompt, use_tagger: !!a.useTagger,
    strength:              a.strength,
    set_cond_area:         a.set_cond_area,
    mask_channel:          a.mask_channel,
    bbox:                  a.bbox,
    resize:                a.resize,
    tagger_mode:           a.tagger_mode,
    tagger_model:          a.tagger_model,
    tagger_threshold:      a.tagger_threshold,
    tagger_char_threshold: a.tagger_char_threshold,
    mask: {
      hash:   _maskHash(a.mask),
      width:  a.mask.w,
      height: a.mask.h,
    },
  }));
  const masks = {};
  for (const a of board.areas) {
    if (a.mask && a.mask.b64) masks[_maskHash(a.mask)] = a.mask.b64;
  }
  return {
    op: "set",
    state: { globals: { ...board.globals }, areas },
    masks,
  };
}

export function _scheduleStateSync() {
  if (_syncTimer) clearTimeout(_syncTimer);
  _syncTimer = setTimeout(_doStateSync, 250);
}

async function _doStateSync() {
  _syncTimer = null;
  try {
    const res = await fetch("/state", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(_buildStatePayload()),
    });
    const payload = await res.json();
    if (payload.success) {
      const v = (payload.version || "").slice(0, 8);
      const el = document.getElementById("stateVersion");
      if (el) el.textContent = v || "—";
      const st = document.getElementById("statusLine");
      if (st) {
        st.textContent = "synced \u00b7 v" + v;
        st.className = "ok";
      }
    }
  } catch (e) {
    const st = document.getElementById("statusLine");
    if (st) {
      st.textContent = "sync failed: " + e.message;
      st.className = "bad";
    }
    // Mirror the failure to the terminal — the persistent
    // #statusLine write above shows it in the panel; console.error
    // routes it through pgkit/panel_core.js's mirror.
    try { console.error("[multimask] state sync:", e.message); } catch (_) {}
  }
}

setStateChangeHook(_scheduleStateSync);

/* ============================================================
   Image actions
   ============================================================ */

function _fileToDataUrl(file) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => resolve(String(reader.result || ""));
    reader.onerror = () => reject(new Error("could not read file"));
    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
  });
}

async function _installImage(file) {
  flashStatus("uploading " + file.name + "\u2026", "");
  try {
    const info = await uploadImageFile(file);
    const dataUrl = await _fileToDataUrl(file);
    setImage(info.hash, dataUrl, info.width, info.height);
    flashStatus("image loaded", "ok");
    syncPanelFields();
    syncAreaList();
    _scheduleStateSync();
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("upload failed: " + e.message, "bad");
  }
}

function _pickImageAction() {
  const input = document.createElement("input");
  input.type = "file";
  input.accept = "image/*";
  input.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const file = input.files && input.files[0];
    if (file) _installImage(file);
  });
  input.click();
}

function _clearImageAction() {
  clearImage();
  syncPanelFields();
  syncAreaList();
  _scheduleStateSync();
  import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
}

async function _importImageFromKritaAction() {
  flashStatus("importing image from Krita\u2026", "");
  try {
    const res = await importFromKrita({});
    if (!res.success) {
      flashStatus("import failed: " + (res.message || "unknown"), "bad");
      return;
    }
    setImage(res.hash, res.data_url, res.width, res.height);
    flashStatus("imported " + res.width + "\u00d7" + res.height, "ok");
    syncPanelFields();
    syncAreaList();
    _scheduleStateSync();
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("import failed: " + e.message, "bad");
  }
}

/* ============================================================
   Manual @thecanvas refresh
   ============================================================
   The autosync poller reacts only to changes in the @thecanvas
   *spec* — `active` → `layer X`, `layer X` → `layer Y`.  A paint
   layer whose content was edited in Krita keeps the same spec, so
   the poller does not fire and the playground keeps showing the
   old pixels.  This button bypasses the spec-change gate: read the
   current spec, resolve it to pixels, applyCanvasImage.

   `applyCanvasImage` preserves the area list (and invalidates each
   mask's pixel caches so the tinted overlays rebuild).  If the new
   image's dimensions differ from the old, a console warning is
   emitted because the area masks are unlikely to line up — the
   user can re-import them if needed. */

async function _refreshCanvasAction() {
  flashStatus("refreshing @thecanvas\u2026", "");
  let state;
  try {
    state = await fetchActiveState();
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("@thecanvas refresh failed: " + e.message, "bad");
    return;
  }
  if (!state || !state.success) {
    flashStatus(
      "@thecanvas refresh failed: "
        + ((state && state.message) || "no active state"),
      "bad",
    );
    return;
  }
  const cfg = (state.data && state.data.config) || null;
  const res = (cfg && cfg.resources) || {};
  const spec = res["@thecanvas"];
  if (!spec || typeof spec !== "object") {
    flashStatus("@thecanvas not set in daemon config", "warn");
    return;
  }
  const normalized = {
    source: spec.source || "active",
    layer_name: spec.layer_name || null,
  };

  let img;
  try {
    img = await fetchResourceImage(normalized);
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("@thecanvas refresh failed: " + e.message, "bad");
    return;
  }
  if (!img || !img.success) {
    flashStatus(
      "@thecanvas refresh failed: "
        + ((img && img.message) || "unknown"),
      "bad",
    );
    return;
  }
  if (!img.data_url) {
    flashStatus("@thecanvas refresh: no data_url", "bad");
    return;
  }

  applyCanvasImage(
    img.hash || ("thecanvas_" + Date.now()),
    img.data_url,
    img.width,
    img.height,
  );
  const label = normalized.source === "layer"
    ? normalized.layer_name
    : normalized.source;
  flashStatus("@thecanvas \u2192 " + label, "ok");

  syncPanelFields();
  syncAreaList();
  import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
}

/* ============================================================
   Area actions
   ============================================================ */

function _slugName(s) {
  const slug = String(s || "").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_]/g, "_").slice(0, 40);
  return slug || undefined;
}

async function _importMasksFromKritaAction() {
  if (!board.imageHash) {
    flashStatus("import an image from Krita first", "warn");
    return;
  }
  flashStatus("importing masks from Krita\u2026", "");
  try {
    const res = await importKritaMasks({});
    if (!res.success) {
      flashStatus("import failed: " + (res.message || "unknown"), "bad");
      return;
    }
    const masks = res.masks || [];
    if (masks.length === 0) {
      const skipped = res.skipped || [];
      const why = skipped.length
        ? " (" + skipped.map(s => s.name + ": " + s.reason).join("; ") + ")"
        : "";
      flashStatus("no masks imported" + why, "warn");
      return;
    }
    for (const m of masks) {
      addAreaFromB64(m.mask_b64, {
        name: _slugName(m.name),
        prompt: "",
      });
    }
    syncPanelFields();
    syncAreaList();
    _scheduleStateSync();
    flashStatus("imported " + masks.length + " area(s)", "ok");
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("import failed: " + e.message, "bad");
  }
}

function _addBlankAreaAction() {
  if (!board.imageWidth || !board.imageHeight) {
    flashStatus("load an image first", "warn");
    return;
  }
  const W = board.imageWidth, H = board.imageHeight;
  const c = document.createElement("canvas");
  c.width = W; c.height = H;
  const cx = c.getContext("2d");
  cx.fillStyle = "#fff";
  cx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  const b64 = c.toDataURL("image/png")
               .replace(/^data:image\/png;base64,/, "");
  addAreaFromB64(b64, { prompt: "" });
  syncPanelFields();
  syncAreaList();
  _scheduleStateSync();
  flashStatus("added blank area", "ok");
  import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
}

/* Empty the area list (masks + prompts) without touching the image.
 * Counterpart to `Clear image`, which resets both.  Kept as its own
 * action so a user who only wants to start over on masks can keep
 * the imported composite in place and re-import masks against it.
 *
 * Every mutation goes through the same debounced state sync the
 * other area operations use, so the daemon's saved state becomes
 * empty and the next `MultiAreaConditioning` execute passes
 * `base_positive` through — matching a running playground with zero
 * areas. */
function _clearAreasAction() {
  const n = board.areas.length;
  if (n === 0) {
    flashStatus("no areas to clear", "warn");
    return;
  }
  board.areas          = [];
  board.selectedAreaId = null;
  board.hoveredAreaId  = null;
  board.nextAreaNum    = 1;
  syncPanelFields();
  syncAreaList();
  _scheduleStateSync();
  flashStatus("cleared " + n + " area(s)", "ok");
  import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
}

function _deleteAreaAction(payload) {
  const n = payload?.target?.name;
  if (typeof n !== "string" || !n.startsWith("area.")) return;
  const id = n.slice(5);
  if (!areaById(id)) return;
  removeArea(id);
  syncAreaList();
  _scheduleStateSync();
  import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
}

/* ============================================================
   Krita status
   ============================================================ */

async function _kritaStatusAction() {
  const res = await checkKritaStatus();
  const el = document.getElementById("kritaStatus");
  if (!el) return;
  if (res.reachable) {
    el.textContent = "\u2713 reachable";
    el.className = "ok";
    el.title = "Kritomatic daemon at localhost:12346";
  } else {
    el.textContent = "\u2717 not reachable";
    el.className = "bad";
    el.title = "Start Krita with the Kritomatic Daemon plugin enabled";
    // Mirror the reason to the terminal.  #kritaStatus is the
    // panel's persistent indicator; console.error routes through
    // pgkit/panel_core.js's mirror to the terminal.
    try {
      console.error("[multimask] krita:", res.message || "not reachable");
    } catch (_) {}
  }
}

/* ============================================================
   Save / Load
   ============================================================ */

function _saveStateAction() {
  const payload = _buildStatePayload();
  const out = {
    globals: payload.state.globals,
    areas: payload.state.areas.map(a => {
      const area = areaById(a.id);
      return { ...a, mask_b64: area.mask.b64 };
    }),
  };
  const text = JSON.stringify(out, null, 2);
  const url = "data:application/json;charset=utf-8," + encodeURIComponent(text);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = "multimask_state.json";
  a.style.display = "none";
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  document.body.removeChild(a);
  flashStatus("saved state", "ok");
}

function _loadStateAction() {
  const input = document.createElement("input");
  input.type = "file";
  input.accept = "application/json,.json";
  input.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const file = input.files && input.files[0];
    if (!file) return;
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => {
      try {
        const data = JSON.parse(String(reader.result || ""));
        if (data.globals) Object.assign(board.globals, data.globals);
        if (Array.isArray(data.areas)) {
          board.areas = [];
          board.selectedAreaId = null;
          board.hoveredAreaId = null;
          board.nextAreaNum = 1;
          for (const a of data.areas) {
            if (!a.mask_b64) continue;
            addAreaFromB64(a.mask_b64, {
              name: a.name, prompt: a.prompt,
              useTagger: a.use_tagger,
              strength: a.strength,
              set_cond_area: a.set_cond_area,
              mask_channel: a.mask_channel,
              bbox: a.bbox, resize: a.resize,
              tagger_mode: a.tagger_mode,
              tagger_model: a.tagger_model,
              tagger_threshold: a.tagger_threshold,
              tagger_char_threshold: a.tagger_char_threshold,
            });
          }
        }
        syncPanelFields();
        syncAreaList();
        _scheduleStateSync();
        flashStatus("state loaded", "ok");
        import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
      } catch (e) {
        flashStatus("load failed: " + e.message, "bad");
      }
    };
    reader.readAsText(file);
  });
  input.click();
}

/* ============================================================

   ============================================================ */

async function _exportGraphAction() {
  try {
    const res = await fetch("/export_graph", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: "{}",
    });
    const payload = await res.json();
    if (!payload.success) {
      flashStatus("export failed: " + (payload.message || "unknown"), "bad");
      return;
    }
    const text = JSON.stringify(payload.graph, null, 2);
    const url  = "data:application/json;charset=utf-8,"
               + encodeURIComponent(text);
    const stamp = new Date().toISOString()
                  .replace(/[:.]/g, "-").slice(0, 19);
    const a = document.createElement("a");
    a.href = url;
    a.download = "multimask_graph_" + stamp + ".json";
    a.style.display = "none";
    document.body.appendChild(a);
    a.click();
    document.body.removeChild(a);

    const v = (payload.version || "").slice(0, 8);
    const fc = payload.final_conditioning || ["?", "?"];
    flashStatus(
      "exported " + Object.keys(payload.graph).length
      + " node(s) \u00b7 v" + v
      + " \u00b7 output " + fc[0] + "[" + fc[1] + "]",
      "ok",
    );
    if (payload.notes && payload.notes.length) {
      console.log("[multimask export]", payload.notes.join("\n"));
    }
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("export failed: " + e.message, "bad");
  }
}

/* ============================================================
   Fetch last run
   ============================================================ */

async function _fetchHistoryAction() {
  try {
    const res = await fetch("/fetch_history", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: "{}",
    });
    const payload = await res.json();
    if (!payload.success) {
      flashStatus("fetch failed: " + (payload.message || "unknown"), "bad");
      const infoEl = document.getElementById("lastRunInfo");
      if (infoEl) {
        infoEl.textContent = "fetch failed: " + (payload.message || "unknown");
        infoEl.className = "bad";
      }
      return;
    }

    const d = payload.diagnostic || {};
    const n  = d.submitted_node_count || 0;
    const clips = d.cliptexts || [];
    const hasMA = d.multi_area_node ? "present" : "absent";
    const stat  = d.status_str || "?";

    const out = {
      prompt_id:   payload.prompt_id,
      fetched_at:  new Date().toISOString(),
      comfy_url:   payload.comfy_url,
      diagnostic:  d,
      status:      payload.status,
      prompt:      payload.prompt,
      outputs:     payload.outputs,
      meta:        payload.meta,
    };
    const text = JSON.stringify(out, null, 2);
    const url  = "data:application/json;charset=utf-8,"
               + encodeURIComponent(text);
    const a = document.createElement("a");
    a.href = url;
    a.download = "last_run_" + String(payload.prompt_id).slice(0, 8) + ".json";
    a.style.display = "none";
    document.body.appendChild(a);
    a.click();
    document.body.removeChild(a);

    flashStatus(
      "fetched \u00b7 " + n + " node(s) \u00b7 "
      + clips.length + " CLIPTextEncode \u00b7 MultiArea: " + hasMA
      + " \u00b7 " + stat,
      "ok",
    );

    const infoEl = document.getElementById("lastRunInfo");
    if (infoEl) {
      const lines = [
        "Last run " + String(payload.prompt_id).slice(0, 8)
        + " \u00b7 " + n + " submitted nodes",
        "  CLIPTextEncode: " + clips.length
        + " \u00b7 MultiAreaConditioning: " + hasMA
        + " \u00b7 status: " + stat,
        "  outputs: " + ((d.output_node_ids || []).length || 0)
        + " node(s)",
      ];
      for (const ct of clips) {
        const t = (ct.text || "").slice(0, 120);
        lines.push("    [" + ct.node + "] " + t);
      }
      if (d.multi_area_node) {
        const mi = d.multi_area_node.inputs || {};
        const url0 = mi.playground_url ?? "(unset)";
        const filt = mi.area_filter   ?? "(unset)";
        lines.push("    MultiArea inputs: url=" + url0 + "  filter=" + filt);
      }
      lines.push("  note: /history shows the SUBMITTED graph, "
                 + "not the expanded one.");
      infoEl.textContent = lines.join("\n");
      infoEl.className = stat === "error" ? "bad" : "ok";
    }

    console.log("[multimask fetch_history] diagnostic:", d);
    for (const ct of clips) {
      console.log("  CLIPTextEncode", ct.node, ":", ct.text);
    }
    if (d.multi_area_node) {
      console.log("  MultiAreaConditioning inputs:",
                  d.multi_area_node.inputs);
    }
  } catch (e) {
    flashStatus("fetch failed: " + e.message, "bad");
  }
}

function _showDropOverlay(on) {
  const el = document.getElementById("dropOverlay");
  if (el) el.classList.toggle("visible", on);
}

function _installDropOverlay() {
  if (document.getElementById("dropOverlay")) return;
  const el = document.createElement("div");
  el.id = "dropOverlay";
  el.textContent = "Drop an image";
  document.body.appendChild(el);
}

export function installPanelBindings() {
  const el = {};
  for (const id of [
    "pickImageBtn", "clearImageBtn", "importImageBtn",
    "importMasksBtn", "blankAreaBtn", "clearAreasBtn", "kritaCheckBtn",
    "saveStateBtn", "loadStateBtn", "exportGraphBtn",
    "fetchHistoryBtn",
    "refreshCanvasBtn",
  ]) {
    el[id] = document.getElementById(id);
  }
  if (el.pickImageBtn)    el.pickImageBtn.addEventListener("click", _pickImageAction);
  if (el.clearImageBtn)   el.clearImageBtn.addEventListener("click", _clearImageAction);
  if (el.importImageBtn)  el.importImageBtn.addEventListener("click", _importImageFromKritaAction);
  if (el.importMasksBtn)  el.importMasksBtn.addEventListener("click", _importMasksFromKritaAction);
  if (el.blankAreaBtn)    el.blankAreaBtn.addEventListener("click", _addBlankAreaAction);
  if (el.clearAreasBtn)   el.clearAreasBtn.addEventListener("click", _clearAreasAction);
  if (el.kritaCheckBtn)   el.kritaCheckBtn.addEventListener("click", _kritaStatusAction);
  if (el.saveStateBtn)    el.saveStateBtn.addEventListener("click", _saveStateAction);
  if (el.loadStateBtn)    el.loadStateBtn.addEventListener("click", _loadStateAction);
  if (el.exportGraphBtn)  el.exportGraphBtn.addEventListener("click", _exportGraphAction);
  if (el.fetchHistoryBtn) el.fetchHistoryBtn.addEventListener("click", _fetchHistoryAction);
  if (el.refreshCanvasBtn) el.refreshCanvasBtn.addEventListener("click", _refreshCanvasAction);

  // Combine-mode select
  const cms = document.getElementById("combineModeSelect");
  if (cms) {
    cms.value = board.globals.combine_mode;
    cms.addEventListener("change", () => {
      board.globals.combine_mode = cms.value;
      _scheduleStateSync();
    });
  }

  // Default strength input
  const dsi = document.getElementById("defaultStrengthInput");
  if (dsi) {
    dsi.value = board.globals.default_strength;
    dsi.addEventListener("change", () => {
      const v = parseFloat(dsi.value);
      if (isFinite(v)) {
        board.globals.default_strength = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v));
        dsi.value = board.globals.default_strength;
        _scheduleStateSync();
      }
    });
  }

  // Bbox crop checkbox
  const bboxCb = document.getElementById("bboxCheckbox");
  if (bboxCb) {
    bboxCb.checked = !!board.globals.bbox;
    bboxCb.addEventListener("change", () => {
      board.globals.bbox = bboxCb.checked;
      _scheduleStateSync();
    });
  }

  // Drop-overlay install + drag/drop
  _installDropOverlay();
  let _dragDepth = 0;
  window.addEventListener("dragenter", () => {
    _dragDepth++;
    _showDropOverlay(true);
  });
  window.addEventListener("dragleave", () => {
    _dragDepth--;
    if (_dragDepth <= 0) _showDropOverlay(false);
  });
  window.addEventListener("dragover", (e) => e.preventDefault());
  window.addEventListener("drop", (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    _dragDepth = 0;
    _showDropOverlay(false);
    const file = e.dataTransfer && e.dataTransfer.files
                 && e.dataTransfer.files[0];
    if (file && file.type.startsWith("image/")) _installImage(file);
  });
}

export function pgkitHandleSelect(level, name) {
  if (typeof name !== "string") return false;
  if (level === "areas") {
    if (!name.startsWith("area.")) return false;
    const id = name.slice(5);
    if (!areaById(id)) return false;
    selectArea(id);
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/* ============================================================
   Boot-time state restore
   ============================================================
   `multimaskBootSync` pulls the server's saved state on page load
   and rehydrates the area list.  The image is NOT auto-fetched from
   Krita — the user picks or imports one explicitly with the panel
   buttons.  There is no image poller. */

async function _applyServerState(payload) {
  if (payload.globals && typeof payload.globals === "object") {
    Object.assign(board.globals, payload.globals);
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(payload.areas)) return;

  board.areas = [];
  board.selectedAreaId = null;
  board.hoveredAreaId  = null;
  board.nextAreaNum    = 1;

  for (const a of payload.areas) {
    const h = a.mask && a.mask.hash;
    if (!h) continue;
    let b64 = null;
    try {
      const res = await fetch("/mask", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({ hash: h }),
      });
      const m = await res.json();
      if (m.success) b64 = m.b64;
    } catch (e) {}
    if (!b64) continue;
    addAreaFromB64(b64, {
      id: a.id, name: a.name, prompt: a.prompt,
      useTagger: a.use_tagger,
      strength:              a.strength,
      set_cond_area:         a.set_cond_area,
      mask_channel:          a.mask_channel,
      bbox:                  a.bbox,
      resize:                a.resize,
      tagger_mode:           a.tagger_mode,
      tagger_model:          a.tagger_model,
      tagger_threshold:      a.tagger_threshold,
      tagger_char_threshold: a.tagger_char_threshold,
    });
  }
}

export async function multimaskBootSync() {
  syncPanelFields();
  syncAreaList();

  // Pull server state first.  Only push if empty — the previous
  // session's areas should survive a page reload.
  let pulled = null;
  try {
    const res = await fetch("/state", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: "{}",
    });
    pulled = await res.json();
  } catch (e) {}

  if (pulled && pulled.success
      && Array.isArray(pulled.areas) && pulled.areas.length > 0) {
    await _applyServerState(pulled);
    syncPanelFields();
    syncAreaList();
  } else {
    _scheduleStateSync();
  }

  _kritaStatusAction();
}
"""

```python
"""The area list: one card per area, with inline prompt textarea and
use_tagger checkbox.  Rebuilds only when the set of area ids changes;
otherwise updates existing cards in place, skipping the focused
input so the user's typing is never stomped.

State-change callbacks are routed through a small hook the bindings
module installs, to avoid a circular import."""

PANEL_LISTS_JS = r"""
import { board, areaColorById } from "./pg_state.js";
import {
  areaById, updateArea, removeArea, selectArea,
} from "./pg_areas.js";
import { pgkitNotifyEntities } from "./pgkit/remote_client.js";

// Focus tracking
let _focusedAreaId = null;
let _focusedField  = null;

// Debounced state-sync hook, installed by pg_panel_bindings
let _stateChangeHook = null;
export function setStateChangeHook(fn) { _stateChangeHook = fn; }
function _onChange() {
  if (_stateChangeHook) _stateChangeHook();
  pgkitNotifyEntities();
}

export function syncAreaList() {
  const list = document.getElementById("areaList");
  if (!list) return;

  if (_focusedAreaId) _updateInPlace(list);
  else                _rebuild(list);

  pgkitNotifyEntities();
}

function _rebuild(list) {
  list.innerHTML = "";

  if (board.areas.length === 0) {
    const e = document.createElement("div");
    e.className = "empty";
    e.textContent = board.imageHash
      ? "no areas — click + From Krita"
      : "load an image first, then + From Krita";
    list.appendChild(e);
    return;
  }

  for (const area of board.areas) {
    list.appendChild(_makeCard(area));
  }
}

function _updateInPlace(list) {
  const idsNow = board.areas.map(a => a.id);

  // Remove cards for areas that no longer exist.
  const existing = {};
  for (const el of list.children) {
    if (el.classList && el.classList.contains("areaCard")) {
      existing[el.dataset.id] = el;
    }
  }
  for (const id in existing) {
    if (!idsNow.includes(id)) existing[id].remove();
  }

  // Update in place, append new at the end.  No reordering: the array
  // only ever appends or removes, so DOM order matches array order
  // without touching existing nodes.
  for (const area of board.areas) {
    const card = existing[area.id];
    if (card) {
      _updateCard(card, area);
    } else {
      list.appendChild(_makeCard(area));
    }
  }
}

function _updateCard(card, area) {
  const nameEl   = card.querySelector(".areaName");
  const promptEl = card.querySelector(".areaPrompt");
  const taggerEl = card.querySelector(".areaTagger");
  const dimsEl   = card.querySelector(".areaDims");
  const sw       = card.querySelector(".areaSwatch");

  if (nameEl && document.activeElement !== nameEl) nameEl.value = area.name;
  if (promptEl && document.activeElement !== promptEl) promptEl.value = area.prompt;
  if (taggerEl && document.activeElement !== taggerEl) taggerEl.checked = !!area.useTagger;
  if (dimsEl) dimsEl.textContent = (area.mask.w || 0) + "\u00d7" + (area.mask.h || 0);
  if (sw) {
    const hue = areaColorById(area.id);
    sw.style.background = "rgb(" + hue.r + "," + hue.g + "," + hue.b + ")";
  }
}

function _makeCard(area) {
  const card = document.createElement("div");
  card.className = "areaCard";
  card.dataset.id = area.id;

  // Header row
  const header = document.createElement("div");
  header.className = "areaHeader";

  const swatch = document.createElement("span");
  swatch.className = "areaSwatch";
  const hue = areaColorById(area.id);
  swatch.style.background = "rgb(" + hue.r + "," + hue.g + "," + hue.b + ")";
  header.appendChild(swatch);

  const nameInput = document.createElement("input");
  nameInput.className = "areaName";
  nameInput.type = "text";
  nameInput.value = area.name;
  nameInput.title = "Area name. Used as the label and by the node's area_filter.";
  nameInput.addEventListener("focus", () => {
    _focusedAreaId = area.id; _focusedField = "name";
  });
  nameInput.addEventListener("blur", () => {
    _focusedAreaId = null; _focusedField = null;
  });
  nameInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    updateArea(area.id, { name: nameInput.value });
    _onChange();
  });
  header.appendChild(nameInput);

  const dims = document.createElement("span");
  dims.className = "areaDims";
  dims.textContent = (area.mask.w || 0) + "\u00d7" + (area.mask.h || 0);
  header.appendChild(dims);

  const del = document.createElement("button");
  del.className = "areaDel";
  del.textContent = "\u00d7";
  del.title = "Remove this area";
  del.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    removeArea(area.id);
    _onChange();
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
  });
  header.appendChild(del);

  card.appendChild(header);

  // Prompt textarea
  const prompt = document.createElement("textarea");
  prompt.className = "areaPrompt";
  prompt.rows = 2;
  prompt.value = area.prompt;
  prompt.placeholder = "prompt for this area";
  prompt.spellcheck = false;
  prompt.addEventListener("focus", () => {
    _focusedAreaId = area.id; _focusedField = "prompt";
  });
  prompt.addEventListener("blur", () => {
    _focusedAreaId = null; _focusedField = null;
  });
  prompt.addEventListener("input", () => {
    updateArea(area.id, { prompt: prompt.value });
    _onChange();
  });
  card.appendChild(prompt);

  // use_tagger row
  const flags = document.createElement("label");
  flags.className = "areaFlags";
  const tagger = document.createElement("input");
  tagger.className = "areaTagger";
  tagger.type = "checkbox";
  tagger.checked = !!area.useTagger;
  tagger.addEventListener("change", () => {
    updateArea(area.id, { useTagger: tagger.checked });
    _onChange();
  });
  flags.appendChild(tagger);
  const taggerLabel = document.createElement("span");
  taggerLabel.textContent = "use_tagger";
  flags.appendChild(taggerLabel);
  card.appendChild(flags);

  // Card click → select the area (unless click was on an input)
  card.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
    if (e.target === nameInput || e.target === prompt
        || e.target === tagger || e.target === del) return;
    selectArea(area.id);
    import("./pg_dispatch.js").then(m => m.draw()).catch(() => {});
  });

  return card;
}
"""

"""Mask pixel access and hit test.  Only the queries multimask
needs — no bbox computation, no rotation caches."""

PIXELS_JS = r"""
import { board } from "./pg_state.js";

function _maskPixelData(mask) {
  if (mask._pixels) return mask._pixels;
  if (!mask.img) return null;
  const w = mask.w, h = mask.h;
  if (!w || !h) return null;
  const off = document.createElement("canvas");
  off.width = w; off.height = h;
  const octx = off.getContext("2d");
  octx.drawImage(mask.img, 0, 0);
  try {
    mask._pixels = octx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h).data;
    return mask._pixels;
  } catch (e) {
    return null;
  }
}

export function maskPixelData(mask) {
  return _maskPixelData(mask);
}

/* Returns the id of the topmost area whose mask has an opaque pixel
   under (ix, iy), or null.  Masks are in their own pixel grid; the
   point is scaled into it, so a mask whose dimensions differ from
   the playground image still hit-tests correctly. */
export function hitTestAreaAtPoint(ix, iy) {
  if (ix < 0 || iy < 0) return null;
  const imgW = board.imageWidth  || 1;
  const imgH = board.imageHeight || 1;
  for (let i = board.areas.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const a = board.areas[i];
    const m = a.mask;
    if (!m || !m.loaded) continue;
    const mx = Math.floor(ix * m.w / imgW);
    const my = Math.floor(iy * m.h / imgH);
    if (mx < 0 || my < 0 || mx >= m.w || my >= m.h) continue;
    const px = _maskPixelData(m);
    if (!px) continue;
    const off = (my * m.w + mx) * 4;
    if (px[off] >= 128) return a.id;
  }
  return null;
}
"""

"""Multimask state: image, areas, view, draw scheduling.

Leaf module.  Every other project module imports from here and
nothing here imports from them.

`applyCanvasImage` is the autosync target — updates the displayed
image in response to a `@thecanvas` spec change without wiping the
area list.  Used by `pg_autosync.js`; NOT called from any
generation path.

TWO SCHEDULERS
==============
`_scheduleDraw`      → full `draw()`: canvas + `syncPanelFields` +
                       `syncAreaList` (card DOM rebuild).
`_scheduleDrawView`  → `drawView()` only: canvas repaint.

Hover changes (`board.hoveredAreaId`) and selection changes feed only
the canvas's alpha and chrome text — no panel field or card row reads
either — so callers that know their mutation is canvas-only (currently
`hoverArea`) use `_scheduleDrawView`, avoiding a full card-DOM rebuild
on every mask-boundary crossing.

Both schedulers coalesce via `requestAnimationFrame`.  A pending
`_scheduleDraw` supersedes a pending `_scheduleDrawView` — the full
draw already calls `drawView()`, so the view-only RAF is dropped.

`fittedImageRect()` is memoized on the tuple of inputs that fully
determine its result: `(innerWidth, innerHeight, imageWidth,
imageHeight, zoom, panX, panY)`.  The function runs 2–4 times per
`mousemove` frame (once explicitly in `pg_dispatch`, once inside
`screenToImage`, once inside `drawView`, once inside `zoomAt`).
The cache turns all but the first into a string compare.

Callers must treat the returned object as read-only — none of them
mutate it, verified across `pg_view.py`, `pg_view_image.py`,
`pg_dispatch.py`, `pg_areas.py`, `pg_autosync.py`."""

STATE_JS = r"""
import {
  VIEW_ZOOM_MIN, VIEW_ZOOM_MAX, VIEW_PAN_MARGIN,
} from "./pg_tuning.js";

export const canvas = document.getElementById("c");
export const ctx    = canvas.getContext("2d");

let _dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;

export const view = { zoom: 1, panX: 0, panY: 0 };

export function resetView() {
  view.zoom = 1;
  view.panX = 0;
  view.panY = 0;
}

export function clampPan() {
  if (!board.imageWidth || !board.imageHeight) return;
  const cw = window.innerWidth, ch = window.innerHeight;
  const pad = 40;
  const sx = (cw - 2 * pad) / board.imageWidth;
  const sy = (ch - 2 * pad) / board.imageHeight;
  const baseS = Math.min(sx, sy);
  const s = baseS * view.zoom;

  const bw = board.imageWidth * s;
  const bh = board.imageHeight * s;
  const baseX = (cw - bw) / 2;
  const baseY = (ch - bh) / 2;
  const m = VIEW_PAN_MARGIN;

  const minPanX = m - baseX - bw;
  const maxPanX = cw - m - baseX;
  view.panX = Math.max(minPanX, Math.min(maxPanX, view.panX));

  const minPanY = m - baseY - bh;
  const maxPanY = ch - m - baseY;
  view.panY = Math.max(minPanY, Math.min(maxPanY, view.panY));
}

export function zoomAt(screenX, screenY, newZoom) {
  const [ix0, iy0] = screenToImage(screenX, screenY);
  view.zoom = Math.max(VIEW_ZOOM_MIN, Math.min(VIEW_ZOOM_MAX, newZoom));
  const [sx1, sy1] = imageToScreen(ix0, iy0);
  view.panX += screenX - sx1;
  view.panY += screenY - sy1;
  clampPan();
}

export const MASK_COLORS = [
  { r: 255, g:  90, b: 105 },
  { r: 120, g: 220, b: 255 },
  { r: 255, g: 200, b:  90 },
  { r: 140, g: 225, b: 160 },
  { r: 180, g: 155, b: 255 },
  { r: 255, g: 165, b: 105 },
  { r: 110, g: 220, b: 210 },
  { r: 220, g: 230, b: 120 },
];

export function areaColorById(id) {
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < id.length; i++) {
    h = ((h << 5) - h + id.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
  }
  return MASK_COLORS[Math.abs(h) % MASK_COLORS.length];
}

export function _defaultGlobals() {
  return {
    combine_mode:             "combine",
    use_base_setarea:         false,
    base_area_width:          1024,
    base_area_height:         1024,
    default_strength:         0.9,
    default_set_cond_area:    "default",
    tagger_mode:              "replace",
    tagger_model:             "wd-v1-4-moat-tagger-v2",
    tagger_threshold:         0.35,
    tagger_char_threshold:    0.85,
    bbox:                     true,
    resize:                   true,
    mask_w:                   1024,
    mask_h:                   1024,
    mask_channel:             "red",
  };
}

export const board = {
  imageHash:     null,
  imageWidth:    0,
  imageHeight:   0,
  imageDataUrl:  null,
  imageEl:       null,
  originalImageEl: null,
  originalWidth:   0,
  originalHeight:  0,

  mouse: { x: 0, y: 0, inside: false },

  areas: [],                // [{id, name, prompt, useTagger, mask: entry, ...}]
  selectedAreaId: null,
  hoveredAreaId:  null,
  nextAreaNum:    1,

  globals: _defaultGlobals(),
};

export function setImage(hash, dataUrl, width, height) {
  board.imageHash       = hash;
  board.originalImageEl = null;
  board.originalWidth   = width;
  board.originalHeight  = height;

  board.imageEl      = null;
  board.imageWidth   = 0;
  board.imageHeight  = 0;
  board.imageDataUrl = null;

  board.areas          = [];
  board.selectedAreaId = null;
  board.hoveredAreaId  = null;
  board.nextAreaNum    = 1;

  resetView();

  const img = new Image();
  img.onload = () => {
    board.originalImageEl = img;
    board.originalWidth   = img.naturalWidth;
    board.originalHeight  = img.naturalHeight;
    board.imageEl         = img;
    board.imageWidth      = img.naturalWidth;
    board.imageHeight     = img.naturalHeight;
    board.imageDataUrl    = dataUrl;
    _scheduleDraw();
  };
  img.onerror = () => _scheduleDraw();
  img.src = dataUrl;
  _scheduleDraw();
}

/* ============================================================
   applyCanvasImage — autosync target
   ============================================================
   Swap the displayed image in response to a `@thecanvas` spec
   change.  Unlike `setImage`, this keeps the area list intact
   (invalidating only each mask's pixel caches so the tinted
   overlays rebuild).  Warns when the new dims differ from the old,
   since area masks may no longer align. */
export function applyCanvasImage(hash, dataUrl, width, height) {
  const oldW = board.imageWidth;
  const oldH = board.imageHeight;
  const dimsMatch = (oldW === 0 || oldH === 0
                     || (width === oldW && height === oldH));

  board.imageHash       = hash;
  board.originalWidth   = width;
  board.originalHeight  = height;

  const img = new Image();
  img.onload = () => {
    board.imageEl         = img;
    board.originalImageEl = img;
    board.originalWidth   = img.naturalWidth;
    board.originalHeight  = img.naturalHeight;
    board.imageWidth      = img.naturalWidth;
    board.imageHeight     = img.naturalHeight;
    board.imageDataUrl    = dataUrl;

    for (const a of board.areas) {
      if (a.mask) {
        a.mask._pixels = null;
        a.mask._tinted = null;
        a.mask._tintedKey = null;
      }
    }

    if (!dimsMatch) {
      console.warn(
        "[multimask] @thecanvas dims changed from "
        + oldW + "\u00d7" + oldH + " to " + width + "\u00d7" + height
        + "; area masks may no longer align"
      );
    }

    _scheduleDraw();
  };
  img.onerror = () => _scheduleDraw();
  img.src = dataUrl;
  _scheduleDraw();
}

export function clearImage() {
  board.imageHash       = null;
  board.originalImageEl = null;
  board.originalWidth   = 0;
  board.originalHeight  = 0;
  board.imageEl         = null;
  board.imageWidth      = 0;
  board.imageHeight     = 0;
  board.imageDataUrl    = null;

  board.areas          = [];
  board.selectedAreaId = null;
  board.hoveredAreaId  = null;
  board.nextAreaNum    = 1;

  resetView();
  _scheduleDraw();
}

/* ============================================================
   Image-fit rect — MEMOIZED on the input tuple.
   See the module docstring.  Callers must not mutate the
   returned object.
   ============================================================ */

let _firCacheKey = null;
let _firCacheVal = null;

export function fittedImageRect() {
  const cw = window.innerWidth, ch = window.innerHeight;
  if (!board.imageWidth || !board.imageHeight) return null;

  const key = cw + "," + ch + ","
            + board.imageWidth + "," + board.imageHeight + ","
            + view.zoom + "," + view.panX + "," + view.panY;
  if (key === _firCacheKey) return _firCacheVal;

  const pad = 40;
  const sx = (cw - 2 * pad) / board.imageWidth;
  const sy = (ch - 2 * pad) / board.imageHeight;
  const baseS = Math.min(sx, sy);
  const s = baseS * view.zoom;
  const w = board.imageWidth  * s;
  const h = board.imageHeight * s;
  const x0 = (cw - w) / 2 + view.panX;
  const y0 = (ch - h) / 2 + view.panY;

  const val = { x0, y0, w, h, s };
  _firCacheKey = key;
  _firCacheVal = val;
  return val;
}

export function imageToScreen(x, y) {
  const r = fittedImageRect();
  if (!r) return [x, y];
  return [r.x0 + x * r.s, r.y0 + y * r.s];
}

export function screenToImage(sx, sy) {
  const r = fittedImageRect();
  if (!r) return [0, 0];
  return [(sx - r.x0) / r.s, (sy - r.y0) / r.s];
}

/* ============================================================
   Draw scheduling — two levels
   ============================================================
   `_drawPending`  a RAF is queued.
   `_drawFull`     the queued RAF should call `_drawFn` (draw), not
                   `_drawViewFn` (drawView).

   `_scheduleDraw`     sets `_drawFull = true` and (re)uses the
                       pending RAF.  Upgrades a pending view-only
                       RAF to full.
   `_scheduleDrawView` sets `_drawFull = false` only if no RAF is
                       pending.  A pending full draw is left alone
                       (it will call `drawView` internally). */

let _drawPending = false;
let _drawFull    = false;
let _drawFn      = null;
let _drawViewFn  = null;

export function _setDraw(fn)     { _drawFn = fn; }
export function _setDrawView(fn) { _drawViewFn = fn; }

function _fire() {
  const full = _drawFull;
  _drawPending = false;
  _drawFull = false;
  if (full) { if (_drawFn) _drawFn(); }
  else      { if (_drawViewFn) _drawViewFn(); }
}

export function _scheduleDraw() {
  _drawFull = true;
  if (_drawPending) return;
  _drawPending = true;
  if (typeof requestAnimationFrame === "function") requestAnimationFrame(_fire);
  else setTimeout(_fire, 16);
}

export function _scheduleDrawView() {
  if (_drawPending) return;   // don't downgrade a pending full draw
  _drawFull = false;
  _drawPending = true;
  if (typeof requestAnimationFrame === "function") requestAnimationFrame(_fire);
  else setTimeout(_fire, 16);
}

export function resize() {
  _dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
  const cw = window.innerWidth, ch = window.innerHeight;
  canvas.width  = Math.round(cw * _dpr);
  canvas.height = Math.round(ch * _dpr);
  canvas.style.width  = cw + "px";
  canvas.style.height = ch + "px";
  ctx.setTransform(_dpr, 0, 0, _dpr, 0, 0);
  clampPan();
  if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
}
window.addEventListener("resize", resize);
"""

"""Main draw entry point.  No rotation, no context rectangle.

CHROME TEXT IS CACHED AS AN OFFSCREEN BLIT
==========================================
`drawView()` clears the canvas at the top of every frame, so the
chrome text can't be skipped outright.  But `fillText` re-shapes the
whole string each call, and the string only changes on: zoom, image
dims, area count, selection, or the selected area's name.  It does
NOT change on pan, hover, or tint alpha — so pan-only frames (where
`drawView()` is called from the pan branch without touching the
panel) always hit the cache.

The cache keys the rendered text; on a hit, the frame blits a
pre-shaped RGBA canvas with one `drawImage`.  On a miss, the string
is measured once, an offscreen canvas is allocated to fit, and
`fillText` runs there."""

VIEW_JS = r"""
import { ctx, board, view, fittedImageRect } from "./pg_state.js";
import { drawImageLayer } from "./pg_view_image.js";

function _chromeText() {
  const sel = board.selectedAreaId
    ? board.areas.find(a => a.id === board.selectedAreaId)
    : null;

  const selLabel = board.areas.length === 0
    ? "NO AREAS — import masks from Krita"
    : (sel ? "AREA " + sel.name + " SELECTED" : "NO AREA SELECTED");

  return "IMAGE " + board.imageWidth + "\u00d7" + board.imageHeight
       + "   \u00b7   ZOOM " + view.zoom.toFixed(2) + "\u00d7"
       + "   \u00b7   " + selLabel
       + "   \u00b7   AREAS " + board.areas.length;
}

let _chromeCache = { key: null, canvas: null };

function _drawChromeText() {
  const text = _chromeText();

  let entry = _chromeCache;
  if (entry.key !== text) {
    // Measure once — only on text change, which is rare.
    ctx.save();
    ctx.font = "700 10px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
    const w = Math.ceil(ctx.measureText(text).width) + 4;
    ctx.restore();

    const c = document.createElement("canvas");
    c.width  = Math.max(1, w);
    c.height = 20;
    const cx = c.getContext("2d");
    cx.font = "700 10px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
    cx.fillStyle = "#5a6774";
    cx.textAlign = "left";
    cx.textBaseline = "top";
    cx.fillText(text, 0, 0);

    entry = _chromeCache = { key: text, canvas: c };
  }

  ctx.drawImage(entry.canvas, 14, 14);
}

export function drawView() {
  const cw = window.innerWidth, ch = window.innerHeight;
  ctx.fillStyle = "#0a0e14";
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, cw, ch);

  const r = fittedImageRect();
  if (!r || !board.imageEl) {
    ctx.fillStyle = "#5a6774";
    ctx.font = "700 12px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace";
    ctx.textAlign = "center";
    ctx.textBaseline = "middle";
    ctx.fillText("drop an image or import from Krita to begin",
                 cw / 2, ch / 2);
    return;
  }

  drawImageLayer(r);
  _drawChromeText();
}
"""

"""The loaded image and the tinted overlay for each area's mask."""

VIEW_IMAGE_JS = r"""
import { ctx, board, areaColorById } from "./pg_state.js";
import { maskPixelData } from "./pg_pixels.js";

function _tintedMask(mask, color) {
  const key = color.r + "," + color.g + "," + color.b;
  if (mask._tinted && mask._tintedKey === key) return mask._tinted;

  const px = maskPixelData(mask);
  if (!px) return null;
  const W = mask.w, H = mask.h;
  if (!W || !H) return null;

  const off = document.createElement("canvas");
  off.width = W; off.height = H;
  const octx = off.getContext("2d");
  const imgData = octx.createImageData(W, H);
  const out = imgData.data;

  for (let i = 0; i < px.length; i += 4) {
    const m = px[i] / 255;
    const a = px[i + 3] / 255;
    out[i]     = color.r;
    out[i + 1] = color.g;
    out[i + 2] = color.b;
    out[i + 3] = Math.round(255 * m * a);
  }
  octx.putImageData(imgData, 0, 0);

  mask._tinted = off;
  mask._tintedKey = key;
  return off;
}

export function drawImageLayer(r) {
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = true;
  ctx.imageSmoothingQuality = "high";
  ctx.drawImage(board.imageEl, r.x0, r.y0, r.w, r.h);

  ctx.strokeStyle = "#1e2836";
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  ctx.strokeRect(r.x0 + 0.5, r.y0 + 0.5, r.w - 1, r.h - 1);

  for (const area of board.areas) {
    const m = area.mask;
    if (!m || !m.loaded) continue;
    const tinted = _tintedMask(m, areaColorById(area.id));
    if (!tinted) continue;
    const isSel   = (area.id === board.selectedAreaId);
    const isHover = (area.id === board.hoveredAreaId);
    let alpha = 0.35;
    if (isSel)   alpha = 0.55;
    if (isHover) alpha = Math.min(0.70, alpha + 0.10);
    ctx.save();
    ctx.globalAlpha = alpha;
    ctx.drawImage(tinted, r.x0, r.y0, r.w, r.h);
    ctx.restore();
  }
}
"""

Four modules now live in `kritomatic_shared`, under `<repo>/src/`, so
the daemon and the playgrounds share one copy of each:

    comfyui_client.py        HTTP + WebSocket client  (setup.py dep:

=======================

from pathlib import Path

def _find_repo_src() -> Path:
    p = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    for _ in range(10):
        cand = p / "src"
        if (cand / "kritomatic").is_dir():
            return cand
        if p == p.parent:
            break
        p = p.parent

        "Could not locate src/kritomatic from "
        + str(Path(__file__).resolve())

import time as _time

_OBJECT_INFO_DEFAULT_TTL = 30.0


def cached_object_info(client, ttl=_OBJECT_INFO_DEFAULT_TTL):
    """Return `client.object_info()`, cached on the client for `ttl` s.

    ComfyUI's `/object_info` endpoint returns a ~200 KB JSON document
    listing every installed custom node and its schema. It changes only
    when ComfyUI restarts or a custom node is installed, so caching it
    on the client (which is process-wide via `get_client()`) removes
    most of the cost without any staleness risk: `reset_client()` drops
    the client and the cache together.
    """
    cached = getattr(client, "_object_info_cache", None)
    now = _time.monotonic()
    if cached is not None and (now - cached["at"]) < ttl:
        return cached["data"]
    data = client.object_info()
    client._object_info_cache = {"at": now, "data": data}
    return data


def __getattr__(name):
    if name == "image":
        from . import image as _image
        return _image
    raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")

```python
"""Minimal image utilities for the browser playgrounds.

Replaces the Krita-specific parts of kritomatic's comfyui_krita.py. Only
what a browser-driven workflow needs: raw bytes → PNG, PNG → raw bytes,
and PNG dimensions. Uses PIL for encode/decode.

`EncodedImage` is re-exported from `tooling.py` (which is copied verbatim
from kritomatic); no new type is defined here.
"""

from io import BytesIO
from typing import Tuple

from PIL import Image

from .tooling import EncodedImage


PNG_MAGIC = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"


def is_png(data: bytes) -> bool:
    return data[:8] == PNG_MAGIC


def png_dimensions(png_bytes: bytes) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    with Image.open(BytesIO(png_bytes)) as im:
        return im.width, im.height


def encode_png_from_rgba(raw: bytes, width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    img = Image.frombytes("RGBA", (width, height), raw)
    buf = BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, "PNG")
    return buf.getvalue()


def decode_png_to_rgba(png_bytes: bytes) -> Tuple[bytes, int, int]:
    with Image.open(BytesIO(png_bytes)) as im:
        im = im.convert("RGBA")
        return im.tobytes(), im.width, im.height


def make_encoded_image(raw_bytes: bytes) -> EncodedImage:
    """Turn arbitrary uploaded bytes into an EncodedImage.

    The workflow's `ETN_LoadImageCache` decodes with PIL and expects a
    PNG or one of PIL's other readable formats. We normalize to PNG
    here so the tooling never sees JPEG/WebP/etc; the cost is one
    decode/re-encode on non-PNG uploads.
    """
    if is_png(raw_bytes):
        w, h = png_dimensions(raw_bytes)
        return EncodedImage(data=raw_bytes, width=w, height=h, is_mask=False)

    with Image.open(BytesIO(raw_bytes)) as im:
        im = im.convert("RGBA")
        w, h = im.width, im.height

"""
pgkit — shared toolkit for the playgrounds.

    pgkit.styles            shared CSS

                            for the kit's own JS
    pgkit.js_check          per-module syntax pre-flight
    pgkit.lint              static check for ES-module import/export
                            consistency across a playground
    pgkit.remote_client     browser-side WebSocket client (ES module)
    pgkit.remote_cli_client Python client for the same protocol;
                            the transport under remote_cli
    pgkit.ws                minimal WebSocket framing (Python)
    pgkit.remote_hub        server-side client registry and relay
    pgkit.server            HTTP + WebSocket server, and /modules/
                            serving

A playground wires these together with its own model, views, and
scene format.  See the module docstrings for the contracts.

ES MODULES
==========
Playground JS is served as ES modules.  Each project module is a
`(label, js_source)` pair inside a `_MODULE_SOURCES` dict in the
project's `*_html.py`.  The dict is passed to both `page()` (for
syntax checking) and `kit_serve()` (for serving at `/modules/<label>`).
A single boot module (also in the dict) does all the imports and the
boot calls.

Splitting each panel file into its own module is what makes
cross-file references loud instead of silent: a missing export is a
load error naming both files, not a ReferenceError hidden 100
kilobytes into a bundle.

==============
`pgkit.remote_cli_client` is the Python-side counterpart to
`pgkit.remote_client`.  It speaks the same wire protocol and is what
`remote_cli/` is built on.  Any Python script can import it to drive a
running playground — see the module docstring for the full contract.

```python
"""pgkit._source_hash — content hash of the hub↔client contract.

Both `pgkit/hub.py` (the server) and `pgkit/hub_client.py` (the
client) compute this hash on startup. If they disagree, the running
hub was loaded from a different version of the source than the
caller is running now — Python does not reload already-imported
modules when their `.py` file changes on disk, so a hub that started
before an edit will keep serving the old code until it is killed.

`hub_client.ensure_running` uses the mismatch to restart the running
hub, so a developer who edits `hub.py` sees their changes on the next
playground start without remembering to `pgkit.hub --shutdown`
manually.

WHICH FILES ARE COVERED
=======================
`_CONTRACT_MODULES` names the files whose content, if changed, forces
a restart. It must include every file that defines a wire-format
decision or a cross-process invariant:

    __init__.py      PROTOCOL_VERSION, __version__
    hub.py           the server itself
    hub_client.py    the client's expectations of the server
    ws.py            the framing (both sides)

Files that are imported by one side only and do not affect the wire
format — `panel_core.py`, `shell.py`, `styles.py`, `js_check.py`,
`lint.py`, `html_shell.py`, `modules.py`, `server.py`,
`remote_client.py`, `remote_cli_client.py`, `remote_hub.py`,
`launcher.py` — are deliberately excluded. Editing one of those
should not force every running playground to restart.

Adding a file to this tuple is a compatibility commitment: any
running hub started before the addition will be considered stale on
the next playground start, shut down, and relaunched. That is the
correct semantics — a new contract file means the old hub does not
have it — but it should be done deliberately, not by accident.

WHY NOT A MANUAL VERSION CONSTANT
=================================
`PROTOCOL_VERSION` is already bumped by hand for wire-compatible
changes. But forgetting to bump it is exactly the failure mode this
module exists to prevent. mtime-based detection is also unreliable:
`touch` without content changes, `git checkout` of an unchanged
branch, a save with no edits — all update mtime without changing the
code. Hashing the bytes sidesteps both: the hash changes iff the
bytes change.

CACHING
=======
The hash is computed once per process and cached. This is
deliberate. The caller's question is "does the running hub have the
same code I loaded?" — not "does the code on disk right now match
what I loaded?" Those become different questions the moment someone
edits a file mid-session. The first question is the one that
determines whether the wire protocol will interoperate, and the
first question is what a cache preserves.

READING FROM DISK, NOT FROM `sys.modules`
=========================================
`source_hash` reads the `.py` files' bytes directly rather than
calling `inspect.getsource` on the imported modules. That means it
works even for files the caller does not import (`hub.py` on the
client side, `hub_client.py` on the server side) — both sides are
contract-committed to include both, and reading from disk is how
either side can honour that commitment without dragging the other
into its import graph.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from pathlib import Path


_CONTRACT_MODULES = (
    "__init__.py",
    "hub.py",
    "hub_client.py",
    "ws.py",
)

_CACHE: "str | None" = None


def source_hash() -> str:
    """Hex sha256 of the contract modules' current on-disk content.

    Cached after the first call; the result is stable for the process
    lifetime. A missing file contributes ``missing:<name>`` to the
    hash. That cannot happen in a working checkout, but it keeps the
    hash deterministic if it does — the alternative, raising, would
    make the whole playground unusable for an unrelated packaging
    mistake.
    """
    global _CACHE
    if _CACHE is not None:
        return _CACHE
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    for name in _CONTRACT_MODULES:
        try:
            data = (here / name).read_bytes()
        except OSError:
            data = b"missing:" + name.encode("utf-8")
        h.update(data)
        h.update(b"\0")
    _CACHE = h.hexdigest()
    return _CACHE


def short_hash() -> str:
    """8-character prefix of `source_hash`, for log messages."""
    return source_hash()[:8]
```

pgkit.html_shell — assemble a playground's HTML page.

The page is the shell (head, CSS, panel wrapper, canvas) plus exactly
one `<script type="module" src="modules/<boot_module>">`.  The boot
module's imports load every other module.

`page()` runs `js_check.check_js` on every module in
`module_sources`, one at a time, before returning HTML.  A syntax
error aborts page assembly with a `JsSyntaxError` naming the file
and line.  The caller catches it and reports; `*_html.py`'s caller
in turn exits with status 1 so no HTML file is written and no
server starts.

BOOT SCRIPT URL IS RELATIVE
===========================
`src="modules/<boot_module>"` is a *relative* URL.  It resolves
against the page's own URL:

    standalone   http://host:87NN/board_playground.html
                 →  http://host:87NN/modules/_boot.js

    under hub    http://host:8780/board/board_playground.html
                 →  http://host:8780/board/modules/_boot.js

The boot module's *own* `import "./pgkit/shell.js"` resolves
against the boot module's URL, so it lands on the right prefix
without any `<base>` tag: the browser already has the URL.  This
is why the kit does not emit `<base href="...">` — it would only
re-duplicate information the page URL already carries, and would
break the "same HTML file, two deployment shapes" property.

The only place in the shell that used an absolute `/modules/` path
was this script tag.  No other template needed a prefix.
"""

from .js_check import JsSyntaxError, check_js
from .styles   import SHELL_CSS


_HEAD = """<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>{title}</title>
<style>
{css}
</style>
</head>
<body>
"""

_PANEL_OPEN = """<div id="ui">
  <h3>{panel_title}
    <button id="collapseBtn" title="Collapse (H)"
      style="margin-left:auto; width:auto; padding:0 6px;
             height:20px; font-size:11px; line-height:1;">−</button>
  </h3>

  <div class="panel-body">
"""

_PANEL_STATUS = """    <div id="status">{status_text}</div>

  </div>
</div>
"""

_PANEL_CLOSE = """
<button id="restoreBtn" title="Show panel (H)">&#9776; Show panel</button>
<div id="remoteBanner" title="A remote client is connected">&#9679; Controlled remotely</div>

<canvas id="c"></canvas>
"""

_BOOT_SCRIPT = """
<script type="module" src="modules/{boot_module}"></script>
</body>
</html>
"""


def head(title, extra_css=""):
    return _HEAD.format(title=title, css=SHELL_CSS + extra_css)


def panel_open(panel_title):
    return _PANEL_OPEN.format(panel_title=panel_title)


def panel_status(status_text):
    return _PANEL_STATUS.format(status_text=status_text)


def panel_close():
    return _PANEL_CLOSE


def tail(boot_module):
    return _BOOT_SCRIPT.format(boot_module=boot_module)


def page(*, title, panel_title, panel_body, module_sources,
         boot_module, extra_css="", status_text="", check_syntax=True):
    """Assemble the full HTML page from its parts.

    Runs each module through `node --check` before assembling the
    page.  `boot_module` must be one of the keys in `module_sources`;
    the boot module's imports load the rest.

    Raises `JsSyntaxError` on a syntax error in any module.  `*_html.py`
    catches it, reports the offending file and line, and exits.
    """
    if boot_module not in module_sources:
        raise ValueError(
            f"page(): boot_module {boot_module!r} is not present "
            f"in module_sources (keys: {sorted(module_sources)})"
        )

    if check_syntax:
        for name, source in module_sources.items():
            check_js(source, label=name)

    return (
        head(title, extra_css)
        + panel_open(panel_title)
        + panel_body
        + panel_status(status_text)
        + panel_close()
        + tail(boot_module)
    )
