"""pgkit.hub — multi-playground hub server.

    python -m pgkit.hub                  # start manually
    python -m pgkit.hub --shutdown       # ask a running hub to exit

A single HTTP server (default 127.0.0.1:8780) that:

    · accepts WebSocket registrations from playgrounds, panels, and
      launchers on  /__hub_ws
    · proxies  /<name>/*  to  localhost:<registered_port>/*  for both
      HTTP and WebSocket upgrades
    · accepts  GET /__playgrounds  for one-shot CLI listings
    · accepts  GET /__hash  for a content fingerprint of its own
      source; see "FRESHNESS" below
    · accepts  POST /__shutdown  (optionally ?quiet=1) for cooperative
      exit
    · exposes cooperative shutdown and (opt-in) hard kill over the
      management WebSocket, never over HTTP polling
    · broadcasts a `playgrounds` event to every connected panel
      whenever the registered set changes — no polling anywhere

FRESHNESS
=========
`GET /__hash` returns `{"source_hash": "<sha256>"}`, computed by
`pgkit._source_hash` over the four files that define the hub↔client
contract. The client (`pgkit.hub_client`) probes this endpoint before
deciding a running hub is usable. A mismatch — or a 404 from a hub
that predates this endpoint — triggers an automatic restart. See
`_source_hash.py` for the full design rationale.

The hash is also printed in the startup banner, so a developer
inspecting `~/.pgkit/hub.log` can compare it with what the current
checkout produces.

QUIET SHUTDOWN
==============
`POST /__shutdown?quiet=1` exits without sending `shutdown` to
registered playgrounds. This is what the auto-restart uses: siblings
that were connected to a stale hub survive the restart and reconnect
to the fresh one via their own reconnect loops.

Without `quiet`, `POST /__shutdown` is the historical behavior — it
notifies every registration (which triggers `os._exit(0)` on those
processes) and then exits. This is what `pgkit.hub --shutdown`
invokes, because a user who types that command means "stop
everything".

One upgrade note: a hub that predates the `quiet` parameter ignores
the query string and kills its siblings on the first auto-restart.
Every hub spawned after this parameter was added honours it. So the
sibling-kill is a one-time cost of the transition, not an ongoing
property.

REGISTRATION IDENTITY
=====================
A `Registration` records the WS socket that created it. `deregister`
takes an optional `sock`: when it matches the current registration's
socket, the registration is removed; when it doesn't, the caller is
an old handler noticing its socket died *after* a newer connection
already took the name, and the removal is a no-op.

GROUPS
======
A registration may carry an optional `group` string (set by
`pgkit.hub_client.ensure_running(group=...)`).  Groups are metadata,
not routing: proxying, `/__playgrounds`, and target selection all
treat each registration independently.  The group is consulted only
by `_kill_playground`, which enriches the kill_result message to
name the group and its member count.

LAUNCHERS
=========
A launcher opens an additional WS with `role="launcher"` and the
same `group` as its playgrounds.  This registration's purpose is to
carry per-group control commands.  It carries an `available` field
(a list of playground names the launcher can start); the field is
pushed by the launcher via `launcher_state` messages and re-broadcast
to panels as part of every `playgrounds` event.

Panels send `launcher_start` / `launcher_stop` / `launcher_restart`
messages over their own management WS; the hub finds the launcher
whose `available` contains the target name and forwards the message.
The launcher replies with `launcher_result`, which the hub broadcasts
to every panel.

Killing any *playground* in a group still shuts down the whole group
(the cooperative `shutdown` message reaches the launcher process,
which exits).  The new launcher_* commands are the way to stop or
start an individual member without touching the rest.

PANELS
======
Two kinds of clients connect with `role="panel"`:

    Registered panels
        The Python-side HubConnection of a running remote_panel
        process. It carries a `name`, `port`, `pid`, and `html_file`
        in its hello frame, and becomes a first-class entry in
        `registrations` with `role="panel"`.

    Listener panels
        The browser-side management WebSocket that
        `remote_panel/rp_client.py` opens. It carries no name and no
        port, only `role="panel"`. It is not registered; it joins
        `panel_socks` for `playgrounds` broadcasts and can send
        `kill`, `shutdown_hub`, and `launcher_*` commands.

ABSOLUTE-PATH FETCHES FROM PANELS
=================================
Panel JS uses `fetch("/krita/import")` and similar absolute paths.
Under the hub, the panel page is at `/<name>/<name>_playground.html`,
but an absolute-path fetch resolves against the hub root.  The
resolver therefore has two rules:

    1. Explicit prefix: `/<registered-name>/<rest>` → forward to
       `/<rest>` on that playground.
    2. Referer fallback: first segment is not a playground, but the
       Referer's first segment is → forward unchanged.

See `Handler._resolve_proxy_target`.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import select
import signal
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time
import uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs

from . import ws as _ws
from ._source_hash import source_hash, short_hash


HUB_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
HUB_PORT = 8780


# ============================================================================
#  State
# ============================================================================

class Registration:
    """One peer's registration, held while its WS is open.

    Fields:
        name, port, role, pid, sock, html_file, group,
        connected_at, send_lock

    `available` is only meaningful for role="launcher"; it is the
    list of playground names the launcher can start.  For any other
    role it is None.
    """

    def __init__(self, name, port, role, pid, sock, html_file=None,
                 group=None, available=None):
        self.name = name
        self.port = port
        self.role = role
        self.pid = pid
        self.sock = sock
        self.html_file = html_file
        self.group = group
        self.available = available
        self.connected_at = time.time()
        self.send_lock = threading.Lock()

    def send(self, msg):
        data = json.dumps(msg)
        with self.send_lock:
            _ws.write_text_frame(self.sock, data)

    def to_json(self):
        d = {
            "name":         self.name,
            "port":         self.port,
            "role":         self.role,
            "pid":          self.pid,
            "html_file":    self.html_file,
            "group":        self.group,
            "connected_at": self.connected_at,
        }
        if self.role == "launcher":
            d["available"] = list(self.available or [])
        return d


class Hub:
    def __init__(self):
        self.registrations = {}
        self.panel_socks = set()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def register(self, reg):
        with self.lock:
            old = self.registrations.get(reg.name)
            self.registrations[reg.name] = reg
        if old is not None and old is not reg:
            try:
                old.sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
        self.broadcast_playgrounds()

    def deregister(self, name, sock=None):
        with self.lock:
            reg = self.registrations.get(name)
            if reg is None:
                return
            if sock is not None and reg.sock is not sock:
                return
            self.registrations.pop(name, None)
        self.broadcast_playgrounds()

    def find(self, name):
        with self.lock:
            return self.registrations.get(name)

    def has(self, name):
        with self.lock:
            return name in self.registrations

    def find_launcher_for(self, target):
        """Return the launcher whose `available` contains `target`."""
        with self.lock:
            for r in self.registrations.values():
                if r.role == "launcher" and target in (r.available or []):
                    return r
        return None

    def add_panel(self, sock):
        with self.lock:
            self.panel_socks.add(sock)
        try:
            _ws.write_text_frame(sock, json.dumps(self._playgrounds_msg()))
        except OSError:
            self.remove_panel(sock)

    def remove_panel(self, sock):
        with self.lock:
            self.panel_socks.discard(sock)

    def _playgrounds_msg(self):
        with self.lock:
            regs = [r.to_json() for r in self.registrations.values()]
        return {"type": "playgrounds", "playgrounds": regs}

    def broadcast_playgrounds(self):
        msg = self._playgrounds_msg()
        data = json.dumps(msg)
        with self.lock:
            socks = list(self.panel_socks)
        dead = []
        for sock in socks:
            try:
                _ws.write_text_frame(sock, data)
            except OSError:
                dead.append(sock)
        for sock in dead:
            self.remove_panel(sock)

    def broadcast_to_panels(self, msg):
        """Send one message to every connected listener panel."""
        data = json.dumps(msg)
        with self.lock:
            socks = list(self.panel_socks)
        dead = []
        for sock in socks:
            try:
                _ws.write_text_frame(sock, data)
            except OSError:
                dead.append(sock)
        for sock in dead:
            self.remove_panel(sock)


_HUB = Hub()


# ============================================================================
#  PID verification for hard kill
# ============================================================================

def _verify_pid(pid, name):
    if not pid:
        return False
    proc = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline")
    if proc.exists():
        try:
            cmd = proc.read_bytes() \
                       .replace(b"\x00", b" ") \
                       .decode(errors="replace")
            return (name in cmd) or ("playground" in cmd)
        except OSError:
            return True
    try:
        import subprocess
        out = subprocess.check_output(
            ["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "command="],
            text=True, timeout=2,
        )
        return (name in out) or ("playground" in out)
    except Exception:
        return True


# ============================================================================
#  HTTP / WS handler
# ============================================================================

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    # ---- dispatch -----------------------------------------------------

    def do_GET(self):
        path = urlparse(self.path).path
        is_ws = self.headers.get("Upgrade", "").lower() == "websocket"

        if not is_ws and path == "/__playgrounds":
            self._send_json(_HUB._playgrounds_msg())
            return

        if not is_ws and path == "/__hash":
            self._send_json({"source_hash": source_hash()})
            return

        if is_ws and path == "/__hub_ws":
            self._serve_hub_ws()
            return

        if is_ws:
            self._proxy_ws(path)
            return

        self._proxy_http(path)

    def do_POST(self):
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        path = parsed.path
        if path == "/__shutdown":
            query = parse_qs(parsed.query)
            quiet = (query.get("quiet", ["0"])[0]
                     .lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"))
            self._send_json({"success": True, "quiet": quiet})
            threading.Timer(0.2, _shutdown_hub, args=(not quiet,)).start()
            return
        self._proxy_http(path)

    def do_PUT(self):    self._proxy_http(urlparse(self.path).path)
    def do_DELETE(self): self._proxy_http(urlparse(self.path).path)

    # ---- helpers ------------------------------------------------------

    def _send_json(self, data, code=200):
        body = json.dumps(data).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
        self.close_connection = True

    def _split_name(self, path):
        parts = path.lstrip("/").split("/", 1)
        name = parts[0] if parts else ""
        rest = "/" + parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else "/"
        return name, rest

    def _resolve_proxy_target(self, path):
        name, rest = self._split_name(path)
        if name and _HUB.has(name):
            return name, rest
        if name and not name.startswith("__"):
            referer = self.headers.get("Referer", "") or ""
            if referer:
                try:
                    ref_path = urlparse(referer).path
                    ref_parts = ref_path.lstrip("/").split("/", 1)
                    ref_name = ref_parts[0] if ref_parts else ""
                    if ref_name and _HUB.has(ref_name):
                        return ref_name, path
                except Exception:
                    pass
        return None

    def _unknown_target_json(self, path):
        name, _ = self._split_name(path)
        self._send_json(
            {"success": False, "message": f"unknown playground: {name}"},
            404,
        )

    # ---- management WS -----------------------------------------------

    def _serve_hub_ws(self):
        key = self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Key")
        if not key:
            self.send_error(400, "Missing Sec-WebSocket-Key")
            return

        self.wfile.write(_ws.handshake_response(key))
        self.wfile.flush()

        sock = self.connection
        sock.settimeout(None)

        role = None
        registered_name = None

        try:
            opcode, payload = _ws.read_frame(sock)
            if opcode != 0x01:
                return
            try:
                hello = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
            except Exception:
                return

            role = hello.get("role")
            name = hello.get("name")
            port = int(hello.get("port") or 0)
            pid  = int(hello.get("pid") or 0)
            html_file = hello.get("html_file") or None
            group     = hello.get("group") or None

            if role == "playground":
                if not name or not port:
                    return
                reg = Registration(name, port, role, pid, sock,
                                   html_file=html_file, group=group)
                _HUB.register(reg)
                registered_name = name
                try:
                    reg.send({"type": "hello_ack", "name": name})
                except OSError:
                    return
                self._read_playground_loop(sock, name)

            elif role == "launcher":
                if not name:
                    return
                reg = Registration(name, port, role, pid, sock,
                                   html_file=html_file, group=group,
                                   available=[])
                _HUB.register(reg)
                registered_name = name
                try:
                    reg.send({"type": "hello_ack", "name": name})
                except OSError:
                    return
                self._read_launcher_loop(sock, name)

            elif role == "panel":
                if name and port:
                    reg = Registration(name, port, role, pid, sock,
                                       html_file=html_file, group=group)
                    _HUB.register(reg)
                    registered_name = name
                    try:
                        reg.send({"type": "hello_ack", "name": name})
                    except OSError:
                        return
                    self._read_playground_loop(sock, name)
                else:
                    _HUB.add_panel(sock)
                    self._read_panel_loop(sock)

        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            if registered_name:
                _HUB.deregister(registered_name, sock=sock)
            elif role == "panel":
                _HUB.remove_panel(sock)
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

    def _read_playground_loop(self, sock, name):
        while True:
            try:
                opcode, _payload = _ws.read_frame(sock)
            except OSError:
                return
            if opcode is None or opcode == 0x08:
                return

    def _read_launcher_loop(self, sock, name):
        while True:
            try:
                opcode, payload = _ws.read_frame(sock)
            except OSError:
                return
            if opcode is None or opcode == 0x08:
                return
            if opcode != 0x01:
                continue
            try:
                msg = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
            except Exception:
                continue
            t = msg.get("type")
            if t == "launcher_state":
                reg = _HUB.find(name)
                if reg is None or reg.sock is not sock:
                    return
                with _HUB.lock:
                    reg.available = list(msg.get("available") or [])
                _HUB.broadcast_playgrounds()
            elif t == "launcher_result":
                _HUB.broadcast_to_panels(msg)

    def _read_panel_loop(self, sock):
        while True:
            try:
                opcode, payload = _ws.read_frame(sock)
            except OSError:
                return
            if opcode is None or opcode == 0x08:
                return
            if opcode != 0x01:
                continue
            try:
                msg = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
            except Exception:
                continue

            t = msg.get("type")

            if t == "kill":
                target = msg.get("name") or ""
                hard   = bool(msg.get("hard", False))
                result = _kill_playground(target, hard)
                try:
                    _ws.write_text_frame(
                        sock,
                        json.dumps({
                            "type":   "kill_result",
                            "name":   target,
                            **result,
                        }),
                    )
                except OSError:
                    return

            elif t == "shutdown_hub":
                try:
                    _ws.write_text_frame(
                        sock, json.dumps({"type": "shutdown_ack"})
                    )
                except OSError:
                    pass
                threading.Timer(0.5, _shutdown_hub).start()
                return

            elif t in ("launcher_start", "launcher_stop", "launcher_restart"):
                target = msg.get("name") or ""
                request_id = msg.get("request_id") or ""
                launcher = _HUB.find_launcher_for(target)
                if launcher is None:
                    try:
                        _ws.write_text_frame(sock, json.dumps({
                            "type": "launcher_result",
                            "request_id": request_id,
                            "name": target,
                            "success": False,
                            "message": (f"no launcher manages {target!r} "
                                        f"(is the playground running "
                                        f"standalone?)"),
                        }))
                    except OSError:
                        return
                    continue
                try:
                    launcher.send({
                        "type": t,
                        "name": target,
                        "request_id": request_id,
                    })
                except OSError:
                    try:
                        _ws.write_text_frame(sock, json.dumps({
                            "type": "launcher_result",
                            "request_id": request_id,
                            "name": target,
                            "success": False,
                            "message": "launcher unreachable",
                        }))
                    except OSError:
                        return

    # ---- HTTP proxy --------------------------------------------------

    def _proxy_http(self, path):
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        query = parsed.query
        resolved = self._resolve_proxy_target(path)
        if resolved is None:
            self._unknown_target_json(path)
            return
        name, forward_path = resolved
        reg = _HUB.find(name)
        if reg is None:
            self._unknown_target_json(path)
            return

        try:
            backend = socket.create_connection(
                (HUB_HOST, reg.port), timeout=10
            )
        except OSError as e:
            self._send_json(
                {"success": False,
                 "message": f"playground {name} unreachable: {e}"},
                502,
            )
            return

        # The connect succeeded; that's the last thing a 10-second
        # timeout is the right bound for. From here the hub is a
        # pass-through: the playground's own handlers own the timeout
        # (INPAINT_TIMEOUT = 180s in the inpaint playground, plus
        # margins; other playgrounds define their own). Any finite
        # hub-side timeout would either be too short and cut off a
        # legitimate slow response (the bug this fixes) or too long
        # and duplicate the playground's own deadline. Let the
        # playground be the sole authority.
        backend.settimeout(None)

        try:
            headers = dict(self.headers.items())
            headers["Host"] = f"{HUB_HOST}:{reg.port}"
            headers["Connection"] = "close"
            forward_with_query = (
                forward_path + ("?" + query if query else "")
            )
            req = f"{self.command} {forward_with_query} HTTP/1.1\r\n"
            for k, v in headers.items():
                req += f"{k}: {v}\r\n"
            req += "\r\n"
            backend.sendall(req.encode("utf-8"))

            content_len = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0") or "0")
            if content_len > 0:
                remaining = content_len
                while remaining > 0:
                    chunk = self.rfile.read(min(remaining, 65536))
                    if not chunk:
                        break
                    backend.sendall(chunk)
                    remaining -= len(chunk)

            while True:
                chunk = backend.recv(65536)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                self.wfile.write(chunk)
                self.wfile.flush()
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            try:
                backend.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
            self.close_connection = True

    # ---- WS proxy ----------------------------------------------------

    def _proxy_ws(self, path):
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        query = parsed.query
        resolved = self._resolve_proxy_target(path)
        if resolved is None:
            self.send_error(404, f"unknown playground: {path}")
            return
        name, forward_path = resolved
        reg = _HUB.find(name)
        if reg is None:
            self.send_error(404, f"unknown playground: {name}")
            return

        try:
            backend = socket.create_connection(
                (HUB_HOST, reg.port), timeout=10
            )
        except OSError as e:
            self.send_error(502, f"playground {name} unreachable: {e}")
            return

        try:
            headers = dict(self.headers.items())
            headers["Host"] = f"{HUB_HOST}:{reg.port}"
            forward_with_query = (
                forward_path + ("?" + query if query else "")
            )
            req = f"GET {forward_with_query} HTTP/1.1\r\n"
            for k, v in headers.items():
                req += f"{k}: {v}\r\n"
            req += "\r\n"
            backend.sendall(req.encode("utf-8"))

            response = b""
            while b"\r\n\r\n" not in response:
                chunk = backend.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    return
                response += chunk

            self.connection.sendall(response)

            client = self.connection
            client.setblocking(False)
            backend.setblocking(False)

            while True:
                try:
                    r, _, _ = select.select([client, backend], [], [], None)
                except (OSError, ValueError):
                    return
                for s in r:
                    try:
                        data = s.recv(65536)
                    except OSError:
                        return
                    if not data:
                        return
                    other = backend if s is client else client
                    try:
                        other.sendall(data)
                    except OSError:
                        return
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            try:
                backend.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
            self.close_connection = True


# ============================================================================
#  Kill
# ============================================================================

def _kill_playground(name, hard):
    reg = _HUB.find(name)
    if reg is None:
        return {"success": False, "message": f"no such playground: {name}"}

    if reg.role == "panel":
        return {"success": False,
                "message": f"{name} is a panel; "
                           f"kill the PID from the shell if it hangs"}

    group = reg.group
    group_count = 0
    group_msg = ""
    if group is not None:
        with _HUB.lock:
            group_count = sum(
                1 for r in _HUB.registrations.values()
                if r.group == group
            )
        group_msg = f" (group '{group}', {group_count} playgrounds)"

    def _ok(verb):
        if group is not None:
            return {"success": True,
                    "message": f"{verb} group '{group}' "
                               f"({group_count} playgrounds)"}
        return {"success": True, "message": f"{name} {verb}"}

    try:
        reg.send({"type": "shutdown", "request_id": uuid.uuid4().hex})
    except OSError as e:
        if hard and reg.pid and _verify_pid(reg.pid, name):
            try:
                os.kill(reg.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
                time.sleep(0.5)
                _HUB.deregister(name)
                return _ok("force-killed")
            except OSError as e2:
                return {"success": False,
                        "message": f"send failed: {e}; hard failed: {e2}"}
        return {"success": False, "message": f"send failed: {e}"}

    deadline = time.time() + 5.0
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if not _HUB.has(name):
            return _ok("shut down")
        time.sleep(0.1)

    if hard and reg.pid and _verify_pid(reg.pid, name):
        try:
            os.kill(reg.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            if _HUB.has(name):
                _HUB.deregister(name)
            return _ok("force-killed")
        except OSError as e:
            return {"success": False, "message": f"hard kill failed: {e}"}

    return {"success": False,
            "message": f"{name}{group_msg} did not shut down within 5s "
                       f"(use hard=1 to escalate)"}


def _shutdown_hub(notify_registrations=True):
    """Exit the hub process.

    When `notify_registrations` is True (the default, and what
    `pgkit.hub --shutdown` triggers), every registered playground
    receives a `shutdown` message, which its client handler turns
    into `os._exit(0)`. This is the historical behaviour, appropriate
    for an explicit user-driven stop.

    When False (`POST /__shutdown?quiet=1`, what the auto-restart
    uses), registered playgrounds are left running. They lose their
    WS connection to the hub, and their reconnect loops pick up the
    freshly-spawned hub within a second or two. Siblings survive a
    restart that was not addressed to them.
    """
    if notify_registrations:
        with _HUB.lock:
            regs = list(_HUB.registrations.values())
            panels = list(_HUB.panel_socks)
        for reg in regs:
            try:
                reg.send({"type": "shutdown",
                          "request_id": uuid.uuid4().hex})
            except OSError:
                pass
        for sock in panels:
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
        time.sleep(0.5)
    os._exit(0)


# ============================================================================
#  Entry point
# ============================================================================

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pgkit.hub")
    parser.add_argument("--host", default=HUB_HOST)
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=HUB_PORT)
    parser.add_argument("--shutdown", action="store_true",
                        help="Ask a running hub to exit.")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.shutdown:
        try:
            import urllib.request
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                f"http://{args.host}:{args.port}/__shutdown",
                method="POST", data=b"{}",
            )
            urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
            print(f"Hub on {args.host}:{args.port} shutdown requested.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"No hub on {args.host}:{args.port} ({e}).")
        return

    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((args.host, args.port), Handler)
    print(f"pgkit hub listening on http://{args.host}:{args.port}")
    print(f"  registrations : ws://{args.host}:{args.port}/__hub_ws")
    print(f"  playgrounds   : http://{args.host}:{args.port}/__playgrounds")
    print(f"  hash          : {short_hash()}")
    print(f"  proxied       : /<name>/* → localhost:<port>/*")
    sys.stdout.flush()

    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nStopped.")
    finally:
        httpd.server_close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""pgkit.hub_client — playground-side registration client.

    conn = ensure_running("board", 8770,
                          html_file="board_playground.html")
    # ... continue; conn runs in a background thread, keeps the WS
    #     connection to the hub alive, and exits the process if the
    #     hub sends a cooperative-shutdown request.

    conn = ensure_running("remote_panel", 8772, role="panel",
                          html_file="remote_panel.html")
    # ... same, but registers as `role="panel"` instead of
    #     `role="playground"`. Panels cannot be killed cooperatively
    #     (see hub.py, _kill_playground), and are filtered out of the
    #     playground dropdown in remote_panel/rp_client.py.

    conn = ensure_running("board", 8770,
                          html_file="board_playground.html",
                          group="core")
    # ... same as the first form, but the registration carries the
    #     group name.  Groups are metadata, not routing; see the
    #     GROUPS section in pgkit/hub.py.

    conn = ensure_running("core", 0,
                          role="launcher", group="core",
                          message_handler=on_cmd)
    # ... a launcher's control channel.  The hub stores this as a
    #     registration whose `available` field is a list of names the
    #     launcher can start; panels use it to send launcher_start /
    #     launcher_stop / launcher_restart commands, which the hub
    #     forwards to this WS.  `message_handler` receives those
    #     commands; the launcher replies via `conn.send(...)`.
    #     Playgrounds still register individually, exactly as before.

`html_file` is the playground's own `kit_serve(html_file=...)` value.
It travels to the hub in the `hello` frame and to panels in every
`playgrounds` event, so remote_panel can build an Open URL without a
hardcoded filename map.

`group` is optional and defaults to None.  Standalone launchers pass
nothing; the shared-process launcher (`pgkit/launcher.py`) passes the
group name so every playground it starts joins the same group.  A
`None` group behaves exactly as before this field was added.

`message_handler` is optional.  When set, every WS message the hub
sends that is not `hello_ack` or `shutdown` is passed to it as a dict
(see `HubConnection._handle`).  The launcher uses this to receive
launcher_* commands; playgrounds and panels leave it None.

`HubConnection.send(msg)` sends an arbitrary JSON message back over
the same WS.  Playgrounds never call it; the launcher uses it to push
`launcher_state` (available names) and `launcher_result` (per-command
replies).

DETACHED HUB SPAWN
==================
If no hub is listening on the configured port, this module spawns
`python -m pgkit.hub` with `start_new_session=True` so killing the
playground's terminal does not kill the hub. Duplicate spawns are
tolerated: whichever hub binds the port first wins; the other exits
silently and its playground's WS client connects to the live one.

STALE HUB DETECTION
===================
A hub process loaded from one version of `pgkit/hub.py` cannot pick
up edits to that file without a restart — Python does not reload
already-imported modules. Historically this left a footgun: a
developer edits `hub.py`, starts a playground, the playground
connects to the still-running old hub, and the mismatch surfaces much
later as an obscure protocol error. The fix was always
`pgkit.hub --shutdown`, but remembering to run it is exactly the kind
of step that gets forgotten three times in a row.

Before deciding a running hub is usable, `_spawn_hub_if_needed`
probes `GET /__hash` and compares the hub's advertised source hash
against this process's own. On a mismatch the client POSTs
`/__shutdown?quiet=1` — quiet, so already-connected siblings are
left to reconnect to the fresh hub rather than being killed — waits
for the port to die, and falls through to the normal spawn path.
The whole check runs under a module-level lock so that, in a
launcher spawning six playgrounds at once, only the first thread
pays the restart cost; the other five block on the lock and wake to
find a fresh hub already running.

Two upgrade caveats:

  · A hub that predates `/__hash` returns 404. The client treats
    that as "stale" and forces one restart. After that every hub
    advertises the endpoint, so the 404 path fires exactly once.

  · A hub that predates `/__shutdown?quiet=1` (but has `/__hash`,
    if that combination somehow arises) ignores the query string and
    performs the historical loud shutdown, killing its siblings on
    the first auto-restart. From then on, quiet is honoured.

FRAMES ARE UNMASKED
===================
This is a private protocol between our own hub and our own
playgrounds. `pgkit.ws.read_frame` accepts unmasked client frames, so
we skip the masking step that RFC 6455 would require for third-party
servers. The hub only ever accepts frames from us.
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

from . import ws as _ws


HUB_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
HUB_PORT = 8780


# Serialises the freshness check and the restart it may trigger across
# every HubConnection instance in this process. See "STALE HUB
# DETECTION" in the module docstring.
_restart_lock = threading.Lock()


# ============================================================================
#  Public entry point
# ============================================================================

def ensure_running(playground_name, playground_port, *,
                   role="playground",
                   html_file=None,
                   group=None,
                   hub_port=HUB_PORT,
                   connect_timeout=10.0,
                   message_handler=None):
    """Return a live HubConnection registered with the hub.

    See the module docstring for the roles and the extra kwargs.
    """
    conn = HubConnection(playground_name, playground_port,
                         hub_port, role=role, html_file=html_file,
                         group=group, message_handler=message_handler)
    conn.start(timeout=connect_timeout)
    return conn


# ============================================================================
#  Connection
# ============================================================================

class HubConnection:
    def __init__(self, name, port, hub_port, role="playground",
                 html_file=None, group=None, message_handler=None):
        self.name = name
        self.port = port
        self.hub_port = hub_port
        self.role = role
        self.html_file = html_file
        self.group = group
        self.message_handler = message_handler
        self.hub_url = f"http://{HUB_HOST}:{hub_port}/{name}/"
        self.stop = threading.Event()
        self.registered = threading.Event()
        self.thread = None
        self._sock = None
        self._sock_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._log_prefix = f"[hub_client:{name}]"

    def start(self, timeout=10.0):
        self._spawn_hub_if_needed()
        self.thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._run, name=f"hub-client-{self.name}", daemon=True
        )
        self.thread.start()
        if not self.registered.wait(timeout):
            print(f"{self._log_prefix} registration timed out "
                  f"after {timeout:.0f}s", file=sys.stderr)

    def stop_now(self):
        """Stop the connection loop. Closes the underlying socket so a
        blocked `read_frame` returns immediately."""
        self.stop.set()
        with self._sock_lock:
            sock = self._sock
            self._sock = None
        if sock is not None:
            try:
                sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
            except OSError:
                pass
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

    def send(self, msg):
        """Send one JSON message over the registration WS.

        Returns True if the frame was written, False otherwise.  The
        launcher uses this to push `launcher_state` and
        `launcher_result`; playgrounds and panels never call it.
        """
        with self._sock_lock:
            sock = self._sock
        if sock is None:
            return False
        try:
            _ws.write_text_frame(sock, json.dumps(msg))
            return True
        except OSError:
            return False

    # ---- hub spawn ---------------------------------------------------

    def _hub_reachable(self):
        try:
            s = socket.create_connection(
                (HUB_HOST, self.hub_port), timeout=0.5
            )
            s.close()
            return True
        except OSError:
            return False

    def _hub_matches_local_source(self) -> bool:
        """True iff the running hub was loaded from the same pgkit
        source as this process. See "STALE HUB DETECTION" in the
        module docstring.

        Return values:
          · True  — hashes match, or we could not reach the endpoint
                    to ask (transient error, or 5xx — a healthy hub
                    that happens to answer a probe badly should not
                    be restarted).
          · False — hashes differ, or the hub answered 404 (a hub
                    predating `/__hash`, cannot prove freshness,
                    treat as stale).
        """
        from ._source_hash import source_hash
        local = source_hash()
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(
                f"http://{HUB_HOST}:{self.hub_port}/__hash", timeout=2
            ) as r:
                body = json.loads(r.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            if e.code == 404:
                return False
            return True
        except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError):
            return True
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            return True
        return body.get("source_hash") == local

    def _restart_stale_hub(self) -> None:
        """POST /__shutdown?quiet=1 and wait for the port to die.

        On a hub that honours `quiet=1`, registered playgrounds are
        left to reconnect. On a hub that predates the parameter (the
        first auto-restart after upgrading to this client), the query
        string is ignored, and existing siblings are killed. That is
        a one-time cost of the transition, not an ongoing property.
        """
        from ._source_hash import short_hash
        print(f"{self._log_prefix} hub at :{self.hub_port} is running "
              f"stale code; restarting (local hash {short_hash()})",
              file=sys.stderr)
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                f"http://{HUB_HOST}:{self.hub_port}/__shutdown?quiet=1",
                method="POST", data=b"{}",
            )
            urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=2).read()
        except Exception:
            pass
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5.0
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if not self._hub_reachable():
                return
            time.sleep(0.1)
        print(f"{self._log_prefix} warning: hub at :{self.hub_port} "
              f"did not shut down within 5s; still running stale code",
              file=sys.stderr)

    def _spawn_hub_if_needed(self):
        if self._hub_reachable():
            with _restart_lock:
                if not self._hub_matches_local_source():
                    self._restart_stale_hub()
        time.sleep(0.1)
        if self._hub_reachable():
            return

        pgkit_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
        log_path = Path.home() / ".pgkit" / "hub.log"
        log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        env = os.environ.copy()
        prev = env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
        env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
            str(pgkit_root) + (os.pathsep + prev if prev else "")
        )
        try:
            with open(log_path, "a") as log:
                subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-m", "pgkit.hub",
                     "--port", str(self.hub_port)],
                    start_new_session=True,
                    stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                    env=env,
                )
            print(f"{self._log_prefix} spawned hub, log at {log_path}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{self._log_prefix} could not spawn hub: {e}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return
        deadline = time.time() + 5.0
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if self._hub_reachable():
                return
            time.sleep(0.1)
        try:
            tail = log_path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()[-10:]
            if tail:
                print(f"{self._log_prefix} hub log tail:", file=sys.stderr)
                for line in tail:
                    print(f"  {line}", file=sys.stderr)
        except OSError:
            pass

    # ---- connection loop ---------------------------------------------

    def _run(self):
        backoff = 1.0
        while not self.stop.is_set():
            try:
                self._connect_and_serve()
                backoff = 1.0
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"{self._log_prefix} {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            if self.stop.is_set():
                return
            time.sleep(backoff)
            backoff = min(backoff * 2, 30.0)

    def _connect_and_serve(self):
        sock = socket.create_connection(
            (HUB_HOST, self.hub_port), timeout=10
        )
        with self._sock_lock:
            self._sock = sock
        try:
            key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(16)).decode("ascii")
            upgrade = (
                f"GET /__hub_ws HTTP/1.1\r\n"
                f"Host: {HUB_HOST}:{self.hub_port}\r\n"
                f"Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
                f"Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
                f"Sec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\n"
                f"Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n"
                f"\r\n"
            ).encode("ascii")
            sock.sendall(upgrade)

            response = b""
            while b"\r\n\r\n" not in response:
                chunk = sock.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    raise ConnectionError("hub closed during handshake")
                response += chunk
            first_line = response.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0]
            if b"101" not in first_line:
                raise ConnectionError(
                    f"hub refused upgrade: {first_line!r}"
                )

            hello = {
                "type": "hello",
                "role": self.role,
                "name": self.name,
                "port": self.port,
                "pid":  os.getpid(),
            }
            if self.html_file:
                hello["html_file"] = self.html_file
            if self.group:
                hello["group"] = self.group
            _ws.write_text_frame(sock, json.dumps(hello))

            sock.settimeout(None)
            while not self.stop.is_set():
                opcode, payload = _ws.read_frame(sock)
                if opcode is None or opcode == 0x08:
                    raise ConnectionError("hub closed connection")
                if opcode != 0x01:
                    continue
                try:
                    msg = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if not self._handle(msg, sock):
                    return
        finally:
            with self._sock_lock:
                if self._sock is sock:
                    self._sock = None
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

    def _handle(self, msg, sock):
        t = msg.get("type")
        if t == "hello_ack":
            self.registered.set()
            print(f"{self._log_prefix} registered "
                  f"(role={self.role}, hub {HUB_HOST}:{self.hub_port})",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return True
        if t == "shutdown":
            try:
                _ws.write_text_frame(
                    sock,
                    json.dumps({"type": "shutdown_ack",
                                "request_id": msg.get("request_id", "")}),
                )
            except OSError:
                pass
            threading.Timer(0.2, lambda: os._exit(0)).start()
            self.stop.set()
            return False
        if self.message_handler is not None:
            try:
                self.message_handler(msg)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"{self._log_prefix} message_handler error: {e}",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        return True

"""
pgkit.js_check — syntax-check a JS module before serving it.

`check_js(source, label)` writes `source` to a temp file and runs
`node --check` on it.  The temp file gets `.mjs` suffix so node
parses `import`/`export` as ES module syntax; a `.js` suffix would
require `--experimental-modules` on older nodes.

Non-tool failures (node missing, subprocess error, timeout) do not
raise — the check is a diagnostic, not a build requirement.

CACHE
=====
`node --check` is a subprocess, and every playground runs it once per
JS module at page-build time.  In the shared-process launcher this is
~120–240 subprocess spawns per `run_all.py` invocation — several
seconds of wall clock, dwarfing the interpreter-startup savings that
justify the shared process in the first place.

The cache eliminates that cost on every run after the first (or after
any JS source edit).  Each entry is keyed by::

    sha256(
        cache_version,
        sys.platform,
        node_path,
        node_version,
        source,
    )

and stored as a small JSON file under `~/.pgkit/js_check_cache/`.
A cache hit is a fast file read (~50 µs); a cache miss is the full
`node --check` subprocess (100–300 ms).  On a warm cache, the whole
`run_all.py` startup shaves several seconds.

The cache invalidates automatically when the source changes, the
node binary moves or is upgraded, or the platform changes (a
`node --check` that succeeded on one OS can fail on another only
pathologically, but the extra safety costs one line of hash input).

Two environment variables affect behavior:

    PGKIT_NO_JS_CACHE=1     disable the cache entirely (always
                            re-run `node --check`).  Use this if you
                            suspect a stale cache entry.
    PGKIT_JS_CACHE_DIR=…    relocate the cache directory.  Useful
                            when sharing a scratch directory across
                            checkouts, or isolating it in CI.

Cached failures replay verbatim — same `JsSyntaxError` with the same
lineno, message, and raw output.  The raw output has the ephemeral
temp path rewritten to the module label so the entry is portable
across runs and does not point at a file the OS has deleted.

The cache is a dev artifact.  Entries are ~200 B for a success and
~1 KB for a failure; even 10,000 entries stay under ~2 MB.  There is
no evictor.  If it ever matters, `rm -rf ~/.pgkit/js_check_cache/`
is the fallback.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional


_LINENO_RE = re.compile(r'^(.+?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?$')


class JsSyntaxError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, label: str, lineno: Optional[int],
                 message: str, raw: str):
        self.label = label
        self.lineno = lineno
        self.message = message
        self.raw = raw
        loc = f"{label}:{lineno}" if lineno is not None else label
        super().__init__(f"{loc}: {message}")


# ============================================================================
#  Node discovery (cached per process)
# ============================================================================

_node_path: Optional[str] = None
_node_path_set = False

def _get_node() -> Optional[str]:
    global _node_path, _node_path_set
    if not _node_path_set:
        _node_path = shutil.which("node")
        _node_path_set = True
    return _node_path


_node_version: Optional[str] = None
_node_version_set = False

def _get_node_version(node_path: str) -> Optional[str]:
    global _node_version, _node_version_set
    if not _node_version_set:
        _node_version_set = True
        try:
            _node_version = subprocess.check_output(
                [node_path, "--version"], text=True, timeout=2,
            ).strip()
        except Exception:
            _node_version = None
    return _node_version


# ============================================================================
#  Cache directory + key
# ============================================================================

_CACHE_VERSION = "1"

def _cache_enabled() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("PGKIT_NO_JS_CACHE", "").lower() not in (
        "1", "true", "yes",
    )

def _cache_dir() -> Path:
    override = os.environ.get("PGKIT_JS_CACHE_DIR")
    if override:
        return Path(override).expanduser()
    return Path.home() / ".pgkit" / "js_check_cache"


def _cache_key(node_path: str, node_version: Optional[str],
               source: str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    h.update(_CACHE_VERSION.encode("ascii"))
    h.update(b"\0")
    h.update(sys.platform.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
    h.update(b"\0")
    h.update(node_path.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
    h.update(b"\0")
    h.update((node_version or "").encode("utf-8", "replace"))
    h.update(b"\0")
    h.update(source.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
    return h.hexdigest()


def _load_cache(key: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    if not _cache_enabled():
        return None
    try:
        with open(_cache_dir() / (key + ".json"),
                  "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None


def _store_cache(key: str, value: dict) -> None:
    if not _cache_enabled():
        return
    d = _cache_dir()
    try:
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError:
        return
    fd = None
    tmp_path = None
    try:
        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
            dir=str(d), prefix=key + "-", suffix=".json",
        )
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(value, f)
        fd = None  # closed by the context manager
        os.replace(tmp_path, d / (key + ".json"))
        tmp_path = None
    except OSError:
        pass
    finally:
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            except OSError:
                pass
        if tmp_path is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp_path)
            except OSError:
                pass


# ============================================================================
#  The public check
# ============================================================================

def check_js(source: str, *, label: str = "bundle") -> None:
    """Raise JsSyntaxError if `source` is not valid JS module source."""
    node = _get_node()
    if node is None:
        _warn_once(
            "pgkit.js_check: `node` not found on PATH — "
            "skipping JS syntax check. Install node to enable it.",
        )
        return

    version = _get_node_version(node)
    key = _cache_key(node, version, source)

    cached = _load_cache(key)
    if cached is not None:
        if cached.get("ok"):
            return
        raise JsSyntaxError(
            label,
            cached.get("lineno"),
            cached.get("message", "syntax error"),
            cached.get("raw", ""),
        )

    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".mjs", prefix="pgkit_check_")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(source)
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [node, "--check", path],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10.0,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            _warn_once(
                f"pgkit.js_check: `node --check` timed out for {label}",
            )
            return
        except OSError as e:
            _warn_once(
                f"pgkit.js_check: could not run node for {label}: {e}",
            )
            return

        if proc.returncode == 0:
            _store_cache(key, {"ok": True})
            return

        raw = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "").strip()
        # The temp path changes on every invocation; rewrite it to the
        # module label so a cached failure is portable across runs and
        # does not point a reader at a file the OS has already deleted.
        display_label = label or "source"
        if path:
            raw = raw.replace(path, display_label)
        lineno = _parse_lineno(raw)
        message = _parse_message(raw) or f"syntax error in {label}"
        _store_cache(key, {
            "ok":      False,
            "lineno":  lineno,
            "message": message,
            "raw":     raw,
        })
        raise JsSyntaxError(label, lineno, message, raw)
    finally:
        try:
            os.unlink(path)
        except OSError:
            pass


# ============================================================================
#  Helpers (unchanged)
# ============================================================================

def _parse_lineno(raw: str) -> Optional[int]:
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        m = _LINENO_RE.match(line.strip())
        if m:
            try:
                return int(m.group(2))
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return None


def _parse_message(raw: str) -> str:
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("SyntaxError:"):
            return s
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            return line.strip()
    return ""


_warned: set = set()


def _warn_once(msg: str) -> None:
    if msg in _warned:
        return
    _warned.add(msg)
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
```

```python
"""
pgkit.launcher — multi-playground launcher.

Run several playgrounds in one Python process.  Each keeps its own
HTTP+WS server, its own `/modules/` manifest, its own per-playground
`pgkit.remote_hub.Hub` for `/remote`, and its own hub registration.

THE SHARED-PROCESS MODEL
========================
Six playgrounds, one interpreter, one Ctrl+C:

    python playgrounds/run_all.py

Every playground was refactored into a package (`board`, `cone`,
..., `text_wall`) and every internal import became relative, so two
`pg_base` files coexist as two distinct modules.  Failure coupling
is the accepted trade-off: a crash in one playground takes down the
whole group; cooperative kill of one member kills the whole group.
That is the intended behavior and is surfaced by the hub and by the
interactive panel.

NON-BLOCKING SERVE
==================
`Launcher.start` uses `pgkit.server.serve_nonblocking` per playground,
which returns an `httpd` and a `hub_conn` WITHOUT starting
`serve_forever`.  The launcher threads each `serve_forever` and owns
the shutdown path.  `Launcher.stop` reverses it: `httpd.shutdown()`,
`httpd.server_close()`, `hub_conn.stop_now()`, join the thread,
forget the entry.  Start/stop can be called repeatedly at runtime.

LAUNCHER HUB CHANNEL
====================
On init, the launcher opens a *second* WS to the hub, tagged
`role="launcher"`, `name=<group>`, `group=<group>`.  This is the
control channel for the panel.  It stays up for the launcher's
lifetime, even when zero playgrounds are running.

The launcher pushes `launcher_state` messages carrying `available`
(the full descriptor list) on every start/stop and after initial
registration.  The hub broadcasts that to panels.

The launcher also receives `launcher_start` / `launcher_stop` /
`launcher_restart` messages on this channel, forwarded from panels
by the hub.  It handles them in-process and replies with
`launcher_result`, which the hub relays back to the sending panel.

INTERACTIVE MODE
================
`run_all.py -i` drives a `Launcher` from a REPL: `start <name>` /
`stop <name>` / `restart <name>`.  Same Launcher, same process, same
group.  Fixed-set mode (`serve_group`) is the non-interactive
counterpart: it starts the initial set, blocks, then shuts down.
"""

import signal
import sys
import threading

from .server import serve_nonblocking


# ============================================================================
#  Launcher
# ============================================================================

class Launcher:
    """Own the lifecycle of a set of playgrounds in one process.

    `Launcher(group, descriptors)` builds the playground map and
    opens the launcher control channel.  `start(name)` and `stop(name)`
    add/remove one playground; both are safe at any time.
    `install_signal_handlers()` wires SIGINT/SIGTERM to `trigger_shutdown`.
    `wait()` blocks until shutdown is signalled.
    """

    def __init__(self, group, playgrounds, *, open_browser=False,
                 enable_hub_control=True):
        self.group = group
        self._order = [p["name"] for p in playgrounds]
        self._playgrounds = {p["name"]: p for p in playgrounds}
        self._running = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._open_browser = open_browser
        self._shutdown_event = threading.Event()
        self._signals_installed = False

        self._launcher_ws = None
        self._launcher_ws_ready = threading.Event()
        if enable_hub_control:
            try:
                self._open_launcher_ws()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  launcher control channel unavailable: {e}",
                      file=sys.stderr)

    # ---- launcher hub channel ----------------------------------------

    def _open_launcher_ws(self):
        from .hub_client import ensure_running
        self._launcher_ws = ensure_running(
            self.group,               # name = group name
            0,                        # port not meaningful for launcher
            role="launcher",
            group=self.group,
            message_handler=self._on_launcher_message,
            connect_timeout=5.0,
        )
        self._launcher_ws_ready.set()
        self._push_launcher_state()

    def _on_launcher_message(self, msg):
        t = msg.get("type")
        target = msg.get("name") or ""
        request_id = msg.get("request_id") or ""
        result = {
            "type":       "launcher_result",
            "request_id": request_id,
            "name":       target,
            "success":    False,
            "message":    "",
        }

        if t == "launcher_start":
            url = self.start(target)
            result["success"] = url is not None
            result["message"] = (
                f"started {target}: {url}" if url
                else f"could not start {target}"
            )
        elif t == "launcher_stop":
            ok = self.stop(target)
            result["success"] = ok
            result["message"] = (
                f"stopped {target}" if ok
                else f"{target} not running"
            )
        elif t == "launcher_restart":
            self.stop(target)
            url = self.start(target)
            result["success"] = url is not None
            result["message"] = (
                f"restarted {target}: {url}" if url
                else f"could not restart {target}"
            )
        else:
            return

        if self._launcher_ws is not None:
            self._launcher_ws.send(result)
        self._push_launcher_state()

    def _push_launcher_state(self):
        if self._launcher_ws is None:
            return
        self._launcher_ws.send({
            "type":      "launcher_state",
            "available": list(self._order),
        })

    # ---- inspection --------------------------------------------------

    def names(self):
        return list(self._order)

    def running(self):
        with self._lock:
            return {n: self._running[n]["url"] for n in self._running}

    def is_running(self, name):
        with self._lock:
            return name in self._running

    # ---- lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------

    def start(self, name):
        desc = self._playgrounds.get(name)
        if desc is None:
            return None
        with self._lock:
            if name in self._running:
                return self._running[name]["url"]

        try:
            httpd, hub_conn, url = serve_nonblocking(
                port            = desc["port"],
                html_file       = desc["html_file"],
                html_render     = desc["html_render"],
                routes          = desc.get("routes") or {},
                raw_routes      = desc.get("raw_routes") or {},
                module_sources  = desc.get("module_sources") or {},
                hub_name        = name,
                hub_role        = "playground",
                group           = self.group,
                open_browser    = self._open_browser,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  [{name}] FAILED to start: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return None

        t = threading.Thread(
            target=httpd.serve_forever,
            name=f"serve-{name}",
            daemon=True,
        )
        t.start()
        with self._lock:
            self._running[name] = {
                "httpd":    httpd,
                "hub_conn": hub_conn,
                "thread":   t,
                "url":      url,
            }
        print(f"  [{name}] {url}")
        self._push_launcher_state()
        return url

    def stop(self, name):
        with self._lock:
            entry = self._running.pop(name, None)
        if entry is None:
            return False

        try:
            entry["httpd"].shutdown()
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            entry["httpd"].server_close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        if entry["hub_conn"] is not None:
            try:
                entry["hub_conn"].stop_now()
            except Exception:
                pass
        t = entry["thread"]
        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
            t.join(timeout=2.0)
        print(f"  [{name}] stopped")
        self._push_launcher_state()
        return True

    def start_all(self):
        for name in self._order:
            if not self.is_running(name):
                self.start(name)

    def stop_all(self):
        with self._lock:
            names = list(self._running.keys())
        for name in names:
            self.stop(name)

    # ---- shutdown coordination ---------------------------------------

    def install_signal_handlers(self):
        if self._signals_installed:
            return
        self._signals_installed = True

        def _on_signal(signum, frame):
            print(f"\n  Signal {signum} received, shutting down...")
            self.trigger_shutdown()

        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _on_signal)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _on_signal)

    def trigger_shutdown(self):
        self._shutdown_event.set()

    def wait(self):
        self._shutdown_event.wait()


# ============================================================================
#  serve_group — fixed-set entry point
# ============================================================================

def serve_group(group, playgrounds, *, open_browser=False, only=None):
    """Start every playground in `playgrounds` (or `only`) in one
    process, block until Ctrl+C, then shut down.

    Panel-side "Stop" and "Start" buttons still work in this mode,
    because the launcher control channel is always open.  Only the
    *starting set* is fixed; runtime start/stop of individual
    members is available via the panel either way.
    """
    launcher = Launcher(group, playgrounds, open_browser=open_browser)
    initial = (list(only) if only is not None
               else [p["name"] for p in playgrounds])
    for name in initial:
        launcher.start(name)

    if not launcher.running():
        print("No playgrounds started.", file=sys.stderr)
        return

    print(f"All {len(launcher.running())} playgrounds in group "
          f"'{group}' are running.")
    print("  Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
    launcher.install_signal_handlers()
    try:
        launcher.wait()
    finally:
        launcher.stop_all()
        print("Stopped.")

"""
pgkit.lint — static check for ES-module import/export consistency.

For every `.py` file in a playground project, extract its JS source
and verify that every `import { a, b } from "./x.js"` names symbols
that `x.py` actually exports.  Catches the ES-module pitfall where
the browser refuses to hand the module to any importer, the module
graph aborts, and the page loads as a shell.

USAGE
=====
    cd playgrounds/
    python -m pgkit.lint cable/

or from inside a project:

    cd playgrounds/cable/
    PYTHONPATH=.. python -m pgkit.lint .

The pgkit package directory is looked up as a sibling of the
argument directory (or the parent of `.`) when `--pgkit` is not given.

WHAT IT CHECKS
==============
    · imports whose target module doesn't exist in the scanned set
    · imports naming symbols their target module doesn't export
    · (both static `import { ... }` and top-of-file `export { ... }`
      lists are parsed; `export *` and `export { X as Y }` patterns
      are not currently handled and will appear as "target not
      found" — a known limitation)

WHAT IT DOESN'T CHECK
=====================
    · `no-undef` — unreferenced identifiers.  Not implemented;
      depends on ESLint being on PATH which isn't a dependency of
      pgkit.
    · runtime behavior — this is a static analysis pass, not a test.

GENERATED MODULES
=================
`pg_geometry.js` (in cable) and `bx_geometry.js` (in boxes) are
baked at render time by `_build_module_sources(geom)` and do not
exist as `.py` files.  The linter knows about these two by name and
treats them as "present" without checking their exports — they are
trivially correct by construction (`export const GEOMETRY = …`).

Any future generated module must be added to `_GENERATED_MODULES`
here, or the linter will emit a false positive.

SELF-EXCLUSION
==============
`pgkit/lint.py` contains docstring examples of the form

    import { a, b } from "./x.js"

which the import regex would match if `lint.py` were scanned as a
source module.  `lint.py` is therefore excluded from the pgkit scan
by name — it is a Python-side tool, not a JS source, and any
`import` line inside it is documentation, not runtime.
"""

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    r'import\s*\{([^}]+)\}\s*from\s*["\'](\./[^"\']+)["\']'
)
_EXPORT_PATTERNS = [
    re.compile(r'\bexport\s+(?:async\s+)?function\s+(\w+)'),
    re.compile(r'\bexport\s+function\s*\*\s*(\w+)'),
    re.compile(r'\bexport\s+(?:const|let|var)\s+(\w+)'),
    re.compile(r'\bexport\s+class\s+(\w+)'),
]
_EXPORT_LIST_RE = re.compile(r'\bexport\s*\{\s*([^}]+)\s*\}')

# Modules generated at build time by _build_module_sources() — treated
# as present, exports not checked.  Any future generated module must
# be listed here.
_GENERATED_MODULES = {
    "pg_geometry.js",
    "bx_geometry.js",
}

# Python files under pgkit/ that are tools, not JS source.  Their
# contents are skipped during the pgkit scan.
_PGKIT_SKIP = {"__init__.py", "lint.py"}


def _parse(text):
    imports = []
    exports = []
    for m in _IMPORT_RE.finditer(text):
        lineno = text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
        names = set()
        for raw in m.group(1).split(","):
            raw = raw.strip()
            if raw:
                names.add(raw.split()[0])
        imports.append((lineno, m.group(2), names))
    for pat in _EXPORT_PATTERNS:
        for m in pat.finditer(text):
            lineno = text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
            exports.append((lineno, m.group(1)))
    for m in _EXPORT_LIST_RE.finditer(text):
        lineno = text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
        for raw in m.group(1).split(","):
            raw = raw.strip()
            if raw:
                exports.append((lineno, raw.split()[0]))
    return imports, exports


def _index(project_dir, pgkit_dir):
    exports = {}
    imports = {}
    sources = {}

    for py in sorted(project_dir.glob("*.py")):
        mod = py.stem + ".js"
        text = py.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        imps, exps = _parse(text)
        exports[mod] = {name for _, name in exps}
        imports[mod] = imps
        sources[mod] = py

    if pgkit_dir and pgkit_dir.is_dir():
        for py in sorted(pgkit_dir.glob("*.py")):
            if py.name in _PGKIT_SKIP:
                continue
            mod = "pgkit/" + py.stem + ".js"
            text = py.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            imps, exps = _parse(text)
            exports[mod] = {name for _, name in exps}
            imports[mod] = imps
            sources[mod] = py

    return exports, imports, sources


def _resolve(source_mod, path):
    if path.startswith("./"):
        path = path[2:]
    if source_mod.startswith("pgkit/"):
        return "pgkit/" + path
    return path


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pgkit.lint")
    p.add_argument("project")
    p.add_argument("--pgkit", default=None)
    args = p.parse_args()

    project_dir = Path(args.project).resolve()
    if not project_dir.is_dir():
        print("not a directory: " + str(project_dir), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if args.pgkit:
        pgkit_dir = Path(args.pgkit).resolve()
    else:
        pgkit_dir = project_dir.parent / "pgkit"
        if not pgkit_dir.is_dir():
            pgkit_dir = None

    exports, imports, sources = _index(project_dir, pgkit_dir)

    errors = []
    for source_mod, imps in imports.items():
        for (lineno, path, names) in imps:
            target = _resolve(source_mod, path)
            if target in _GENERATED_MODULES:
                continue
            if target not in exports:
                errors.append((sources[source_mod], lineno,
                               path, "target not found"))
                continue
            for name in sorted(names):
                if name not in exports[target]:
                    errors.append((sources[source_mod], lineno,
                                   name, "not exported by " + target))

    print("import/export ", end="")
    if not errors:
        print("✓  (" + str(len(exports)) + " module(s))")
        return 0
    print("FAIL")
    for py, lineno, name, reason in errors:
        print("  " + str(py) + ":" + str(lineno))
        print("    " + name + " — " + reason)
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
