"""
pgkit.panel_core — flashStatus, log mirroring, and _installScrubInput,
as an ES module.

`flashStatus` and `_installScrubInput` are exported.  `_installScrubInput`
calls a `draw` callback on every value change; the callback is injected
at boot via `setPanelDraw(draw)`.  The previous inline `draw()` reference
relied on `draw` being a global, which is not true inside a module.

LOG MIRRORING
=============
Every playground is a terminal process.  When a browser-side error or
warning happens in a playground tab, the developer running the server
needs to see it without alt-tabbing to DevTools.  This module is the
single point where that forwarding happens.

Four kinds of browser-side event reach the terminal through here:

  * Panel errors — `flashStatus(msg, "bad")` writes the DOM status bar
    (unchanged behaviour) and also mirrors `msg` to the server.

  * Panel warnings — `flashStatus(msg, "warn")` mirrors too.  "warn"
    is used in this codebase for actionable diagnostics (mask dimension
    mismatch, mirror-disabled-during-expansion, empty context bbox)
    that a headless operator needs to see.

  * `console.error(...)` / `console.warn(...)` — the module overrides
    these at load, forwarding to the server while still calling the
    original so DevTools sees the message exactly as before.  This is
    what makes "boot catch blocks call console.error" reach the
    terminal, and what makes any direct `console.error` in playground
    code visible in the server's stdout.

  * Uncaught errors and unhandled rejections — installed via `window.
    addEventListener` hooks at load.

BOOT LOG MIRRORING — THE UNIFIED BOOT STANDARD
==============================================
Boot modules come in two shapes across the playgrounds:

  * Dynamic-import boots (`board`, `cone`, `boxes`): an async IIFE calls
    `await import(path)` in a loop, logging each step via
    `console.log("[boot]", ...)` and each failure via
    `console.error("[boot]", "FAIL", ...)`.

  * Static-import boots (`inpaint`, `multimask`, `interceptor`,
    `segment`, `text_boxes`, `text_wall`): imports are static, the
    body wraps its setup in a try/catch, and it logs success via
    `console.log("[boot] message")` and failure via
    `console.error("[boot] FAILED:", e)`.

Both shapes agree on one thing: **the literal token `[boot]` at the
start of the first console argument identifies a boot log line.** This
module exploits that to give both shapes identical mirroring behaviour
without any per-playground change:

  * Any `console.log` call whose first argument is exactly `"[boot]"`,
    or is a string starting with `"[boot] "`, is mirrored with class
    `"boot-ok"`.  This covers both forms — `console.log("[boot]", ...)`
    and `console.log("[boot] message")`.  The `[boot] ` prefix is
    stripped from the mirrored text because the class already says
    "boot-ok"; the terminal output is `[inpaint] boot-ok: starting`,
    not `[inpaint] boot-ok: [boot] starting`.

  * Any `console.error` call whose first argument is exactly `"[boot]"`,
    or is a string starting with `"[boot] "`, is mirrored with class
    `"boot-error"`, prefix stripped, same rationale.

  * Every other `console.log` / `console.error` call stays
    un-boot-classed: `console.log` is not mirrored at all (too noisy),
    `console.error` is mirrored as class `"console-error"` with its
    arguments passed through verbatim.

Why mirror boot *success* at all: a headless developer (Playwright,
Selenium, a `run_all.py` session with no browser tab) has no other
signal that boot completed.  The `[boot] BOOT COMPLETE` line, mirrored,
gives them the same per-step confirmation a browser developer reads in
DevTools.  Because the mirror is opt-in by tag, no per-playground
boot module needs to change — the mechanism is uniform across both
shapes.

Why separate `boot-ok` and `boot-error` classes rather than reusing
`console-error` for boot failures: a developer watching the terminal
gets a clean signal — anything tagged `boot-*` is a boot event, split
by success or failure.  Before this class existed, boot failures
appeared as `[prefix] console-error: [boot] FAIL import state → ...`
which was readable but forced the reader to parse the payload to know
it was a boot event.  Now success and failure are symmetric: `[prefix]
boot-ok: import state ok` / `[prefix] boot-error: FAIL import state
→ ...`.

The mirror target is `POST ./__log`, a built-in route installed
unconditionally by `pgkit/server.py::make_handler` on every playground.
The URL is *relative* to the page, not absolute — under the pgkit hub
the page lives at `/<name>/<name>.html`, so `./__log` resolves to
`/<name>/__log`, which the hub proxies back to that playground.  An
absolute `/__log` would hit the hub root where nothing handles it.

`document.title` supplies the prefix: `"Inpaint playground"` → `inpaint`,
`"Multimask"` → `multimask`, `"Remote panel"` → `remote`.  Matches each
server's own `_log("[...]")` convention, so a terminal running several
playgrounds under the hub stays readable.

The `console.error` / `console.warn` / `console.log` overrides are
*transparent*: the message still reaches DevTools in its original
form.  Only after the original call returns does the override POST the
message to the server.  This means an operator with a browser tab open
loses nothing, and an operator running headless gains the terminal
trace.

`console.log` is otherwise deliberately not mirrored.  It is used
pervasively for benign diagnostics (fetch timing, cache hits, dev
tracing); forwarding every `console.log` would flood the server's
stdout.  The `[boot]` tag is the only whitelisted case.

Opting out
==========
Three URL query parameters disable mirroring at three scopes.  The
broadest one wins — `pgkit_no_mirror=1` disables everything, including
the narrower two.

    ?pgkit_no_mirror=1         disable all mirroring: errors, warnings,
                               boot messages, console.error/warn, and
                               uncaught exceptions.

    ?pgkit_no_mirror_warn=1    silence warning-class mirroring only:
                               `flashStatus(..., "warn")` and
                               `console.warn(...)`.  Error mirroring,
                               boot mirroring, and uncaught-exception
                               mirroring stay on.

    ?pgkit_no_mirror_boot=1    silence boot-class mirroring only (the
                               `[boot]`-tagged `console.log` and
                               `console.error` paths).  Non-boot
                               console.error still mirrors; uncaught
                               exceptions still mirror via
                               `window.onerror`.

These use URL parameters rather than environment variables because
browser-side code cannot read the server's environment.  The knob is
per-page-load; closing the tab resets it.  Useful when debugging the
mirror itself, or when comparing page behaviour with the mirror on
versus off.

`reportPanelError(message, cls)` is the public explicit-report entry
point.  Used by `pgkit/remote_client.js` for remote-command failures,
and available to any playground that wants to mirror a message that
does not fit the status-bar lifecycle (e.g. a boot-time failure caught
before `flashStatus` is wired).

Recursion
=========
`_postLog` catches all errors internally and never throws, and its
fetch path never calls any overridden console method.  Each override's
mirror call is wrapped in try/catch.  Even if the mirror itself fails,
no further console method fires and no infinite loop is possible.

Multi-line messages
===================
A message that spans multiple lines — typically a stack trace — is
mirrored as one POST.  The server's `_handle_log` prints the first
line with a `[prefix] class:` tag and indents the rest by four spaces.
"""

export function _installScrubInput(el, opts) {

    if (!drag.moved) {
      if (Math.abs(dx) < SCRUB_DRAG_THRESHOLD) return;
      drag.moved = true;

    if (el.disabled) return;
    if (document.activeElement === el) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    drag = {
      startX: e.clientX,
      startValue: opts.read(),
      moved: false,
    };
    if (opts.onDragStart) opts.onDragStart(drag);
    window.addEventListener("mousemove", onMove);
    window.addEventListener("mouseup", onUp);
  });

  el.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
    if (e.key === "Enter") {
      e.preventDefault();
      const v = parseFloat(el.value);
      if (isFinite(v)) opts.write(v);
      el.blur();
      if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
    } else if (e.key === "Escape") {
      e.preventDefault();
      el.blur();
      if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
    }
  });

  el.addEventListener("blur", () => {
    const v = parseFloat(el.value);
    if (isFinite(v)) opts.write(v);
    if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
  });
}

```python
"""
pgkit.remote_cli_client — Python client for the pgkit remote protocol.

The Python-side counterpart to `pgkit/remote_client.py` (the browser
client). Same wire protocol, same `hello` handshake, same message
types. Any Python process can import this module and drive a running
playground exactly the way the browser does.

Public API
==========
    RemoteCliClient(url)

Lifecycle
    .connect(timeout=15.0, require_browser=False)
    .close()
    .__enter__ / .__exit__

Snapshots (all returned dicts are defensive copies)
    .values()         field name -> current value
    .schema()         field name -> metadata dict
    .entities()       level name -> {label, selected, parent, items}
    .entity_order()   ordered list of level names
    .presence()       {"browser": N, "remote": M}
    .client_id()      the hub-assigned client id
    .is_connected()

Sends
    .request_state()
    .request_state_and_wait(timeout=5.0)
    .patch(values)
    .patch_and_verify(values, timeout=5.0)
    .command(kind, payload=None, timeout=30.0)
    .raw_send(msg)

Waits
    .wait_value(name, predicate, timeout=10.0)
    .wait_change(fields=None, timeout=10.0)
    .wait_until_settled(name, timeout=60.0)     legacy; see below

Convenience
    .bundle(set=None, actions=None, select=None,
            wait_for_running=False, timeout=60.0, on_progress=None)

Events
    .on(msg_type, callback)
    .off(msg_type, callback)

Async actions
=============
`command()` blocks until the action's observable work settles, because
`pgkit/remote_client.js`'s `pgkitRemoteHandleCommand` `await`s the
action's `run` function. A playground whose `run` is `async function`,
or whose `run` is a sync function that `return`s its async work's
Promise, gets this for free: `command()` returns only after the work
is done, and a subsequent `state_request` sees the side effects. The
same guarantee holds for `select` (via `pgkitHandleSelect`) and
`deselect` (via the injected deselect handler).

Playgrounds whose action `run` is a sync function that calls async
work *without returning the Promise* do not get this guarantee — the
`command_result` fires at the moment `run` returns, before the async
work has started.  The correct fix is on the playground side: make
`run` return the Promise, or wrap the body in `async function`.  The
`wait_until_settled` / `bundle(wait_for_running=True)` mechanism is a
legacy best-effort safety net for such playgrounds; it is not relied
on by well-formed callers and its default is now off.

Reader thread + condition variable
==================================
The reader thread updates the caches under `self._cv` and notifies;
every wait method parks on the condition variable and re-checks its
predicate on each notification. Sends are gated by a separate
`_send_lock` so a slow send never blocks a state update.

Echo suppression: the hub forwards a `patch` to every client except
its sender, so this client never receives its own patches. That is
how the browser-side client behaves too.

Browser appearance: the browser's schema is only sent in response to
`state_request`. When a browser connects to the hub *after* this
client, the browser does not push its own schema — it only answers
`state_request`s. The client therefore watches `presence` and issues
a fresh `state_request` on the 0→1 browser transition, so a CLI that
connected to a browser-less hub learns the schema the moment a
browser appears.

Disconnect handling: when the WebSocket closes or `close()` is called,
every pending `command()` is failed immediately with
`RemoteNotConnected`. A `command()` that was waiting on a
`command_result` does not block out its full timeout; it raises the
underlying disconnect immediately.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional

try:
    from websockets.sync.client import connect as _ws_connect
    from websockets.exceptions import ConnectionClosed as _WSConnectionClosed
    _WS_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    _ws_connect = None
    _WSConnectionClosed = Exception
    _WS_AVAILABLE = False

from . import PROTOCOL_VERSION


# ============================================================================
#  Errors
# ============================================================================

class RemoteCliError(Exception):
    """Base for every client-side error."""


class RemoteTimeout(RemoteCliError):
    """A wait or command timed out."""


class RemoteNotConnected(RemoteCliError):
    """Operation attempted before connect() or after close()."""


class RemoteCommandFailed(RemoteCliError):
    """The playground refused or errored on a command."""

    def __init__(self, kind: str, message: str, result: Optional[dict]):
        self.kind = kind
        self.result = result
        super().__init__(f"{kind}: {message}")


# ============================================================================
#  Helpers
# ============================================================================

_log_send: Optional[Callable[[dict], None]] = None
_log_recv: Optional[Callable[[dict], None]] = None


def set_verbose(enabled: bool = True) -> None:
    """Turn message tracing on/off. Tracing goes to stderr."""
    import sys
    global _log_send, _log_recv
    if enabled:
        _log_send = lambda m: print(f"→ {json.dumps(m)}", file=sys.stderr)
        _log_recv = lambda m: print(f"← {json.dumps(m)}", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        _log_send = None
        _log_recv = None


def parse_value(raw):
    """Turn a shell string into a typed Python value.

    Tries json.loads first: handles numbers, booleans, quoted strings,
    arrays, objects. Falls back to the raw string for anything JSON
    cannot parse (which is most bare words).
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return raw
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return raw


def _predicate_matches(op: str, expected, actual) -> bool:
    if op == "equals":
        return actual == expected
    if op == "not_equals":
        return actual != expected
    if op == "greater_than":
        try: return float(actual) > float(expected)
        except (TypeError, ValueError): return False
    if op == "less_than":
        try: return float(actual) < float(expected)
        except (TypeError, ValueError): return False
    if op == "contains":
        try: return expected in actual
        except TypeError: return False
    if op == "matches":
        import re
        try: return bool(re.search(str(expected), str(actual)))
        except re.error: return False
    raise ValueError(f"unknown predicate: {op}")


# ============================================================================
#  Client
# ============================================================================

class RemoteCliClient:
    """Python client for a pgkit playground's /remote endpoint."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, *, protocol: int = PROTOCOL_VERSION):
        if not _WS_AVAILABLE:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "websockets>=12 is required for RemoteCliClient. "
                "Install with: pip install 'websockets>=12'"
            )
        self._url = url
        self._protocol = protocol

        self._ws = None
        self._reader_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._send_lock = threading.Lock()

        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._cv = threading.Condition(self._lock)

        self._client_id: Optional[str] = None
        self._values: dict = {}
        self._schema: dict = {}
        self._entities: Optional[dict] = None
        self._entity_order: list = []
        self._presence = {"browser": 0, "remote": 0}
        self._connected = False
        self._state_recv_count = 0

        self._seq = 0
        self._pending: dict = {}
        self._listeners: dict = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Lifecycle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def connect(self, *, timeout: float = 15.0,
                require_browser: bool = False) -> None:
        if self._ws is not None:
            raise RemoteCliError("already connected")

        try:
            self._ws = _ws_connect(
                self._url,
                max_size=2 ** 30,
                open_timeout=10.0,
                close_timeout=5.0,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            raise RemoteCliError(
                f"could not connect to {self._url}: {e}"
            ) from e

        with self._cv:
            self._connected = True
            self._cv.notify_all()

        self._reader_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._reader_loop,
            name="remote-cli-reader",
            daemon=True,
        )
        self._reader_thread.start()

        self._send({
            "type": "hello",
            "role": "remote",
            "protocol": self._protocol,
        })

        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout

        with self._cv:
            while self._client_id is None:
                if not self._connected:
                    raise RemoteCliError(
                        "connection closed before hello_ack"
                    )
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise RemoteTimeout("no hello_ack from playground")
                self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.5))

            # Wait for the first presence event so we learn whether a
            # browser is connected.  When `require_browser` is set,
            # wait the full connection timeout — the caller explicitly
            # asked for a browser, so a slow one (ngrok handshake, a
            # tab reload in progress) should not be mistaken for none.
            # Otherwise use a short cap so a browser-less session
            # returns promptly and the caller can start a command that
            # will wait for the browser to appear.
            if require_browser:
                presence_deadline = deadline
            else:
                presence_deadline = min(
                    deadline, time.monotonic() + 3.0
                )

            while (self._presence["browser"] == 0
                   and self._presence["remote"] <= 1):
                remaining = presence_deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    break
                self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.25))

            have_browser = self._presence["browser"] > 0

            if require_browser and not have_browser:
                raise RemoteCliError(
                    f"no browser connected at {self._url} after "
                    f"{timeout:.0f}s. Open the playground in a browser "
                    f"tab first, or increase --timeout."
                )

            if have_browser:
                while True:
                    if (self._state_recv_count > 0
                            and self._entities is not None):
                        break
                    remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                    if remaining <= 0:
                        raise RemoteTimeout(
                            "browser connected but "
                            "state/schema/entities did not arrive"
                        )
                    self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.5))

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        ws = self._ws
        self._ws = None
        if ws is not None:
            try:
                ws.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
        if self._reader_thread is not None:
            self._reader_thread.join(timeout=3.0)
            self._reader_thread = None
        with self._cv:
            self._connected = False
            self._cv.notify_all()
        # Defensive: if the reader thread already failed the pending
        # commands when it noticed the socket close, this is a no-op
        # (each pending event is already set).  If close() raced the
        # reader and the reader hasn't yet reached its own finally,
        # this fails them now so the caller does not wait out a
        # command timeout.
        self._fail_pending(RemoteNotConnected("client closed"))

    def __enter__(self):
        self.connect()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Reader
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _reader_loop(self) -> None:
        ws = self._ws
        if ws is None:
            return
        try:
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                try:
                    raw = ws.recv(timeout=1.0)
                except TimeoutError:
                    continue
                except _WSConnectionClosed:
                    break
                if isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray)):
                    continue
                try:
                    msg = json.loads(raw)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
                self._handle(msg)
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            with self._cv:
                self._connected = False
                self._cv.notify_all()
            self._fail_pending(RemoteNotConnected(
                "connection closed before command result"
            ))

    def _handle(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        t = msg.get("type")
        if _log_recv is not None:
            try:
                _log_recv(msg)
            except Exception:
                pass

        need_state_refresh = False
        callbacks = []

        with self._cv:
            if t == "hello_ack":
                self._client_id = msg.get("clientId")
            elif t == "state":
                self._values = dict(msg.get("values") or {})
                self._state_recv_count += 1
            elif t == "schema":
                self._schema = dict(msg.get("fields") or {})
            elif t == "entities":
                self._entities = dict(msg.get("levels") or {})
                self._entity_order = list(msg.get("order") or [])
            elif t == "presence":
                new_browser = int(msg.get("browser") or 0)
                old_browser = self._presence["browser"]
                self._presence = {
                    "browser": new_browser,
                    "remote": int(msg.get("remote") or 0),
                }
                if new_browser > old_browser and not self._schema:
                    need_state_refresh = True
            elif t == "patch":
                values = msg.get("values") or {}
                if isinstance(values, dict):
                    self._values.update(values)
            elif t == "command_result":
                cmd_id = msg.get("id")
                pending = self._pending.get(cmd_id)
                if pending is not None:
                    pending["result"] = msg
                    pending["event"].set()

            self._cv.notify_all()
            callbacks = list(self._listeners.get(t, []))

        if need_state_refresh:
            try:
                self._send({"type": "state_request"})
            except Exception:
                pass

        for cb in callbacks:
            try:
                cb(msg)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def _fail_pending(self, exc: Exception) -> None:
        """Set `error` on every pending command and wake its waiter.

        Called from the reader loop's shutdown path and from close().
        The `is_set` guard makes it idempotent: the first call wins,
        subsequent calls are no-ops.
        """
        with self._lock:
            snapshot = list(self._pending.values())
        for pending in snapshot:
            if pending["event"].is_set():
                continue
            pending["error"] = exc
            pending["event"].set()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Send
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _send(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        if _log_send is not None:
            try:
                _log_send(msg)
            except Exception:
                pass
        with self._send_lock:
            if self._ws is None:
                raise RemoteNotConnected("not connected")
            self._ws.send(json.dumps(msg))

    def raw_send(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        self._send(msg)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Snapshot accessors
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def values(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._values)

    def schema(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._schema)

    def entities(self) -> Optional[dict]:
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._entities) if self._entities is not None else None

    def entity_order(self) -> list:
        with self._lock:
            return list(self._entity_order)

    def presence(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._presence)

    def client_id(self) -> Optional[str]:
        with self._lock:
            return self._client_id

    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            return self._connected

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Requests
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def request_state(self) -> None:
        self._send({"type": "state_request"})

    def request_state_and_wait(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            baseline = self._state_recv_count
        self._send({"type": "state_request"})
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        with self._cv:
            while self._state_recv_count <= baseline:
                if not self._connected:
                    raise RemoteNotConnected("connection closed")
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise RemoteTimeout("state_request timed out")
                self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.5))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Patch
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def patch(self, values: dict) -> None:
        if not isinstance(values, dict) or not values:
            return
        with self._lock:
            self._seq += 1
            seq = self._seq
            origin = self._client_id
        self._send({
            "type": "patch",
            "origin": origin,
            "seq": seq,
            "values": values,
        })

    def patch_and_verify(self, values: dict,
                         timeout: float = 5.0) -> dict:
        """Send a patch, wait for the resulting state, return applied.

        Returns a dict mapping each requested field to the value the
        browser reports after the patch.  A field whose applied value
        differs from the requested value was clamped, rejected, or
        not applied at all; the caller compares.  If the state does
        not arrive within `timeout`, the returned dict reflects the
        last-known cache (which may be pre-patch); the caller can
        distinguish "applied a different value" from "could not
        verify" only by repeating the read.
        """
        self.patch(values)
        try:
            self.request_state_and_wait(timeout=timeout)
        except RemoteTimeout:
            pass
        with self._lock:
            return {k: self._values.get(k) for k in values}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Command
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def command(self, kind: str, payload: Optional[dict] = None,
                timeout: float = 30.0) -> dict:
        """Send one command and block until it settles.

        Returns the `command_result` message on `ok: true`.  Raises
        `RemoteCommandFailed` on `ok: false`.  Raises
        `RemoteNotConnected` if the connection closes while the
        command is in flight — the disconnect is surfaced immediately
        rather than after `timeout`.  Raises `RemoteTimeout` if the
        command does not settle within `timeout`.

        See "Async actions" in the module docstring for what "settles"
        means: on a correctly-fixed playground, `command()` returns
        after the action's observable work is done, not merely after
        the action was dispatched.
        """
        cmd_id = "cli-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        pending = {
            "event":  threading.Event(),
            "result": None,
            "error":  None,
        }
        with self._lock:
            self._pending[cmd_id] = pending
        try:
            self._send({
                "type": "command",
                "id": cmd_id,
                "kind": kind,
                "payload": payload or {},
            })
            if not pending["event"].wait(timeout=timeout):
                raise RemoteTimeout(
                    f"command {kind!r} did not complete within {timeout}s"
                )
        finally:
            with self._lock:
                self._pending.pop(cmd_id, None)

        if pending["error"] is not None:
            raise pending["error"]
        result = pending["result"]
        if result is None:
            raise RemoteCommandFailed(kind, "no result", None)
        if not result.get("ok"):
            raise RemoteCommandFailed(
                kind,
                result.get("error") or "unknown error",
                result,
            )
        return result

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Waits
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def wait_value(self, name: str,
                   predicate: Callable[[Any], bool],
                   timeout: float = 10.0) -> Any:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        with self._cv:
            while True:
                current = self._values.get(name)
                try:
                    if predicate(current):
                        return current
                except Exception:
                    pass
                if not self._connected:
                    raise RemoteNotConnected("connection closed")
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise RemoteTimeout(
                        f"wait_value({name!r}) timed out after {timeout}s"
                    )
                self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.5))

    def wait_change(self, *, fields=None,
                    timeout: float = 10.0) -> list:
        with self._lock:
            baseline_values = dict(self._values)
            baseline_entities = (
                json.dumps(self._entities, sort_keys=True, default=str)
                if self._entities is not None else None
            )
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        with self._cv:
            while True:
                changed: list = []
                for k, v in self._values.items():
                    if k not in baseline_values or baseline_values[k] != v:
                        changed.append(k)
                for k in baseline_values:
                    if k not in self._values:
                        changed.append(k)
                if (self._entities is not None
                        and baseline_entities is not None):
                    curr = json.dumps(self._entities,
                                      sort_keys=True, default=str)
                    if curr != baseline_entities:
                        changed.append("__entities__")
                if fields is not None:
                    changed = [c for c in changed
                               if c in fields or c == "__entities__"]
                if changed:
                    return changed
                if not self._connected:
                    raise RemoteNotConnected("connection closed")
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise RemoteTimeout(
                        f"wait_change timed out after {timeout}s"
                    )
                self._cv.wait(timeout=min(remaining, 0.5))

    def wait_until_settled(self, name: str,
                           timeout: float = 60.0) -> None:
        """Legacy safety net: wait for a bool field to finish running.

        On a correctly-fixed playground, `command()` already blocks
        until the action's work settles (see "Async actions" in the
        module docstring).  By the time `command()` returns,
        `status.running` is already False, and this method returns
        immediately after one `state_request` round trip.  It is a
        no-op.

        On a playground whose action `run` dispatches async work
        *without* returning the Promise, `command()` returns
        immediately and the action's work may still be in flight.
        This method does one `state_request` and checks the flag: if
        it reads True, it waits for the flag to go False; if it
        reads False, it returns.

        This is best-effort and racy.  A wrapper that has not yet
        flipped the flag when the `state_request` reaches the browser
        is missed.  The correct fix is on the playground side (make
        `run` return its Promise, or wrap its body in `async
        function`), not here.
        """
        try:
            self.request_state_and_wait(timeout=min(2.0, timeout))
        except RemoteTimeout:
            pass
        with self._lock:
            is_running = bool(self._values.get(name))
        if not is_running:
            return
        self.wait_value(name, lambda v: not v, timeout=timeout)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Events
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def on(self, msg_type: str,
           callback: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._listeners.setdefault(msg_type, []).append(callback)

    def off(self, msg_type: str,
            callback: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            lst = self._listeners.get(msg_type, [])
            if callback in lst:
                lst.remove(callback)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #  Bundle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def bundle(self, *, set: Optional[dict] = None,
               actions: Optional[list] = None,
               select: Optional[tuple] = None,
               wait_for_running: bool = False,
               timeout: float = 60.0,
               on_progress: Optional[Callable[[str, dict], None]] = None,
               ) -> dict:
        """Apply a coordinated set of writes and actions.

        `set`       : one patch with N field updates, then one
                      `state_request` to verify.  A field whose
                      applied value differs from the requested value
                      (setter clamped it, rejected it, or the patch
                      never landed) appears in the returned
                      `mismatched` dict.

        `actions`   : sequential commands, one round trip each.
                      `command()` blocks until the action's work
                      settles on a correctly-fixed playground, so
                      sequential actions can rely on the previous
                      having taken effect.  See "Async actions" in
                      the module docstring.

        `select`    : one final `select` command.

        Then a single refresh and return of the fresh values,
        entities, and any set mismatches.

        `wait_for_running` inserts a `wait_until_settled("status.running")`
        after each action.  This is a legacy safety net for
        playgrounds whose `run` dispatches async work without
        returning the Promise; it is best-effort and racy (see
        `wait_until_settled`'s docstring).  Defaults to False.  On a
        correctly-fixed playground, leave it False — you would pay
        one extra round trip per action for no correctness gain.

        Returns:
            {
              "values":     dict of all current field values,
              "entities":   dict of level -> items, or None,
              "mismatched": dict of {field: {"requested": x,
                                             "applied":   y}}
                            for any `set` field whose applied value
                            differs from the requested value.
                            Empty when `set` is None or the patch
                            applied cleanly.
            }
        """
        progress = on_progress or (lambda kind, data: None)
        mismatched: dict = {}

        if set:
            applied = self.patch_and_verify(set, timeout=5.0)
            mismatched = {
                k: {"requested": set[k], "applied": applied.get(k)}
                for k in set
                if applied.get(k) != set[k]
            }
            progress("patch", {
                "values":     dict(set),
                "mismatched": mismatched,
            })

        if actions:
            has_running = "status.running" in self.schema()
            for spec in actions:
                kind = spec.get("kind") or spec.get("action")
                if not kind:
                    raise ValueError(f"action missing 'kind': {spec!r}")
                payload = spec.get("payload") or {}
                result = self.command(kind, payload, timeout=timeout)
                progress("action", {"kind": kind, "result": result})
                if wait_for_running and has_running:
                    try:
                        self.wait_until_settled(
                            "status.running", timeout=timeout
                        )
                    except RemoteTimeout:
                        progress("action", {
                            "kind": kind,
                            "warning": "status.running wait timed out",
                        })

        if select:
            level, name = select
            result = self.command(
                "select", {"level": level, "name": name},
                timeout=timeout,
            )
            progress("select",
                     {"level": level, "name": name, "result": result})

        try:
            self.request_state_and_wait(timeout=5.0)
        except RemoteTimeout:
            pass

        with self._lock:
            return {
                "values":     dict(self._values),
                "entities":   (dict(self._entities)
                               if self._entities is not None else None),
                "mismatched": mismatched,
            }

```python
"""
pgkit.remote_client — the browser's WebSocket client, as an ES module.

The module exports its register/notify functions.  Three things that
used to rely on globals are now injected at boot:

    setRemoteDraw(fn)            — called from pgkitRemoteApplyPatch
    setRemoteSelect(fn)          — dispatches `select` commands
    setRemoteDeselect(fn)        — dispatches `deselect` commands
    setRemoteExtraCommand(fn)    — dispatches playground-specific
                                   command kinds

The module's boot IIFE at the bottom still runs at module load,
opening the WebSocket.  All cross-module injectors are set by the
boot module *after* this one is imported — but before any command
arrives over the socket, since the WebSocket handshake takes at
least one round trip.

Async command handlers
======================
`pgkitRemoteHandleCommand` is `async`, and it `await`s each of the
three injected handler calls (action `run`, `select`, `deselect`,
plus the extra-command fallback).  A project whose `run` function is
an `async function` will have its `command_result` fire only after
the async work settles; a project whose `run` function is
synchronous is unaffected (`await` on a non-Promise resolves in one
microtask tick, which is unobservable on the wire).

This is what makes `remote_cli`'s `command(kind, payload)` — and
`bundle(actions=[...])` — block until the action is *done*, not
merely *dispatched*.  Without the `await`, an action whose `run` is
async would return its `command_result` in the tens of milliseconds
before its HTTP round-trip even started, and a script like

    action action.segmentAll
    select masks mask.0

would race: `select` would fire while `segmentAll` was still
running, and the `command_result` for `select` would report the
mask missing.

Sync actions never opt in and never see a change.  Async actions
opt in just by being `async function` — the `await` in this file
makes their settle-time the reply-time automatically.

Sync-wrapper actions opt in by `return`ing their async work's
Promise.  A sync wrapper that dispatches an async function without
returning the Promise breaks the guarantee for that action; the
correct fix is on the playground side (change the wrapper to
`async function`, or to `return someAsyncCall()`).

Overlapping commands do not queue.  Two `command` messages that
arrive back to back start their async work concurrently, and each
reply goes out when *its* work settles.  The CLI's `command()`
method serializes its own sends (it blocks on each `command_result`
before sending the next), so this overlap does not arise from the
CLI.  A browser-side caller that fires two commands without
waiting — a rapid double-click, a script author writing against
`remote_panel` — may see the replies out of order; both replies
carry their originating `id`, so the recipient matches them
correctly.  Introducing a queue would break `cancel`, which is
exactly the action a user fires *while* another action is running.

LOG MIRRORING FOR REMOTE COMMANDS
=================================
`pgkitRemoteHandleCommand`'s catch does not currently surface its
failure anywhere the playground server can see.  A remote-driven
action that throws browser-side produces a `command_result {ok:
false}`, which the caller (`remote_cli` or `remote_panel`) sees as
its own error; the playground's terminal shows nothing.  The catch
therefore calls `reportPanelError` from `pgkit/panel_core.js`
before building the failure reply, so a browser-side action failure
that came in over `/remote` is visible in the terminal just like a
locally-triggered failure is.

The import is static: `pgkit/panel_core.js` is a leaf module (no
imports of its own), so there is no cycle.  Its console-override
side effects install before this module's boot IIFE opens the
WebSocket, which is exactly the order we want — every subsequent
`console.error` from anywhere in the page already reaches the
server terminal.
"""

REMOTE_CLIENT_JS = r"""
import { reportPanelError } from "./panel_core.js";

/* ==========================================================================
   REMOTE CLIENT — STATE
   ========================================================================== */

const _pgkitRemote = {
  socket:          null,
  clientId:        null,
  connected:       false,
  reconnectDelay:  500,
  seq:             0,
  remoteCount:     0,
  browserCount:    0,
  registry:        {},
  levels:          {},
  protocolVersion: 1,
};

let _pgkitApplyingRemote = false;

let _pgkitNotifyPending   = {};
let _pgkitFlushScheduled  = false;
let _pgkitEntitiesPending = false;
let _pgkitLastEntitiesSig = null;

let _pgkitLastSent = {};

/* Injectable handlers.  Set at boot by the project's boot module. */
let _drawFn            = null;
let _selectFn          = null;
let _deselectFn        = null;
let _extraCommandFn    = null;

export function setRemoteDraw(fn)         { _drawFn = fn; }
export function setRemoteSelect(fn)       { _selectFn = fn; }
export function setRemoteDeselect(fn)     { _deselectFn = fn; }
export function setRemoteExtraCommand(fn) { _extraCommandFn = fn; }

/* ==========================================================================
   VALUE EQUALITY
   ========================================================================== */

function _pgkitValuesEqual(a, b) {
  if (a === b) return true;
  if (a == null || b == null) return a === b;
  if (typeof a !== "object" || typeof b !== "object") return false;
  try { return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b); }
  catch (e) { return false; }
}

/* ==========================================================================
   REGISTRY — FIELDS
   ========================================================================== */

export function pgkitRegisterField(name, opts) {
  if (!name) throw new Error("pgkitRegisterField: name required");
  if (_pgkitRemote.registry[name]) {
    throw new Error("pgkitRegisterField: duplicate " + name);
  }
  _pgkitRemote.registry[name] = {
    isAction: false,
    get: opts.get,
    set: opts.set,
    meta: opts.meta || {},
  };
}

/* ==========================================================================
   REGISTRY — ACTIONS
   ========================================================================== */

export function pgkitRegisterAction(name, opts) {
  if (!name) throw new Error("pgkitRegisterAction: name required");
  if (_pgkitRemote.registry[name]) {
    throw new Error("pgkitRegisterAction: duplicate " + name);
  }

  const scope = opts.scope || "global";
  const level = (scope === "global") ? null : (opts.level || null);
  if (scope !== "global" && !level) {
    throw new Error("pgkitRegisterAction: " + name
                    + " needs a level for scope '" + scope + "'");
  }
  if (scope === "row" && typeof opts.appliesTo !== "function") {
    throw new Error("pgkitRegisterAction: " + name
                    + " (row scope) needs appliesTo(item)");
  }

  const meta = Object.assign(
    { kind: "action", label: opts.label || name },
    opts.meta || {}
  );
  meta.scope = scope;
  meta.level = level;

  _pgkitRemote.registry[name] = {
    isAction:  true,
    run:       opts.run,
    appliesTo: opts.appliesTo || null,
    meta:      meta,
  };
}

/* ==========================================================================
   REGISTRY — LEVELS
   ========================================================================== */

export function pgkitRegisterLevel(name, opts) {
  if (!name) throw new Error("pgkitRegisterLevel: name required");
  if (_pgkitRemote.levels[name]) {
    throw new Error("pgkitRegisterLevel: duplicate " + name);
  }
  _pgkitRemote.levels[name] = {
    label:    opts.label || name,
    items:    opts.items    || (() => []),
    selected: opts.selected || (() => null),
    parent:   opts.parent   || (() => null),
  };
}

/* ==========================================================================
   DUMPS
   ========================================================================== */

function pgkitDumpState() {
  const out = {};
  for (const name in _pgkitRemote.registry) {
    const r = _pgkitRemote.registry[name];
    if (r.isAction) continue;
    try { out[name] = r.get(); }
    catch (e) {}
  }
  return out;
}

function pgkitDumpSchema() {
  const out = {};
  for (const name in _pgkitRemote.registry) {
    out[name] = _pgkitRemote.registry[name].meta || {};
  }
  return out;
}

function pgkitDumpEntities() {
  const levels = {};
  const order  = [];

  for (const levelName in _pgkitRemote.levels) {
    const lvl = _pgkitRemote.levels[levelName];

    let rawItems = [];
    try { rawItems = lvl.items() || []; } catch (e) { rawItems = []; }

    let selected = null;
    try { selected = lvl.selected(); } catch (e) { selected = null; }

    let parent = null;
    try { parent = lvl.parent(); } catch (e) { parent = null; }

    const items = rawItems.map(it => {
      const applies = {};
      for (const aname in _pgkitRemote.registry) {
        const a = _pgkitRemote.registry[aname];
        if (!a.isAction) continue;
        if (a.meta.level !== levelName) continue;
        if (a.meta.scope !== "row") continue;
        if (!a.appliesTo) continue;
        try { applies[aname] = !!a.appliesTo(it); }
        catch (e) { applies[aname] = false; }
      }
      return {
        name:    it.name,
        label:   it.label,
        extra:   it.extra || null,
        applies: applies,
      };
    });

    levels[levelName] = {
      label:    lvl.label,
      selected: selected,
      parent:   parent,
      items:    items,
    };
    order.push(levelName);
  }

  return { levels, order };
}

/* ==========================================================================
   NOTIFICATION
   ========================================================================== */

export function pgkitNotifyLocal(name) {
  if (_pgkitApplyingRemote) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.connected) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.clientId) return;
  const f = _pgkitRemote.registry[name];
  if (!f || f.isAction) return;
  let v;
  try { v = f.get(); } catch (e) { return; }
  _pgkitNotifyPending[name] = v;
  _pgkitScheduleFlush();
}

export function pgkitNotifyAll() {
  if (_pgkitApplyingRemote) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.connected) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.clientId) return;
  for (const name in _pgkitRemote.registry) {
    const r = _pgkitRemote.registry[name];
    if (r.isAction) continue;
    let v;
    try { v = r.get(); } catch (e) { continue; }
    _pgkitNotifyPending[name] = v;
  }
  _pgkitEntitiesPending = true;
  _pgkitScheduleFlush();
}

export function pgkitNotifyEntities() {
  if (_pgkitApplyingRemote) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.connected) return;
  if (!_pgkitRemote.clientId) return;
  _pgkitEntitiesPending = true;
  _pgkitScheduleFlush();
}

function _pgkitScheduleFlush() {
  if (_pgkitFlushScheduled) return;
  _pgkitFlushScheduled = true;
  if (typeof requestAnimationFrame === "function") {
    requestAnimationFrame(_pgkitFlush);
  } else {
    setTimeout(_pgkitFlush, 16);
  }
}

function _pgkitFlush() {
  _pgkitFlushScheduled = false;

  const pending = _pgkitNotifyPending;
  _pgkitNotifyPending = {};

  const toSend = {};
  let any = false;
  for (const k in pending) {
    if (!(k in _pgkitLastSent)
        || !_pgkitValuesEqual(_pgkitLastSent[k], pending[k])) {
      toSend[k] = pending[k];
      any = true;
    }
  }

  if (any) {
    for (const k in toSend) _pgkitLastSent[k] = toSend[k];
    _pgkitRemote.seq++;
    _pgkitRemoteSend({
      type:   "patch",
      origin: _pgkitRemote.clientId,
      seq:    _pgkitRemote.seq,
      values: toSend,
    });
  }

  if (_pgkitEntitiesPending) {
    _pgkitEntitiesPending = false;
    const dump = pgkitDumpEntities();
    const sig  = JSON.stringify(dump);
    if (sig !== _pgkitLastEntitiesSig) {
      _pgkitLastEntitiesSig = sig;
      _pgkitRemoteSend({
        type:   "entities",
        levels: dump.levels,
        order:  dump.order,
      });
    }
  }
}

/* ==========================================================================
   WIRE
   ========================================================================== */

function _pgkitRemoteSend(msg) {
  const s = _pgkitRemote.socket;
  if (!s || s.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return;
  s.send(JSON.stringify(msg));
}

function pgkitRemoteConnect() {
  let url;
  try {
    const u = new URL("remote", document.baseURI);
    u.protocol = (u.protocol === "https:") ? "wss:" : "ws:";
    url = u.toString();
  } catch (e) {
    url = (location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:")
        + "//" + location.host + "/remote";
  }

  let socket;
  try { socket = new WebSocket(url); }
  catch (e) { return; }
  _pgkitRemote.socket = socket;

  socket.addEventListener("open", () => {
    _pgkitRemote.connected = true;
    _pgkitRemote.reconnectDelay = 500;
    _pgkitRemoteSend({
      type:     "hello",
      role:     "browser",
      protocol: _pgkitRemote.protocolVersion,
    });
  });

  socket.addEventListener("message", (ev) => {
    let msg;
    try { msg = JSON.parse(ev.data); } catch (e) { return; }
    pgkitRemoteHandle(msg);
  });

  socket.addEventListener("close", () => {
    _pgkitRemote.connected = false;
    _pgkitRemote.clientId  = null;
    _pgkitRemote.remoteCount  = 0;
    _pgkitRemote.browserCount = 0;
    _pgkitNotifyPending   = {};
    _pgkitFlushScheduled  = false;
    _pgkitEntitiesPending = false;
    _pgkitLastEntitiesSig = null;
    _pgkitLastSent        = {};
    _pgkitUpdatePanelVisibility();
    setTimeout(pgkitRemoteConnect, _pgkitRemote.reconnectDelay);
    _pgkitRemote.reconnectDelay = Math.min(
      _pgkitRemote.reconnectDelay * 2, 5000);
  });

  socket.addEventListener("error", () => {});
}

function pgkitRemoteHandle(msg) {
  switch (msg.type) {
    case "hello_ack":
      _pgkitRemote.clientId = msg.clientId;
      break;

    case "state_request": {
      const values = pgkitDumpState();
      _pgkitRemoteSend({
        type:   "state",
        seq:    _pgkitRemote.seq,
        values: values,
      });
      _pgkitRemoteSend({
        type:   "schema",
        fields: pgkitDumpSchema(),
      });
      const dump = pgkitDumpEntities();
      _pgkitLastEntitiesSig = JSON.stringify(dump);
      _pgkitRemoteSend({
        type:   "entities",
        levels: dump.levels,
        order:  dump.order,
      });
      for (const name in values) _pgkitLastSent[name] = values[name];
      break;
    }

    case "patch":
      if (msg.origin === _pgkitRemote.clientId) break;
      pgkitRemoteApplyPatch(msg.values || {});
      break;

    case "command":
      /* Async because pgkitRemoteHandleCommand is async.  The
       * promise resolves when the command's reply has been sent;
       * we do not wait on it here, and we do not need to.  The
       * .catch is defensive: the function already wraps its whole
       * body in try/catch, but _pgkitRemoteSend lives outside that
       * try, so a WebSocket close between settle and send would
       * otherwise surface as an unhandled rejection. */
      pgkitRemoteHandleCommand(msg).catch((e) => {
        console.error("command handler threw:", e);
      });
      break;

    case "presence":
      _pgkitRemote.remoteCount  = msg.remote  || 0;
      _pgkitRemote.browserCount = msg.browser || 0;
      _pgkitUpdatePanelVisibility();
      break;
  }
}

function pgkitRemoteApplyPatch(values) {
  _pgkitApplyingRemote = true;
  try {
    for (const name in values) {
      const f = _pgkitRemote.registry[name];
      if (!f || f.isAction) continue;

      _pgkitLastSent[name] = values[name];

      let cur;
      try { cur = f.get(); } catch (e) { cur = undefined; }
      if (_pgkitValuesEqual(cur, values[name])) continue;

      try { f.set(values[name]); } catch (e) {}
    }
  } finally {
    _pgkitApplyingRemote = false;
  }
  if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
}

/* ==========================================================================
   COMMANDS
   ==========================================================================
   Async: `await` on each injected handler means a `command_result`
   fires when the handler's work has *settled*, not when it was
   dispatched.  A synchronous handler resolves in one microtask tick
   (unobservable on the wire); an async handler resolves when its
   promise does.  This is what makes `remote_cli`'s `command()`
   block until an action is done, without any per-playground
   `status.running` field.

   The `reset_view` global lookup that used to live here was removed:
   `resetView` is not a global in any ES-module playground, so the
   guard was never true.  A playground that wants a reset action
   registers one via `pgkitRegisterAction`, and it is dispatched
   through the registry like any other action.

   A failure inside the handler — thrown synchronously by a sync
   action, or a rejected promise from an async one — is mirrored to
   the server terminal via `reportPanelError` before the failure
   reply is built.  Without this mirror, remote-driven action
   failures (remote_cli, remote_panel, any other WS client) are
   visible only to the client that fired them; the server's stdout
   stays silent. */

async function pgkitRemoteHandleCommand(msg) {
  let ok = true;
  let error = null;
  let result;

  try {
    const kind  = msg.kind;
    const entry = _pgkitRemote.registry[kind];

    if (entry && entry.isAction) {
      try { result = await entry.run(msg.payload || {}); }
      catch (e) {
        ok = false;
        error = String(e);
        reportPanelError(
          "remote command " + kind + ": " + error,
          "js-remote-error",
        );
      }
    } else if (kind === "select") {
      const payload = msg.payload || {};
      if (_selectFn) {
        const selOk = await _selectFn(payload.level, payload.name);
        if (!selOk) {
          ok = false;
          error = "select failed";
          reportPanelError(
            "remote command select " + payload.level + "/" + payload.name
              + ": handler returned false",
            "js-remote-error",
          );
        } else {
          pgkitNotifyAll();
        }
      } else {
        ok = false;
        error = "no select handler";
        reportPanelError(
          "remote command select: no handler installed",
          "js-remote-error",
        );
      }
    } else if (kind === "deselect") {
      if (_deselectFn) await _deselectFn();
      if (_drawFn) _drawFn();
      pgkitNotifyAll();
    } else if (_extraCommandFn) {
      const handled = await _extraCommandFn(kind, msg.payload || {});
      if (!handled) {
        ok = false;
        error = "unknown command";
        reportPanelError(
          "remote command " + kind + ": unknown kind",
          "js-remote-error",
        );
      }
    } else {
      ok = false;
      error = "unknown command";
      reportPanelError(
        "remote command " + kind + ": unknown kind",
        "js-remote-error",
      );
    }
  } catch (e) {
    ok = false;
    error = String(e);
    reportPanelError(
      "remote command handler threw: " + error,
      "js-remote-error",
    );
  }

  const reply = {
    type:  "command_result",
    id:    msg.id,
    ok:    ok,
    error: error,
  };
  if (result !== undefined) reply.result = result;
  _pgkitRemoteSend(reply);
}

/* ==========================================================================
   PRESENCE → PANEL VISIBILITY
   ========================================================================== */

function _pgkitUpdatePanelVisibility() {
  const ui         = document.getElementById("ui");
  const banner     = document.getElementById("remoteBanner");
  const restoreBtn = document.getElementById("restoreBtn");
  if (!ui) return;

  const hide = _pgkitRemote.connected && _pgkitRemote.remoteCount > 0;

  if (hide) {
    ui.classList.add("collapsed");
    if (banner) banner.classList.add("visible");
    if (restoreBtn) restoreBtn.classList.remove("visible");
  } else {
    ui.classList.remove("collapsed");
    if (banner) banner.classList.remove("visible");
  }
}

/* ==========================================================================
   BOOT — opens the WebSocket at module load
   ========================================================================== */

(function pgkitRemoteBoot() {
  function start() { setTimeout(pgkitRemoteConnect, 100); }
  if (document.readyState === "loading") {
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", start);
  } else {
    start();
  }
})();

"""
pgkit.remote_hub — server-side WebSocket hub.

A `Hub` owns a list of connected clients and broadcasts messages
among them.  Its only protocol-level knowledge is the `hello`
handshake: it assigns each client an id, remembers its role
(`browser` or `remote`), and re-broadcasts presence.

Everything else is forwarded verbatim.  The hub does not maintain
playground state; the browser does.

FORWARDED MESSAGE TYPES
=======================
The hub relays any of:

    patch, command, command_result, state, state_request, schema,
    entities

`schema` carries the field and action metadata the browser
advertises alongside its state dump; `entities` carries the
per-level item lists, the current selection per level, and the
per-item `applies` map for row-scope actions.  Both come from the
browser's `state_request` handler.  A remote client that does not
understand either receives them and ignores them, exactly as it
would ignore any other unrecognized `type`.

A missing entry in this list means the message is silently dropped
by the hub — it never reaches any client.  This is the single most
likely failure mode when a new message type is introduced; if a
level or a field shows up on the browser but not on the remote
panel, this tuple is the first place to check.

DUPLICATE HELLO
===============
A client may only send `hello` once per connection.  A second
`hello` on the same socket is treated as a protocol violation and
the connection is closed by the server loop (via an exception that
propagates out of `handle_message`).  This prevents a client from
silently switching its role mid-session, which would leave the
hub's role counts inconsistent and confuse presence-driven panel
visibility.
"""

import json
import threading

from . import ws as _ws
from . import PROTOCOL_VERSION


_FORWARDED_TYPES = (
    "patch",
    "command",
    "command_result",
    "state",
    "state_request",
    "schema",
    "entities",
)


class Client:
    """One connected WebSocket peer."""

    def __init__(self, sock, peer=None):
        self.sock      = sock
        self.peer      = peer
        self.id        = "c-%x" % id(self)
        self.role      = None
        self.send_lock = threading.Lock()

    def send(self, msg):
        data = json.dumps(msg)
        with self.send_lock:
            _ws.write_text_frame(self.sock, data)

    def recv(self):
        opcode, payload = _ws.read_frame(self.sock)
        if opcode is None:
            return None
        if opcode == 0x08:
            return None
        if opcode == 0x01:
            try:
                return payload.decode("utf-8")
            except Exception:
                return ""
        return ""


class Hub:
    def __init__(self):
        self.clients = []
        self.lock    = threading.Lock()

    def add(self, client):
        with self.lock:
            self.clients.append(client)
        self._broadcast_presence()

    def remove(self, client):
        with self.lock:
            if client in self.clients:
                self.clients.remove(client)
        self._broadcast_presence()

    def broadcast(self, msg, exclude=None):
        dead = []
        with self.lock:
            targets = [c for c in self.clients if c is not exclude]
        for c in targets:
            try:
                c.send(msg)
            except Exception:
                dead.append(c)
        for c in dead:
            self.remove(c)

    def _broadcast_presence(self):
        with self.lock:
            browser = sum(1 for c in self.clients if c.role == "browser")
            remote  = sum(1 for c in self.clients if c.role == "remote")
        self.broadcast({
            "type":    "presence",
            "browser": browser,
            "remote":  remote,
        })


def handle_message(hub, client, msg):
    """Interpret one JSON message from `client` and dispatch.

    Raises on protocol violations (currently: a duplicate `hello` on
    the same connection).  The server loop catches exceptions from
    this function and closes the connection.
    """
    t = msg.get("type")

    if t == "hello":
        if client.role is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"duplicate hello on connection {client.id} "
                f"(role was already {client.role!r})"
            )
        client.role = msg.get("role") or "remote"
        client.send({
            "type":     "hello_ack",
            "clientId": client.id,
            "protocol": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        })
        if client.role == "browser":
            client.send({"type": "state_request"})
        else:
            hub.broadcast({"type": "state_request"}, exclude=client)
        hub._broadcast_presence()
        return

    if t in _FORWARDED_TYPES:
        hub.broadcast(msg, exclude=client)
        return
